### The ShotCoordinator Durable Object (`src/objects/ShotCoordinator.ts`)

```typescript
import { DurableObject } from 'cloudflare:workers';
import type { 
  ShotActorState, 
  DispatchShotPayload, 
  RunPodJobResult 
} from '../types/orchestrator';

const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2;
const WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_MS = 180_000; // 3 minutes TTL

export class ShotCoordinator extends DurableObject<Env> {
  private state!: ShotActorState;
  private isLoaded = false;

  private async initialize(shotId: string): Promise<void> {
    if (this.isLoaded) return;

    const stored = await this.ctx.storage.get<ShotActorState>('state');
    if (stored) {
      this.state = stored;
    } else {
      this.state = {
        shot_id: shotId,
        scene_id: '',
        status: 'IDLE',
        attempt_count: 0,
        active_job_id: null,
        latest_asset_url: null,
        processed_keys: [],
        created_at: Date.now(),
        updated_at: Date.now()
      };
      await this.ctx.storage.put('state', this.state);
    }
    this.isLoaded = true;
  }

  private async persist(): Promise<void> {
    this.state.updated_at = Date.now();
    await this.ctx.storage.put('state', this.state);
  }

  /**
   * Dispatches render pass to RunPod Serverless with atomic idempotency validation
   * and circuit breaker enforcement.
   */
  async dispatch(payload: DispatchShotPayload) {
    await this.initialize(payload.shot_id);
    this.state.scene_id = payload.scene_id;

    // 1. Idempotency Guard
    if (this.state.processed_keys.includes(payload.idempotency_key)) {
      return {
        success: false,
        code: 'IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY',
        message: `Key '${payload.idempotency_key}' was already executed.`,
        current_status: this.state.status,
        job_id: this.state.active_job_id
      };
    }

    // 2. Strict Circuit Breaker Guard
    if (this.state.attempt_count >= MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
      this.state.status = 'CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TRIPPED';
      await this.persist();
      await this.ctx.storage.deleteAlarm();

      return {
        success: false,
        code: 'CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TRIPPED',
        message: `Execution blocked. Maximum attempts (${MAX_ATTEMPTS}) exceeded for ${payload.shot_id}. Manual reset required.`,
        current_status: this.state.status
      };
    }

    // 3. Atomically Transition State Before External I/O
    this.state.attempt_count += 1;
    this.state.status = 'DISPATCHED';
    this.state.processed_keys.push(payload.idempotency_key);
    await this.persist();

    // 4. Arm Watchdog Alarm for Spot Eviction / Network Loss
    await this.ctx.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_MS);

    // 5. Build Outbound RunPod Payload
    const endpointId = payload.is_inpaint 
      ? this.env.RUNPOD_INPAINT_ENDPOINT_ID 
      : this.env.RUNPOD_STANDARD_ENDPOINT_ID;

    const runpodBody = {
      input: {
        shot_id: payload.shot_id,
        scene_id: payload.scene_id,
        target_frames: payload.target_frames,
        visual_prompt: payload.visual_prompt,
        character_lora: payload.character_lora,
        is_inpaint: payload.is_inpaint,
        inpaint_params: payload.inpaint_params
      },
      webhook: `${this.env.WEBHOOK_CALLBACK_URL}?shot_id=${payload.shot_id}`
    };

    try {
      const response = await fetch(`https://api.runpod.ai/v2/${endpointId}/run`, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: {
          'Content-Type': 'application/json',
          'Authorization': `Bearer ${this.env.RUNPOD_API_KEY}`
        },
        body: JSON.stringify(runpodBody)
      });

      if (!response.ok) {
        throw new Error(`RunPod HTTP Gateway Fault: ${response.status} ${response.statusText}`);
      }

      const runpodRes = (await response.json()) as { id: string };
      this.state.active_job_id = runpodRes.id;
      this.state.status = 'PROCESSING';
      await this.persist();

      // Mirror state transition to D1 ledger
      await this.env.CANON_DB.prepare(`
        INSERT INTO render_jobs (id, shot_id, attempt_index, idempotency_key)
        VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
      `).bind(runpodRes.id, payload.shot_id, this.state.attempt_count, payload.idempotency_key).run();

      return {
        success: true,
        code: 'DISPATCH_ACKNOWLEDGED',
        job_id: runpodRes.id,
        attempt: this.state.attempt_count,
        status: this.state.status
      };
    } catch (err: any) {
      this.state.status = 'FAILED';
      await this.persist();
      await this.ctx.storage.deleteAlarm();

      return {
        success: false,
        code: 'DISPATCH_COMMUNICATION_ERROR',
        error: err.message
      };
    }
  }

  /**
   * Processes serialized webhooks delivered via the Queue Consumer.
   */
  async handleWebhook(result: RunPodJobResult) {
    await this.initialize(this.state.shot_id);

    // Mismatched or stale job check
    if (this.state.active_job_id && this.state.active_job_id !== result.id) {
      return {
        ignored: true,
        reason: 'MISMATCHED_JOB_ID',
        active_id: this.state.active_job_id,
        incoming_id: result.id
      };
    }

    // Disarm Watchdog Alarm immediately
    await this.ctx.storage.deleteAlarm();

    if (result.status === 'COMPLETED') {
      const outputUrl = result.output?.asset_url;
      if (!outputUrl) {
        this.state.status = 'FAILED';
        await this.persist();
        return { success: false, code: 'CORRUPTED_PAYLOAD_MISSING_ASSET' };
      }

      this.state.status = 'COMPLETED';
      this.state.latest_asset_url = outputUrl;
      this.state.active_job_id = null;
      await this.persist();

      // Update D1 State
      await this.env.CANON_DB.batch([
        this.env.CANON_DB.prepare(`
          UPDATE shots 
          SET status = 'COMPLETED', updated_at = unixepoch() 
          WHERE id = ?
        `).bind(this.state.shot_id),
        this.env.CANON_DB.prepare(`
          UPDATE render_jobs 
          SET output_asset_url = ?, render_duration_seconds = ? 
          WHERE id = ?
        `).bind(outputUrl, result.output?.render_duration_seconds ?? 0, result.id)
      ]);

      return { success: true, status: 'COMPLETED', asset_url: outputUrl };
    }

    if (result.status === 'FAILED' || result.status === 'CANCELLED') {
      this.state.active_job_id = null;

      if (this.state.attempt_count >= MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
        this.state.status = 'CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TRIPPED';
      } else {
        this.state.status = 'FAILED';
      }
      await this.persist();

      // Log failure in D1
      await this.env.CANON_DB.batch([
        this.env.CANON_DB.prepare(`
          UPDATE shots 
          SET status = ?, updated_at = unixepoch() 
          WHERE id = ?
        `).bind(this.state.status, this.state.shot_id),
        this.env.CANON_DB.prepare(`
          UPDATE render_jobs 
          SET error_log = ? 
          WHERE id = ?
        `).bind(result.error ?? 'Unknown Worker Failure', result.id)
      ]);

      return {
        success: true,
        status: this.state.status,
        attempts_used: this.state.attempt_count
      };
    }

    return { ignored: true, reason: 'UNHANDLED_WEBHOOK_STATUS' };
  }

  /**
   * Watchdog Alarm: Fires when RunPod fails to report completion within 180 seconds.
   * Mitigates silent spot evictions and dead data center instances.
   */
  async alarm(): Promise<void> {
    await this.initialize(this.state.shot_id);

    if (this.state.status === 'PROCESSING' || this.state.status === 'DISPATCHED') {
      this.state.active_job_id = null;
      
      if (this.state.attempt_count >= MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
        this.state.status = 'CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TRIPPED';
      } else {
        this.state.status = 'TIMED_OUT';
      }
      
      await this.persist();

      await this.env.CANON_DB.prepare(`
        UPDATE shots 
        SET status = ?, updated_at = unixepoch() 
        WHERE id = ?
      `).bind(this.state.status, this.state.shot_id).run();

      console.error(`[Watchdog Alarm] Shot ${this.state.shot_id} timed out after ${WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_MS}ms. Attempt: ${this.state.attempt_count}`);
    }
  }

  async getStatus(): Promise<ShotActorState> {
    await this.initialize(this.state?.shot_id || 'UNKNOWN');
    return this.state;
  }

  async manualSupervisorReset(reason: string): Promise<ShotActorState> {
    await this.initialize(this.state.shot_id);
    this.state.attempt_count = 0;
    this.state.status = 'IDLE';
    this.state.active_job_id = null;
    await this.persist();
    await this.ctx.storage.deleteAlarm();

    await this.env.CANON_DB.prepare(`
      UPDATE shots 
      SET status = 'PENDING', updated_at = unixepoch() 
      WHERE id = ?
    `).bind(this.state.shot_id).run();

    return this.state;
  }
}

```

### Ingress & Queue Consumer Implementation (`src/index.ts`)

```typescript
import { Hono } from 'hono';
import { ShotCoordinator } from './objects/ShotCoordinator';
import { flagDirtyDependencies } from './services/canonGraph';
import type { 
  DispatchShotPayload, 
  RunPodJobResult, 
  WebhookQueueMessage 
} from './types/orchestrator';

export { ShotCoordinator };

export interface Env {
  CANON_DB: D1Database;
  SHOT_COORDINATOR: DurableObjectNamespace<ShotCoordinator>;
  WEBHOOK_QUEUE: Queue<WebhookQueueMessage>;
  RUNPOD_API_KEY: string;
  RUNPOD_STANDARD_ENDPOINT_ID: string;
  RUNPOD_INPAINT_ENDPOINT_ID: string;
  WEBHOOK_CALLBACK_URL: string;
}

const app = new Hono<{ Bindings: Env }>();

// 1. Trigger Dependency Invalidation Audit
app.post('/api/canon/audit', async (c) => {
  const dirty = await flagDirtyDependencies(c.env.CANON_DB);
  return c.json({
    status: 'AUDIT_COMPLETE',
    dirty_count: dirty.length,
    dirty_dependencies: dirty
  });
});

// 2. Dispatch Shot Render
app.post('/api/shots/dispatch', async (c) => {
  const payload = await c.req.json<DispatchShotPayload>();

  if (!payload.shot_id || !payload.idempotency_key) {
    return c.json({ error: 'Missing shot_id or idempotency_key' }, 400);
  }

  // Pre-flight check: Verify scene is not dirty in D1
  const dependencyCheck = await c.env.CANON_DB.prepare(`
    SELECT COUNT(*) as dirty_count 
    FROM scene_fact_dependencies 
    WHERE scene_id = ? AND is_dirty = 1
  `).bind(payload.scene_id).first<{ dirty_count: number }>();

  if (dependencyCheck && dependencyCheck.dirty_count > 0) {
    return c.json({
      error: 'SCENE_DIRTY_DEPENDENCIES',
      message: `Cannot dispatch shot ${payload.shot_id}. Scene ${payload.scene_id} contains stale canonical facts.`
    }, 409);
  }

  // Bind to the designated Durable Object Actor
  const doId = c.env.SHOT_COORDINATOR.idFromName(payload.shot_id);
  const actor = c.env.SHOT_COORDINATOR.get(doId);

  const result = await actor.dispatch(payload);

  if (!result.success && result.code === 'CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TRIPPED') {
    return c.json(result, 429);
  }
  if (!result.success && result.code === 'IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY') {
    return c.json(result, 409);
  }

  return c.json(result, result.success ? 200 : 502);
});

// 3. Ultra-Fast Webhook Receiver (Ingress Shock Absorber)
app.post('/api/webhooks/runpod', async (c) => {
  const shotId = c.req.query('shot_id');
  if (!shotId) {
    return c.json({ error: 'Missing shot_id query parameter' }, 400);
  }

  const jobResult = await c.req.json<RunPodJobResult>();

  // Hand off immediately to Cloudflare Queue; terminate HTTP context in under 5ms
  await c.env.WEBHOOK_QUEUE.send({
    received_at: Date.now(),
    shot_id: shotId,
    job_data: jobResult
  });

  return c.json({ received: true }, 202);
});

// 4. Manual Human Supervisor Reset
app.post('/api/shots/:shot_id/reset', async (c) => {
  const shotId = c.req.param('shot_id');
  const { reason } = await c.req.json<{ reason: string }>();

  const doId = c.env.SHOT_COORDINATOR.idFromName(shotId);
  const actor = c.env.SHOT_COORDINATOR.get(doId);

  const state = await actor.manualSupervisorReset(reason || 'Supervisor reset');
  return c.json(state, 200);
});

// 5. Export Default Fetch Handler
export default {
  fetch: app.fetch,

  // 6. Asynchronous Cloudflare Queue Consumer
  async queue(batch: MessageBatch<WebhookQueueMessage>, env: Env): Promise<void> {
    for (const msg of batch.messages) {
      const { shot_id, job_data } = msg.body;

      try {
        const doId = env.SHOT_COORDINATOR.idFromName(shot_id);
        const actor = env.SHOT_COORDINATOR.get(doId);

        const outcome = await actor.handleWebhook(job_data);
        
        // Acknowledge processing
        msg.ack();
      } catch (err) {
        console.error(`[Queue Consumer] Failure processing message for shot ${shot_id}:`, err);
        // Exponential backoff / retry triggered automatically up to max_retries
        msg.retry();
      }
    }
  }
};

```

---

## 5. Failure Modes, Network Splits, and Recovery Matrix

By distributing the control plane across D1, Durable Objects, and Queues, failure surfaces become strictly compartmentalized:

| Failure Scenario | Manifestation | Automated System Mitigation | Final State |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **RunPod Community Spot Eviction** | Instance destroyed without sending a webhook. | The Durable Object's 180s storage alarm fires (`ctx.storage.setAlarm()`), transitioning status from `PROCESSING` to `TIMED_OUT`. | Attempt counter increments. If `< 2`, system re-dispatches to reliable tier. If `== 2`, status shifts to `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TRIPPED`. |
| **Rapid Double Click / Agent Replay** | Agent hits `/api/shots/dispatch` multiple times due to a dropped socket. | Durable Object checks `processed_keys` inside single-threaded memory before network I/O. | Second request rejected immediately with `HTTP 409 (IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY)`. Zero duplicate GPU spend. |
| **Out-of-Order Webhook Delivery** | A delayed completion webhook from Job A arrives after Job B has already been dispatched. | Actor checks `if (state.active_job_id !== result.id)`. | Stale webhook dropped with `MISMATCHED_JOB_ID`. State remains clean. |
| **Canonical Fact Drift Mid-Production** | Human updates a character fact while an episode animatic is queued. | `flagDirtyDependencies` detects `pinned_version < max_version`, sets `is_dirty = 1`, and downgrades scene to `DRAFT`. | Dispatch endpoint returns `HTTP 409 (SCENE_DIRTY_DEPENDENCIES)`, halting execution before cloud GPUs spin up. |
| **Webhook Ingress Flood** | 60 workers complete simultaneously, flooding the edge gateway. | Cloudflare Queue absorbs all incoming webhooks within 5ms HTTP responses, buffering up to thousands of messages. | Consumer processes messages in batches of 10, passing them sequentially to the respective Durable Objects without drops. |

---

## 6. End-to-End State Machine Audit Trail

When a shot executes through this architecture, state progresses through a strictly verifiable lifecycle:

```
[ T+0.00s ] Astro UI initiates Dispatch.
            POST /api/shots/dispatch
            Headers: { Idempotency-Key: "uuid-v4-01" }

[ T+0.02s ] Hono Router checks D1: scene_fact_dependencies.is_dirty == 0. (PASS)
[ T+0.04s ] ShotCoordinator instantiated (ep01_sc03_sh01).
[ T+0.05s ] Actor verifies attempt_count (0 < 2). Increments to 1.
[ T+0.06s ] Actor sets 180s Alarm. Status -> DISPATCHED.
[ T+0.42s ] RunPod API returns { id: "job_runpod_98765" }. Status -> PROCESSING.
[ T+0.45s ] Actor persists state to Transactional Storage.
[ T+0.48s ] D1 logs render_job row (Attempt 1, PENDING).

... (72.00 seconds of GPU tensor execution on RunPod worker) ...

[ T+72.48s ] RunPod worker uploads MP4 to Cloudflare R2.
[ T+72.50s ] RunPod fires webhook -> POST /api/webhooks/runpod?shot_id=ep01_sc03_sh01.
[ T+72.51s ] Ingress Worker puts payload on runpod-webhook-queue, returns HTTP 202.
[ T+72.55s ] Queue Consumer pulls message batch, executes Workers RPC -> actor.handleWebhook().
[ T+72.56s ] Actor verifies job ID ("job_runpod_98765" == active_job_id).
[ T+72.57s ] Actor deletes 180s Alarm. Status -> COMPLETED.
[ T+72.58s ] Actor records asset URL: "https://assets.series.internal/outputs/raw_video/ep01_sc03_sh01.mp4".
[ T+72.62s ] D1 batch update: shots.status = 'COMPLETED', render_jobs.output_asset_url populated.
[ T+72.65s ] Message acknowledged (msg.ack()). Pipeline ready for Remotion assembly.

```

This ensures the entire edge-to-GPU execution cycle is fully deterministic, protected against network failures, and bounded by hard financial constraints.The Agentic Parameter Injector and Production Frontend represent the human-in-the-loop control plane of the generative pipeline. This layer translates high-level dramatic premises into machine-readable parameter vectors, renders interactive exposure sheets and animatic previews, and provides the supervisory controls needed to govern cloud GPU execution.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ASTRO FRONTEND (HYBRID SSR + REACT ISLANDS)                                                            │
│                                                                                                        │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────────┐  │
│  │ Narrative Premise & Canon Input │   │ Embedded Remotion Player Island  │   │ Dispatch & Circuit  │  │
│  │ (Writer Workspace)              │   │ (Animatic / Radio Play Review)   │   │ Breaker Console     │  │
│  └────────────────┬────────────────┘   └────────────────▲─────────────────┘   └──────────▲──────────┘  │
└───────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────┼─────────────┘

                    ▼                                     │                                │
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────┴─────────────┐

│  1. Ingests Premise ──► Queries D1 Fact Graph ──► Resolves Character States & Version Pins             │
```

## 1. The Cloudflare Agent: Dynamic Parameter Injector

The Cloudflare Workers AI Agent acts as the digital Assistant Director. It does not write prose directly; it operates as an analytical compiler. It evaluates human narrative intent against canonical constraints stored in Cloudflare D1, maps dramatic beats to mathematical parameters, selects character-specific text LoRAs, and formats the execution payload for Child Graph A (`dialogue_generation.json`).

### Parameter Vector Translation

The agent translates subjective qualitative intent into deterministic floats ($0.00$ to $1.00$) consumed by the downstream prompt-assembly nodes:

* **`curtness` ($C \in [0.0, 1.0]$):** Governs syntactic density and mean sentence length. At $C \ge 0.75$, the system prompt enforces monosyllabic responses, ellipses, and dialogue blocks under eight words. At $C \le 0.25$, clauses expand into complex, rhythmic sentences.
* **`pacing` ($P \in [0.0, 1.0]$):** Controls the ratio of action lines to dialogue lines. At $P \ge 0.70$, action blocks are constrained to a single telegraphic sentence describing raw physical motion.
* **`threat_level` ($T \in [0.0, 1.0]$):** Regulates subtext versus explicit conflict. At $T \ge 0.80$, dialogue drops veiled references and targets physical leverage, weapons, or immediate stakes.
* **`subtext_suppression` ($S \in [0.0, 1.0]$):** Determines whether characters verbalize their internal goals or disguise them behind evasive small talk.

### Text LoRA Routing Engine

Open-weights models running locally in Child Graph A (such as Qwen 2.5 14B or 32B) rely on fine-tuned Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) weights to lock character idiolects, vocabularies, and accents. The Agent queries D1 for character metadata and builds the dynamic adapter chain:

| Character ID | Base Model Target | LoRA Artifact | Rank ($r$) / Alpha ($\alpha$) | Trigger Keyword |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `char_elias` | Qwen 2.5 14B Instruct | `elias_voice_v4.safetensors` | $r=16, \alpha=32$ | `<lora:elias_voice:0.85>` |
| `char_vance` | Qwen 2.5 14B Instruct | `vance_cynic_v2.safetensors` | $r=16, \alpha=32$ | `<lora:vance_cynic:0.80>` |
| `char_mira` | Qwen 2.5 14B Instruct | `mira_clinical_v1.safetensors` | $r=8, \alpha=16$ | `<lora:mira_clinical:0.90>` |

### Agent Service Implementation (`src/agent/AssistantDirector.ts`)

```typescript
import { Ai } from '@cloudflare/ai';
import type { D1Database } from '@cloudflare/workers-types';
import { z } from 'zod';

export const AgentInputSchema = z.object({
  scene_id: z.string().min(1),
  episode_num: z.number().int().positive(),
  raw_premise: z.string().min(10),
  active_character_ids: z.array(z.string().min(1)),
  target_conflict_intensity: z.enum(['LOW', 'MEDIUM', 'HIGH', 'EXTREME'])
});

export type AgentInput = z.infer<typeof AgentInputSchema>;

export interface CompiledScenePayload {
  scene_id: string;
  system_instructions: string;
  parameters: {
    curtness: number;
    pacing: number;
    threat_level: number;
    subtext_suppression: number;
  };
  character_configs: Array<{
    id: string;
    name: string;
    lora_path: string;
    trigger: string;
    appearance_anchor: string;
  }>;
  pinned_facts: Array<{
    fact_id: string;
    fact_key: string;
    version: number;
    fact_value: string;
  }>;
}

export class AssistantDirectorAgent {
  constructor(
    private ai: Ai,
    private db: D1Database
  ) {}

  async compileSceneDirective(input: AgentInput): Promise<CompiledScenePayload> {
    // 1. Ingest Canonical Facts from D1
    const placeholders = input.active_character_ids.map(() => '?').join(',');
    const factsQuery = `
      SELECT f.id as fact_id, f.fact_key, f.version, f.fact_value
      FROM facts f
      JOIN (
        SELECT entity_id, fact_key, MAX(version) as max_ver
        FROM facts
        WHERE is_active = 1
        GROUP BY entity_id, fact_key
      ) latest ON f.entity_id = latest.entity_id 
              AND f.fact_key = latest.fact_key 
              AND f.version = latest.max_ver
      WHERE f.entity_id IN (${placeholders})
    `;

    const { results: factRows } = await this.db
      .prepare(factsQuery)
      .bind(...input.active_character_ids)
      .all<{ fact_id: string; fact_key: string; version: number; fact_value: string }>();

    // 2. Fetch Character Manifests and LoRA Profiles
    const charactersQuery = `
      SELECT id, name, entity_type 
      FROM entities 
      WHERE id IN (${placeholders})
    `;
    const { results: charRows } = await this.db
      .prepare(charactersQuery)
      .bind(...input.active_character_ids)
      .all<{ id: string; name: string }>();

    // Static registry mapping character IDs to model adapters
    const LORA_REGISTRY: Record<string, { lora: string; trigger: string; anchor: string }> = {
      char_elias: {
        lora: 'elias_voice_v4.safetensors',
        trigger: '<lora:elias_voice:0.85>',
        anchor: 'Weathered 40s, soaked canvas duster, exposed hydraulic servo arm'
      },
      char_vance: {
        lora: 'vance_cynic_v2.safetensors',
        trigger: '<lora:vance_cynic:0.80>',
        anchor: '50s, grease-smeared jumpsuit, bleeding temple, pinned against rusted steel'
      }
    };

    const characterConfigs = (charRows || []).map((char) => {
      const reg = LORA_REGISTRY[char.id] || {
        lora: 'generic_dialogue.safetensors',
        trigger: '',
        anchor: 'Standard cinematic character'
      };
      return {
        id: char.id,
        name: char.name,
        lora_path: reg.lora,
        trigger: reg.trigger,
        appearance_anchor: reg.anchor
      };
    });

    // 3. Workers AI Evaluation of Dramatic Parameters
    const parameterPrompt = `
      Analyze the following cinematic scene premise and output a strict JSON object mapping dramatic tension.
      Premise: "${input.raw_premise}"
      Intensity setting: "${input.target_conflict_intensity}"
      
      Return EXACTLY this JSON structure:
      {
        "curtness": <float between 0.0 and 1.0>,
        "pacing": <float between 0.0 and 1.0>,
        "threat_level": <float between 0.0 and 1.0>,
        "subtext_suppression": <float between 0.0 and 1.0>
      }
    `;

    const aiResponse = await this.ai.run('@cf/meta/llama-3-8b-instruct', {
      messages: [
        { role: 'system', content: 'You are an automated screenwriting parameter compiler. Return only valid JSON.' },
        { role: 'user', content: parameterPrompt }
      ]
    }) as { response: string };

    let resolvedParams = { curtness: 0.7, pacing: 0.7, threat_level: 0.7, subtext_suppression: 0.8 };
    try {
      resolvedParams = JSON.parse(aiResponse.response);
    } catch {
      // Deterministic fallback based on intensity category
      const intensityMap = {
        LOW: { curtness: 0.3, pacing: 0.3, threat_level: 0.2, subtext_suppression: 0.3 },
        MEDIUM: { curtness: 0.5, pacing: 0.5, threat_level: 0.5, subtext_suppression: 0.5 },
        HIGH: { curtness: 0.75, pacing: 0.8, threat_level: 0.8, subtext_suppression: 0.7 },
        EXTREME: { curtness: 0.9, pacing: 0.9, threat_level: 0.95, subtext_suppression: 0.9 }
      };
      resolvedParams = intensityMap[input.target_conflict_intensity];
    }

    // 4. Pin Fact Dependencies in D1
    for (const fact of factRows || []) {
      await this.db.prepare(`
        INSERT INTO scene_fact_dependencies (scene_id, fact_id, pinned_version, is_dirty)
        VALUES (?, ?, ?, 0)
        ON CONFLICT(scene_id, fact_id) DO UPDATE SET
          pinned_version = excluded.pinned_version,
          is_dirty = 0
      `).bind(input.scene_id, fact.fact_id, fact.version).run();
    }

    return {
      scene_id: input.scene_id,
      system_instructions: `Maintain high visual and phonetic consistency. Adhere strictly to the character anchors.`,
      parameters: resolvedParams,
      character_configs: characterConfigs,
      pinned_facts: factRows || []
    };
  }
}

```

## 2. Astro Production Frontend Architecture

The user interface uses Astro’s hybrid architecture. Static and server-rendered layouts deliver zero-bundle-overhead structural scaffolding, while interactive islands (built with React and Tailwind CSS) manage dynamic timeline manipulation, media playback, and live telemetry streaming.

```
src/
├── layouts/
│   └── ProductionLayout.astro        (Root shell, global nav, system status)
├── pages/
│   ├── index.astro                   (Episode overview, DAG scene dependency board)

│   │   └── [id].astro                (Primary production suite for a single scene)
│   └── api/
│       ├── agent/
│       │   └── compile.ts            (SSR endpoint triggering Cloudflare Agent)
│       ├── animatic/
│       │   └── generate.ts           (Triggers local Child Graphs A & B)

│           └── execute.ts            (Triggers Cloudflare Durable Object)
├── components/

│   │   ├── RemotionPlayerIsland.tsx  (Embedded canvas playing compiled animatic)
│   │   ├── ExposureSheetTable.tsx    (Interactive shot list, timing data, foley cues)
│   │   └── CircuitBreakerMonitor.tsx (Real-time telemetry, attempt counts, overrides)

└── types/
    └── frontend.ts
```

### SSR Endpoint: Compiling and Running Animatic (`src/pages/api/animatic/generate.ts`)

When the user clicks **"Generate Radio Play"** in the Astro interface, this endpoint executes the end-to-end local generation loop:

1. Calls the Cloudflare Workers AI Agent to extract parameters and query D1.
2. Injects the output into Child Graph A via ComfyUI’s local API (`[http://127.0.0.1:8188/prompt](http://127.0.0.1:8188/prompt)`).
3. Takes the generated `dialogue_ast.json`, flushes VRAM, and runs Child Graph B to generate audio stems and calculate frame totals.
4. Returns the compiled `locked_schedule.json` to the client for immediate rendering in the Remotion Player.

```typescript
import type { APIRoute } from 'astro';
import { AssistantDirectorAgent, AgentInputSchema } from '../../../agent/AssistantDirector';
import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import path from 'node:path';

const LOCAL_COMFY = 'http://127.0.0.1:8188';

export const POST: APIRoute = async ({ request, locals }) => {
  try {
    const rawBody = await request.json();
    const validatedInput = AgentInputSchema.parse(rawBody);

    // 1. Initialize Agent
    const agent = new AssistantDirectorAgent(locals.runtime.env.AI, locals.runtime.env.CANON_DB);
    const directive = await agent.compileSceneDirective(validatedInput);

    // 2. Dispatch Local Child Graph A (Dialogue Generation)
    const graphAPath = path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'workflows/dialogue_generation.json');
    const graphATemplate = JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(graphAPath, 'utf-8'));

    // Inject parameters into Graph A nodes
    graphATemplate['2'].inputs.premise = validatedInput.raw_premise;
    graphATemplate['2'].inputs.curtness = directive.parameters.curtness;
    graphATemplate['2'].inputs.threat_level = directive.parameters.threat_level;
    graphATemplate['2'].inputs.pacing = directive.parameters.pacing;

    const queueResA = await fetch(`${LOCAL_COMFY}/prompt`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: graphATemplate })
    });
    const { prompt_id: pidA } = await queueResA.json();

    // Poll local ComfyUI for completion
    await pollComfyCompletion(pidA);

    // 3. Purge Text Models from VRAM
    await fetch(`${LOCAL_COMFY}/free`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ unload_models: true, free_memory: true })
    });

    // 4. Dispatch Local Child Graph B (Audio Synthesis & Duration Calculation)
    const graphBPath = path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'workflows/audio_timing.json');
    const graphBTemplate = JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(graphBPath, 'utf-8'));

    const queueResB = await fetch(`${LOCAL_COMFY}/prompt`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: graphBTemplate })
    });
    const { prompt_id: pidB } = await queueResB.json();

    await pollComfyCompletion(pidB);

    // 5. Ingest Locked Schedule Generated by Graph B
    const schedulePath = path.resolve(process.cwd(), `outputs/manifests/${validatedInput.scene_id}_locked_schedule.json`);
    const lockedSchedule = JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(schedulePath, 'utf-8'));

    return new Response(JSON.stringify({
      success: true,
      scene_id: validatedInput.scene_id,
      schedule: lockedSchedule
    }), {
      status: 200,
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }
    });

  } catch (err: any) {
    return new Response(JSON.stringify({ success: false, error: err.message }), {
      status: 500,
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }
    });
  }
};

async function pollComfyCompletion(promptId: string): Promise<void> {
  let complete = false;
  while (!complete) {
    const res = await fetch(`${LOCAL_COMFY}/history/${promptId}`);
    const data = await res.json();
    if (data[promptId] && data[promptId].status?.completed) {
      complete = true;
    } else {
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 800));
    }
  }
}

```

## 3. Interactive Director Console Island (`src/components/islands/DirectorConsole.tsx`)

This React island gives the user interactive control over narrative variables. Sliders initialize to values recommended by the AI agent based on the conflict setting, but the human director retains manual override authority.

```tsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';

interface DirectorConsoleProps {
  sceneId: string;
  episodeNum: number;
  initialCharacters: Array<{ id: string; name: string }>;
  onAnimaticCompiled: (schedule: any) => void;
}

export const DirectorConsole: React.FC<DirectorConsoleProps> = ({
  sceneId,
  episodeNum,
  initialCharacters,
  onAnimaticCompiled
}) => {
  const [premise, setPremise] = useState('');
  const [intensity, setIntensity] = useState<'LOW' | 'MEDIUM' | 'HIGH' | 'EXTREME'>('HIGH');
  const [curtness, setCurtness] = useState(0.75);
  const [pacing, setPacing] = useState(0.80);
  const [threatLevel, setThreatLevel] = useState(0.85);
  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(false);
  const [statusMessage, setStatusMessage] = useState('');

  const handleGenerate = async () => {
    setIsLoading(true);
    setStatusMessage('Querying Canon Graph & Compiling Directives...');

    try {
      const res = await fetch('/api/animatic/generate', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          scene_id: sceneId,
          episode_num: episodeNum,
          raw_premise: premise,
          active_character_ids: initialCharacters.map((c) => c.id),
          target_conflict_intensity: intensity
        })
      });

      const data = await res.json();
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(data.error || 'Failed to compile animatic');

      setStatusMessage('Animatic Compiled Successfully.');
      onAnimaticCompiled(data.schedule);
    } catch (err: any) {
      setStatusMessage(`Compilation Failed: ${err.message}`);
    } finally {
      setIsLoading(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <div className="bg-[#121218] border border-[#22222e] rounded-lg p-6 text-gray-200">
      <div className="flex justify-between items-center mb-4">
        <h2 className="text-xl font-mono font-bold text-white tracking-wide">
          DIRECTOR PARAMETER CONTROL // {sceneId.toUpperCase()}
        </h2>
        <span className="text-xs font-mono bg-blue-950 text-blue-400 border border-blue-800 px-2.5 py-1 rounded">
          EPISODE {episodeNum}
        </span>
      </div>

      <div className="mb-4">
        <label className="block text-xs font-mono text-gray-400 uppercase tracking-wider mb-2">
          Scene Narrative Premise
        </label>
        <textarea
          rows={3}
          value={premise}
          onChange={(e) => setPremise(e.target.value)}
          placeholder="Elias corners Vance against the rusted shipping containers. Rain is torrential. Elias requires the cipher before perimeter lockdown."
          className="w-full bg-[#0a0a0e] border border-[#2a2a38] rounded p-3 text-sm text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-blue-500 font-sans"
        />
      </div>

      <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 mb-6">
        <div>
          <label className="block text-xs font-mono text-gray-400 uppercase mb-2">
            Conflict Intensity Preset
          </label>
          <select
            value={intensity}
            onChange={(e) => setIntensity(e.target.value as any)}
            className="w-full bg-[#0a0a0e] border border-[#2a2a38] rounded p-2 text-sm text-white font-mono"
          >
            <option value="LOW">LOW (Expository, Reflective)</option>
            <option value="MEDIUM">MEDIUM (Rising Suspicion)</option>
            <option value="HIGH">HIGH (Imminent Violence)</option>
            <option value="EXTREME">EXTREME (Physical Lethality)</option>
          </select>
        </div>

        <div className="space-y-3">
          <div>
            <div className="flex justify-between text-xs font-mono">
              <span className="text-gray-400">CURTNESS</span>
              <span className="text-blue-400">{curtness.toFixed(2)}</span>
            </div>
            <input
              type="range"
              min="0"
              max="1"
              step="0.05"
              value={curtness}
              onChange={(e) => setCurtness(parseFloat(e.target.value))}
              className="w-full h-1 bg-[#22222e] rounded appearance-none cursor-pointer"
            />
          </div>

          <div>
            <div className="flex justify-between text-xs font-mono">
              <span className="text-gray-400">PACING (ACTION DENSITY)</span>
              <span className="text-blue-400">{pacing.toFixed(2)}</span>
            </div>
            <input
              type="range"
              min="0"
              max="1"
              step="0.05"
              value={pacing}
              onChange={(e) => setPacing(parseFloat(e.target.value))}
              className="w-full h-1 bg-[#22222e] rounded appearance-none cursor-pointer"
            />
          </div>

          <div>
            <div className="flex justify-between text-xs font-mono">
              <span className="text-gray-400">THREAT LEVEL</span>
              <span className="text-blue-400">{threatLevel.toFixed(2)}</span>
            </div>
            <input
              type="range"
              min="0"
              max="1"
              step="0.05"
              value={threatLevel}
              onChange={(e) => setThreatLevel(parseFloat(e.target.value))}
              className="w-full h-1 bg-[#22222e] rounded appearance-none cursor-pointer"
            />
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div className="flex items-center justify-between pt-4 border-t border-[#1e1e2a]">
        <span className="text-xs font-mono text-gray-400">{statusMessage}</span>
        <button
          onClick={handleGenerate}
          disabled={isLoading || premise.length < 10}
          className="bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-500 disabled:bg-gray-800 disabled:text-gray-600 text-white font-mono text-sm px-5 py-2.5 rounded transition flex items-center gap-2"
        >
          {isLoading ? (
            <>
              <svg className="animate-spin h-4 w-4 text-white" viewBox="0 0 24 24">
                <circle className="opacity-25" cx="12" cy="12" r="10" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="4" fill="none" />
                <path className="opacity-75" fill="currentColor" d="M4 12a8 8 0 018-8V0C5.373 0 0 5.373 0 12h4z" />
              </svg>
              COMPILING LOCAL ANIMATIC...
            </>
          ) : (
            'EXECUTE RADIO PLAY PIPELINE'
          )}
        </button>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};

```

## 4. The Remotion Player Island (`src/components/islands/RemotionPlayerIsland.tsx`)

The Remotion Player Island embeds the Step 2 React composition engine directly within the Astro browser view. It ingests the JSON schedule produced by the API, mounts audio stems dynamically from local public storage, and allows the director to scrub through the locked animatic.

This component holds the **Director Sign-Off Gate**. The cloud GPU batch cannot be dispatched until the human views this playback and clicks **"Authorize Cloud Video Batch"**.

```tsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { Player } from '@remotion/player';
import { RadioPlayComposition } from '../../remotion/RadioPlayComposition';
import type { SceneManifest } from '../../types/radioPlay';

interface RemotionPlayerIslandProps {
  sceneId: string;
  initialSchedule: SceneManifest | null;
}

export const RemotionPlayerIsland: React.FC<RemotionPlayerIslandProps> = ({
  sceneId,
  initialSchedule
}) => {
  const [schedule, setSchedule] = useState<SceneManifest | null>(initialSchedule);
  const [isAuthorizing, setIsAuthorizing] = useState(false);
  const [dispatchStatus, setDispatchStatus] = useState<string | null>(null);

  if (!schedule) {
    return (
      <div className="bg-[#0e0e12] border border-[#1f1f2a] rounded-lg h-[480px] flex flex-col items-center justify-center text-gray-500 font-mono">
        <svg className="w-12 h-12 mb-3 text-gray-600" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke="currentColor">
          <path strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round" strokeWidth={1.5} d="M14.752 11.168l-3.197-2.132A1 1 0 0010 9.87v4.263a1 1 0 001.555.832l3.197-2.132a1 1 0 000-1.664z" />
          <path strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round" strokeWidth={1.5} d="M21 12a9 9 0 11-18 0 9 9 0 0118 0z" />
        </svg>
        <p>AWAITING SCRIPT & AUDIO COMPILATION</p>
        <p className="text-xs text-gray-600 mt-1">Execute the parameter pipeline above to populate animatic.</p>
      </div>
    );
  }

  // Calculate master duration in frames across all serialized shots
  const totalFrames = schedule.shots.reduce(
    (acc, shot) => acc + (shot.calculated_frames ?? 24),
    0
  );

  const handleAuthorizeCloudBatch = async () => {
    setIsAuthorizing(true);
    setDispatchStatus('Contacting Edge Orchestrator...');

    try {
      const res = await fetch('/api/dispatch/execute', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          scene_id: sceneId,
          shots: schedule.shots.map((s) => ({
            shot_id: s.shot_id,
            target_frames: s.calculated_frames,
            character_id: s.character_id,
            visual_prompt: s.action_context,
            camera_intent: s.camera_intent
          }))
        })
      });

      const data = await res.json();
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(data.message || 'Dispatch rejected by Orchestrator');

      setDispatchStatus(`Dispatched ${data.dispatched_count} shots to RunPod. Monitoring active.`);
    } catch (err: any) {
      setDispatchStatus(`Authorization Blocked: ${err.message}`);
    } finally {
      setIsAuthorizing(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <div className="bg-[#121218] border border-[#22222e] rounded-lg p-6">
      <div className="flex justify-between items-center mb-4">
        <div>
          <h3 className="font-mono font-bold text-white text-lg">ANIMATIC PREVIEW // RADIO PLAY</h3>
          <p className="text-xs font-mono text-gray-400">
            TOTAL DURATION: {totalFrames} FRAMES ({(totalFrames / 24).toFixed(2)}s) @ 24 FPS
          </p>
        </div>
        <span className="text-xs font-mono bg-green-950 text-green-400 border border-green-800 px-2.5 py-1 rounded">
          TEMPORAL LOCK ACHIEVED
        </span>
      </div>

      {/* Embedded 16:9 Canvas Player */}
      <div className="w-full aspect-video rounded overflow-hidden border border-[#2a2a3a] mb-6 bg-black">
        <Player
          component={RadioPlayComposition as any}
          inputProps={{
            manifest: schedule,
            totalDurationInFrames: totalFrames
          }}
          durationInFrames={Math.max(1, totalFrames)}
          fps={24}
          compositionWidth={1920}
          compositionHeight={1080}
          style={{ width: '100%', height: '100%' }}
          controls
        />
      </div>

      {/* Verification Matrix & Sign-Off Button */}
      <div className="bg-[#0a0a0e] border border-[#1e1e2a] rounded p-4 flex items-center justify-between">
        <div>
          <div className="text-xs font-mono text-gray-300 font-bold mb-1">
            GATEWAY 3: DIRECTOR VERIFICATION
          </div>
          <p className="text-xs text-gray-500 font-sans max-w-xl">
            Confirm speech cadences, parenthetical inflections, and shot boundaries. 
            Authorizing will lock fact dependencies in D1 and dispatch serverless GPUs.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
          {dispatchStatus && (
            <span className="text-xs font-mono text-blue-400 max-w-xs text-right">
              {dispatchStatus}
            </span>
          )}
          <button
            onClick={handleAuthorizeCloudBatch}
            disabled={isAuthorizing}
            className="bg-emerald-600 hover:bg-emerald-500 disabled:bg-gray-800 disabled:text-gray-600 text-white font-mono text-sm px-6 py-3 rounded transition flex items-center gap-2 font-bold shadow-lg shadow-emerald-950/40"
          >
            {isAuthorizing ? 'DISPATCHING...' : 'AUTHORIZE CLOUD VIDEO BATCH'}
          </button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};

```

## 5. Live Circuit Breaker & Telemetry Monitor Island (`src/components/islands/CircuitBreakerMonitor.tsx`)

Once shots dispatch to RunPod via the `ShotCoordinator` Durable Objects (Step 4), this island establishes a Server-Sent Events (SSE) or WebSocket connection to monitor execution states, inspect error logs, track attempt counters ($N \le 2$), and display manual override buttons if a circuit breaker trips.

```tsx
import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react';

interface ShotTelemetry {
  shot_id: string;
  status: 'IDLE' | 'DISPATCHED' | 'PROCESSING' | 'COMPLETED' | 'FAILED' | 'TIMED_OUT' | 'CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TRIPPED';
  attempt_count: number;
  active_job_id: string | null;
  latest_asset_url: string | null;
  error_log?: string;
}

export const CircuitBreakerMonitor: React.FC<{ sceneId: string; shotIds: string[] }> = ({
  sceneId,
  shotIds
}) => {
  const [telemetry, setTelemetry] = useState<Record<string, ShotTelemetry>>({});

  // Poll shot states from edge orchestrator
  useEffect(() => {
    const fetchStates = async () => {
      const updates: Record<string, ShotTelemetry> = {};
      for (const id of shotIds) {
        try {
          const res = await fetch(`/api/shots/${id}/status`);
          if (res.ok) {
            updates[id] = await res.json();
          }
        } catch {
          // Ignore network drops; poll will retry
        }
      }
      setTelemetry(updates);
    };

    fetchStates();
    const interval = setInterval(fetchStates, 2500);
    return () => clearInterval(interval);
  }, [shotIds]);

  const handleManualReset = async (shotId: string) => {
    const reason = window.prompt(`Enter justification for overriding circuit breaker on ${shotId}:`);
    if (!reason) return;

    await fetch(`/api/shots/${shotId}/reset`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ reason })
    });
  };

  return (
    <div className="bg-[#121218] border border-[#22222e] rounded-lg p-6">
      <div className="flex justify-between items-center mb-4">
        <h3 className="font-mono font-bold text-white text-lg">
          ORCHESTRATOR TELEMETRY // REAL-TIME EXECUTION
        </h3>
        <span className="text-xs font-mono text-gray-400">POLLING CLOUDFLARE DURABLE OBJECTS</span>
      </div>

      <div className="overflow-x-auto">
        <table className="w-full text-left font-mono text-xs">
          <thead>
            <tr className="border-b border-[#22222e] text-gray-500">
              <th className="pb-3">SHOT ID</th>
              <th className="pb-3">STATUS</th>
              <th className="pb-3">ATTEMPTS</th>
              <th className="pb-3">ACTIVE RUNPOD ID</th>
              <th className="pb-3">DELIVERABLE</th>
              <th className="pb-3 text-right">ACTION</th>
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody className="divide-y divide-[#1a1a24]">
            {shotIds.map((id) => {
              const shot = telemetry[id] || {
                shot_id: id,
                status: 'IDLE',
                attempt_count: 0,
                active_job_id: null,
                latest_asset_url: null
              };

              const isTripped = shot.status === 'CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TRIPPED';
              const isCompleted = shot.status === 'COMPLETED';

              return (
                <tr key={id} className="text-gray-300">
                  <td className="py-3.5 font-bold text-white">{id}</td>
                  <td className="py-3.5">
                    <span
                      className={`px-2 py-0.5 rounded border text-[10px] ${
                        isCompleted
                          ? 'bg-emerald-950 text-emerald-400 border-emerald-800'
                          : isTripped
                          ? 'bg-red-950 text-red-400 border-red-800 animate-pulse'
                          : shot.status === 'PROCESSING'
                          ? 'bg-blue-950 text-blue-400 border-blue-800'
                          : 'bg-gray-900 text-gray-400 border-gray-800'
                      }`}
                    >
                      {shot.status}
                    </span>
                  </td>
                  <td className="py-3.5">
                    <span className={shot.attempt_count >= 2 ? 'text-red-400 font-bold' : ''}>
                      {shot.attempt_count} / 2
                    </span>
                  </td>
                  <td className="py-3.5 text-gray-500">{shot.active_job_id || '---'}</td>
                  <td className="py-3.5">
                    {shot.latest_asset_url ? (
                      <a
                        href={shot.latest_asset_url}
                        target="_blank"
                        rel="noreferrer"
                        className="text-blue-400 hover:underline flex items-center gap-1"
                      >
                        VIEW MP4
                      </a>
                    ) : (
                      <span className="text-gray-600">NOT PRODUCED</span>
                    )}
                  </td>
                  <td className="py-3.5 text-right">
                    {isTripped && (
                      <button
                        onClick={() => handleManualReset(id)}
                        className="bg-red-900/60 hover:bg-red-800 text-red-200 border border-red-700 px-3 py-1 rounded text-[11px] font-bold"
                      >
                        RESET CIRCUIT
                      </button>
                    )}
                  </td>
                </tr>
              );
            })}
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};

```

## 6. The Master Astro Scene Page (`src/pages/scenes/[id].astro`)

This page unifies all server-side context and client-side islands into an operational workspace.

```astro
---
import ProductionLayout from '../../layouts/ProductionLayout.astro';
import { DirectorConsole } from '../../components/islands/DirectorConsole';
import { RemotionPlayerIsland } from '../../components/islands/RemotionPlayerIsland';
import { CircuitBreakerMonitor } from '../../components/islands/CircuitBreakerMonitor';

const { id: sceneId } = Astro.params;

if (!sceneId) {
  return Astro.redirect('/404');
}

// Fetch canonical scene details and assigned characters from Cloudflare D1
const db = Astro.locals.runtime.env.CANON_DB;

const sceneData = await db.prepare(`
  SELECT id, episode_num, scene_order, slugline, status 
  FROM scenes 
  WHERE id = ?
`).bind(sceneId).first();

if (!sceneData) {
  return Astro.redirect('/404');
}

// Extract characters present in this scene
const { results: characters } = await db.prepare(`
  SELECT e.id, e.name 
  FROM entities e
  JOIN scene_fact_dependencies sfd ON e.id = sfd.fact_id
  WHERE sfd.scene_id = ? AND e.entity_type = 'CHARACTER'
  GROUP BY e.id
`).bind(sceneId).all();

// Default characters if no dependencies explicitly pinned yet
const resolvedCharacters = characters && characters.length > 0 ? characters : [
  { id: 'char_elias', name: 'ELIAS' },
  { id: 'char_vance', name: 'VANCE' }
];

const mockShotIds = [
  `${sceneId}_sh01`,
  `${sceneId}_sh02`,
  `${sceneId}_sh03`
];
---

<ProductionLayout title={`Scene Console // ${sceneId}`}>
  <main className="max-w-7xl mx-auto px-4 py-8 space-y-8">
    <div className="flex justify-between items-center border-b border-[#22222e] pb-4">
      <div>
        <h1 className="text-2xl font-mono font-bold text-white">{sceneData.slugline}</h1>
        <p className="text-xs font-mono text-gray-400 mt-1">
          SCENE ID: <span className="text-blue-400">{sceneId}</span> | STATUS: <span className="text-emerald-400">{sceneData.status}</span>
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <!-- 1. Narrative Directive & Parameter Injector -->
    <DirectorConsole
      client:load
      sceneId={sceneId}
      episodeNum={sceneData.episode_num}
      initialCharacters={resolvedCharacters}
      onAnimaticCompiled={() => {}}
    />

    <!-- 2. The Remotion Radio Play Verification Canvas -->
    <RemotionPlayerIsland
      client:visible
      sceneId={sceneId}
      initialSchedule={null}
    />

    <!-- 3. Serverless Orchestrator Telemetry & Circuit Breakers -->
    <CircuitBreakerMonitor
      client:idle
      sceneId={sceneId}
      shotIds={mockShotIds}
    />
  </main>
</ProductionLayout>
```

## 7. End-to-End Operational Lifecycle: Concept to Cloud Batch

The complete production lifecycle functions through a deterministic sequence:

```
[ Step 1: Input Premise ]
  Director enters: "Elias corners Vance on Sector 4 docks. High physical stakes."
  Director selects preset: "EXTREME"
        │
        ▼
[ Step 2: Agent Compilation (Workers AI + D1) ]
  • D1 query pulls latest Fact versions: Elias has hydraulic arm (v3).
  • Llama-3-8B evaluates premise -> Emits { curtness: 0.9, pacing: 0.95, threat_level: 0.95 }.
  • Fact versions pinned into scene_fact_dependencies (is_dirty = 0).
        │
        ▼
[ Step 3: Local Generation (Child Graphs A & B via ComfyUI) ]
  • Graph A runs Qwen 2.5 14B with Elias & Vance LoRAs. Emits Screenplay + Dialogue AST.
  • VRAM flushed via /free API.
  • Graph B runs Parler-TTS/CosyVoice -> Generates audio stems.
  • Math nodes compute duration:
      sh01: 3.8s -> 92 frames (+ 16 padding = 108 frames)
      sh02: 4.2s -> 101 frames (+ 16 padding = 117 frames)
  • Manifest emitted: ep01_sc03_locked_schedule.json.
        │
        ▼
[ Step 4: Director Animatic Review (Remotion Player Island) ]
  • Astro mounts Remotion Composition inside the browser.
  • Dialogue stems play over ducked industrial rain bed.
  • Director inspects pacing and dialogue deliveries on the visual slate HUD.
        │
        ▼
[ Step 5: Authorization & Cloud Dispatch ]
  • Director clicks "AUTHORIZE CLOUD VIDEO BATCH".
  • Astro hits /api/dispatch/execute.
  • Edge Orchestrator verifies scene is not dirty (is_dirty == 0).
  • ShotCoordinator Durable Objects instantiate per shot:
      - ep01_sc03_sh01 DO arms 180s watchdog, sets attempt = 1.
      - Dispatches payload (108 frames, #00FF00 prompt) to RunPod.
        │
        ▼
[ Step 6: GPU Execution & Telemetry Feedback ]
  • Serverless RTX 4090 hydrates from R2, renders greenscreen video plate.
  • Webhook fires -> Cloudflare Queue -> ShotCoordinator DO marks COMPLETED.
  • CircuitBreakerMonitor island updates table row: [COMPLETED] [VIEW MP4].

```

This ensures the writer-director retains complete creative authority over dramatic intent while delegating formatting, timing calculations, and infrastructure management to specialized automated layers. System costs remain bounded, assets are verified prior to heavy GPU allocation, and edge actors prevent catastrophic execution runaways.This entire architecture is built on a radical shift in how we approach generative AI: moving away from treating AI as a "magic box" where you type a prompt and hope for a good video, and instead treating it as an industrial assembly line.

If we strip away all the code, serverless configurations, and database schemas, the system rests on these six fundamental concepts.

## 1. Audio is the Architect of Time

Generative video is the most expensive and volatile part of the pipeline. You cannot afford to guess how long a scene should be.

* **The Principle:** Audio is computationally cheap; video is computationally expensive.
* **The Execution:** The system generates the dialogue and foley first (the "Radio Play"), measures the exact millisecond duration, and converts it to a hard frame count.
* **The Result:** When the cloud GPU spins up, it is given an exact, non-negotiable frame target (e.g., exactly 108 frames). Not a single GPU cycle is wasted rendering unused footage.

## 2. Structural Enforcement over Agent Trust

LLM agents are prone to hallucination, infinite loops, and forgetting instructions. You cannot trust an agent to follow rules about budgets or story continuity.

* **The Principle:** Do not ask the agent to behave; remove its mechanical ability to misbehave.
* **The Execution:** The agent is cast as a Line Producer. Its parameters are locked into strict JSON schemas. Retry limits (circuit breakers) and narrative continuity (canon facts) are enforced by server-side Cloudflare Durable Objects and D1 databases, not by prompt instructions.
* **The Result:** If an agent tries to spend too much money or break narrative canon, the server physically rejects the request.

## 3. Decoupling Modalities (The Contract System)

Jamming text generation, text-to-speech, and high-resolution video diffusion into a single ComfyUI graph causes massive VRAM bottlenecks and catastrophic failures.

* **The Principle:** Isolate every modality and connect them with strict data contracts.
* **The Execution:**
* Child Graph A (LLM) outputs a JSON Script.
* Child Graph B (TTS) reads the JSON and outputs Audio + a Timing Manifest.
* Child Graph C (Video) reads the Manifest and outputs MP4s.


* **The Result:** Memory is cleanly flushed between steps. If the audio fails, the video GPU never turns on.

## 4. The Greenscreen VFX Paradigm

Asking a diffusion model to render a consistent character, consistent motion, *and* a consistent background all at once causes perspective warping and geometry hallucinations.

* **The Principle:** Subtract complexity from the neural network and give it back to traditional software.
* **The Execution:** The video model is constrained to generate only the character on a solid `#00FF00` neon green background. The background environment is added later using traditional chroma-key compositing via Remotion code.
* **The Result:** VRAM is dedicated 100% to character fidelity. Backgrounds stop morphing, and characters stop melting into the furniture.

## 5. Scale-to-Zero Economics (The Hydration Method)

Renting persistent cloud GPUs costs hundreds of dollars a month per machine, even when you aren't rendering.

* **The Principle:** You should only pay for the exact seconds a GPU is rendering a frame.
* **The Execution:** Serverless RunPod instances boot from zero, use `s5cmd` to hyper-fetch 20GB of models from Cloudflare R2 in under 15 seconds without bandwidth fees, render the video, push the result, and terminate.
* **The Result:** Professional-grade animation plates cost roughly $0.015 per take. The infrastructure costs $0.00 when you are asleep.

## 6. The Human as the Pre-Compute Gatekeeper

Automated pipelines can rapidly generate massive amounts of garbage, burning through budgets in minutes if left unchecked.

* **The Principle:** Automation handles the logistics; humans handle the authorization.
* **The Execution:** The system builds a lightweight, audio-only animatic (via Remotion) and presents it in the Astro UI. The cloud GPUs are physically locked until the human director reviews the pacing and clicks "Authorize."
* **The Result:** You maintain total creative authority. No heavy compute is ever purchased without human sign-off on the underlying script and audio timing.

---

**The Bottom Line:** You are not building an AI video generator. You are building an automated animation studio where AI models are treated as highly specialized, strictly managed factory workers.To understand how this highly structured, serverless, database-driven architecture empowers the artist, we must first dispel the greatest misconception about generative AI: the idea that the "prompt" is the art.

In consumer-grade AI, the user types a prompt into a text box, rolls the dice, and accepts whatever the black box spits out. That is not art; that is slot-machine curation. The architecture we have built—the modular child graphs, the Cloudflare D1 continuity database, the Remotion audio engine, and the serverless greenscreen execution—is explicitly designed to kill the slot machine.

This system does not replace the artist. It elevates the artist to the role of **Showrunner, Director, and Executive Producer**. By offloading the mechanical drudgery of tracking continuity, calculating frame counts, and rendering pixels to the machine, the architecture isolates the artist’s most valuable asset: **Creative Intent.**

Here is an exhaustive, nuanced exploration of how this specific pipeline empowers the artist at every stage of the creative lifecycle, transforming a solitary creator into an entire animation studio.

---

## 1. The Artist as Worldbuilder: Reclaiming Character and Canon

In traditional generative video, artists suffer from "latent space amnesia." You generate a character in one shot, and in the next, their jacket changes color, their scar switches sides, and their personality drifts. The artist spends all their time fighting the model to remember basic facts, which crushes creative momentum.

This architecture solves this through the **Cloudflare D1 Canon Database** and the **Text/Visual LoRA routing**.

### Curating the Actor, Not the Frame

Instead of typing exhaustive visual descriptions into every prompt (e.g., *"man, 40s, brown duster, metal arm, brooding"*), the artist’s primary visual work shifts to the pre-production phase. The artist designs the character once—perhaps by painting turnaround sheets, sculpting a 3D reference model, or photographing a real actor. They train a Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) on this specific, curated dataset.

The LoRA becomes the "Actor." When the system dispatches to the ComfyUI RunPod worker, it seamlessly loads `visual_char_elias_v4.safetensors`. The artist is no longer begging the AI to generate someone who *looks like* Elias; they are casting their bespoke, handcrafted digital actor into the scene.

### The Immutable Show Bible

The D1 relational database acts as an automated script supervisor. When an artist is writing Episode 8, they don't have to remember if the protagonist's cybernetic arm was damaged in Episode 3. The database knows.

Because the artist built the world logic into the SQLite tables, the Cloudflare Agent automatically appends canonical facts to the generation payloads. This empowers the writer to focus purely on the emotional stakes of the scene, secure in the knowledge that the system will mathematically enforce physical and narrative continuity. The artist is freed from the cognitive load of micro-management, allowing them to construct vast, serialized, multi-season narratives that would normally require a room full of continuity editors to maintain.

---

## 2. The Artist as Director: Speaking the Language of Drama

Look at the Astro Frontend we designed. Notice what is missing: there is no text box asking the artist to write a ComfyUI diffusion prompt. There are no input fields for `cfg_scale`, `denoise_strength`, or `sampler_name`.

Artists should not have to speak the language of tensor mathematics. They should speak the language of drama.

### The Parameter Injector as a Directorial Interface

The Astro UI gives the artist a console with sliders for **Curtness**, **Pacing**, **Threat Level**, and **Conflict Intensity**. This is a profound shift in human-computer interaction.

When a director is on a live-action set, they do not tell an actor, *"Contract your zygomatic major muscle by 15% and increase your vocal decibels."* They say, *"He's lying to you. Be colder. Cut him off."*

By using the Cloudflare Workers AI Agent to translate these dramatic intents into the JSON Abstract Syntax Tree (AST), the artist is empowered to direct the local LLM (Child Graph A) exactly as they would a human performer. If the scene feels too melodramatic, the artist doesn't rewrite the dialogue by hand; they simply drag the "Curtness" slider to 0.85 and hit generate. The system rewrites the scene, stripping out the subtext and delivering blunt, fragmented dialogue. The artist iterates on *emotion*, while the machine handles the syntax.

---

## 3. The Artist as Editor: The Power of the Radio Play

Animation is uniquely unforgiving. In live-action film, if a scene's pacing is wrong, you can save it in the edit room by cutting to B-roll or holding on a reaction shot. In animation, every single frame must be drawn or rendered. If you render 500 frames and realize the scene is boring, you have wasted immense time and money.

This is why the **Remotion Radio Play Engine (Child Graph B)** is the most creatively empowering tool in the entire pipeline.

### Sculpting Time at Zero Cost

Before a single cloud GPU is rented, the system synthesizes the text-to-speech dialogue and layers it over ambient foley (rain, machinery, room tone) inside the Astro browser.

The artist closes their eyes and listens.

* *Does the villain's monologue drag?*
* *Is there enough silence after the gunshot?*
* *Does the dialogue overlap sound natural?*

Because this step runs locally and costs nothing, the artist is free to fail. They can re-roll the audio, adjust the pre-roll and post-roll frame padding, and experiment with radically different pacing structures in seconds.

### The Human Gatekeeper

We explicitly designed the pipeline to halt at the Remotion Animatic stage. The cloud GPUs cannot spin up until the artist clicks **"Authorize Cloud Video Batch."**

This is a psychological safety net. When artists know a system will automatically spend money, they become conservative. They play it safe. By placing a hard human checkpoint between the cheap audio generation and the expensive video generation, the system encourages wild, avant-garde experimentation in the writing and audio phases, knowing the artist has absolute veto power before the meter starts running.

---

## 4. The Artist as VFX Supervisor: The Greenscreen Paradigm

The greatest aesthetic flaw of generative AI video is the total lack of spatial intent. Latent diffusion models do not understand 3D space; they hallucinate pixels based on noise. If you ask an AI to generate a character walking down a hallway, the walls will morph, the lighting will shift, and the perspective will warp. The artist is held hostage by the model's hallucinations.

By isolating the video diffusion (Child Graph C) to generate characters exclusively on a `#00FF00` greenscreen, the architecture hands absolute spatial and environmental control back to the artist.

### Marrying AI with Traditional Art Forms

Because the AI is only generating the character silhouette, the artist is free to create the background environment using whatever medium they love most:

* **The Painter:** A traditional artist can paint a sprawling, hyper-detailed matte painting in watercolor or acrylic, scan it, and composite the AI character walking through their hand-painted world.
* **The 3D Generalist:** An artist can build a gritty, cyberpunk alleyway in Unreal Engine or Blender, lock the camera angle, render it with perfect ray-traced lighting, and drop the AI greenscreen character into the scene.
* **The Stop-Motion Artisan:** An artist could build physical miniature sets out of cardboard and clay, light them with practical LEDs, photograph them, and composite the digital actors inside.

The AI ceases to be a replacement for the artist’s style; it becomes a rotoscoped asset *within* the artist’s style.

### Remotion as the Digital Optical Printer

Once the greenscreen character and the bespoke background are combined in Remotion, the artist acts as the VFX compositor. Through code, they apply global color grades, simulate lens distortion, add film grain, and program camera shakes. By applying these effects globally over both the AI character and the bespoke background, the layers are "welded" together, creating a cohesive, intentional cinematic frame that no raw prompt could ever generate.

## 5. The Artist as Executive Producer: Financial and Output Independence

Historically, the barrier to entry for producing high-quality episodic animation has been capital. You needed millions of dollars to hire storyboard artists, voice actors, layout artists, keyframe animators, and render farm technicians.

Because of this financial barrier, artists had to pitch their ideas to network executives. To get funding, they had to compromise their vision, sand down the edges of their stories, and appeal to the widest possible demographic. Capital requirements breed creative homogenization.

### The Democratization of the Studio

The scale-to-zero serverless architecture (RunPod + Cloudflare R2 + Durable Objects) fundamentally alters the unit economics of storytelling.

As we calculated, generating a frame-accurate, aesthetically locked, green-screened animation plate costs roughly **$0.015 per take**. A full 10-minute animated episode might contain 150 shots. Even at a 3:1 take ratio, the total cloud GPU compute cost for an entire episode drops to under **$10.00**.

When an episode of television costs ten dollars to render, the artist no longer needs a network executive. They do not need greenlights, focus groups, or venture capital.

### The Freedom of Niche Storytelling

Because the financial risk is essentially zero, the creative risk can be absolute.

* Want to create a hyper-violent, biopunk-noir Southern Gothic mystery that only appeals to 50,000 people on YouTube? You can.
* Want to rewrite the climax of your season finale because you had a better idea in the shower this morning? You can, because re-rendering the scene costs less than a cup of coffee.

The Cloudflare edge orchestrator ensures that no idle servers are draining the artist's bank account while they sleep. The infrastructure scales instantly from zero to 100 GPUs when the artist clicks "Authorize," and immediately scales back to zero the millisecond the MP4s are uploaded to R2.
