### The Deterministic Invariant Linter (`src/services/invariantLinter.ts`)

This pure function inspects candidate screenplay text and AST shots generated by Child Graph A, catching illegal actions before audio or GPU execution begins:

```typescript
import { SomaticVector, LogisticalVector, EpistemicVector } from '../types/canonState';

export interface LinterViolation {
  rule: 'SOMATIC_MOTOR_BREACH' | 'LOGISTICAL_IMPOSSIBILITY' | 'EPISTEMIC_THIRD_RAIL';
  entity_id: string;
  offending_text: string;
  reason: string;
}

export function lintSceneAgainstCanon(params: {
  screenplay_text: string;
  shots: Array<{ character_id: string; dialogue_text: string; action_context: string }>;
  somatic_states: Record<string, SomaticVector>;
  logistical_states: Record<string, LogisticalVector>;
  epistemic_states: Record<string, EpistemicVector>;
}): { valid: boolean; violations: LinterViolation[] } {
  const violations: LinterViolation[] = [];
  const textLower = params.screenplay_text.toLowerCase();

  // 1. Audit Somatic Invariants (Banned Kinetic Verbs & Motor Limits)
  for (const [entityId, somatic] of Object.entries(params.somatic_states)) {
    for (const bannedVerb of somatic.banned_kinetic_verbs) {
      // Check if candidate prose describes this character executing a forbidden verb
      const regex = new RegExp(`\\b(${entityId.replace('char_', '')}|he|she)\\s+([\\w\\s]{0,15})\\b${bannedVerb}\\b`, 'i');
      if (regex.test(textLower)) {
        violations.push({
          rule: 'SOMATIC_MOTOR_BREACH',
          entity_id: entityId,
          offending_text: bannedVerb,
          reason: `Character '${entityId}' has motor restrictions under baseline '${somatic.locomotion_baseline}'. Action '${bannedVerb}' is physically impermissible.`
        });
      }
    }
  }

  // 2. Audit Logistical Invariants (Equip Slots & Held Items)
  for (const shot of params.shots) {
    const logistics = params.logistical_states[shot.character_id];
    if (!logistics) continue;

    // Verify two-handed actions don't occur when hand slot is filled with an un-holstered prop
    if (logistics.slots.held && /draws\s+a\s+weapon|racks\s+the\s+slide/i.test(shot.action_context)) {
      if (logistics.slots.held !== 'service_revolver') {
        violations.push({
          rule: 'LOGISTICAL_IMPOSSIBILITY',
          entity_id: shot.character_id,
          offending_text: shot.action_context,
          reason: `Character is already holding '${logistics.slots.held}' in hand slot; cannot draw another item without a holstering action.`
        });
      }
    }
  }

  // 3. Audit Epistemic Third Rails (Escalation Ceilings)
  for (const [entityId, epistemic] of Object.entries(params.epistemic_states)) {
    if (!epistemic.escalation_ceiling) continue;

    // Search shots delivered by this character for unprompted third-rail keywords
    const keywords = epistemic.escalation_ceiling.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).filter(w => w.length > 4);
    for (const shot of params.shots) {
      if (shot.character_id === entityId) {
        const dialogueLower = shot.dialogue_text.toLowerCase();
        const hit = keywords.find(k => dialogueLower.includes(k));
        if (hit) {
          violations.push({
            rule: 'EPISTEMIC_THIRD_RAIL',
            entity_id: entityId,
            offending_text: shot.dialogue_text,
            reason: `Dialogue breached the character's uncrossable Escalation Ceiling ('${epistemic.escalation_ceiling}').`
          });
        }
      }
    }
  }

  return {
    valid: violations.length === 0,
    violations
  };
}

```

### Part 1: The Core Reiteration (What We Know to Be True vs. What Was Overclaimed)

#### 1. The Validated Structural Backbone (Keep & Defend)

* **Typed State Vectors over Flat Strings:** Expanding the Phase 0 minimal Fact model into typed categories (**Somatic**, **Logistical**, **Epistemic**) is mathematically sound. A relational engine cannot enforce physical impossibility from an arbitrary string (`"Octavius is sick"`), but it *can* compute constraints against discrete enums (`locomotion: neuropathy_shuffle`) and bounded scalar values (`fuel_liters: 28, max: 120`).
* **Deterministic Gating Over AI Critics:** Keeping LLMs completely out of the gatekeeper role remains the correct architectural choice. A regex/AST rule-engine checking against a fixed state ledger never hallucinates, costs zero tokens, and cannot be bribed by prompt-drift.
* **Blast-Radius Invalidation via Snapshot Hashing:** Replacing single-fact version checks with cryptographic entity-state hashes ($S_n \rightarrow S_{n+1}$) preserves the core load-bearing feature of the entire project: **automatic dirty-state propagation.** Modifying an upstream truth cascades downstream without mutating historic ledger entries.
* **The Dual-Database Locality Split:** Separating the authoring environment (Neo4j for deep graph traversals and relational intuition) from the edge execution path (Cloudflare D1 for sub-10ms boolean render gates) respects the physical constraints of serverless compute without sacrificing query ergonomics.

#### 2. The Punctured Overclaims (The Explicit Pushback)

* **The "Subtext Extraction = Masterclass Writing" Fallacy:** Injecting three extracted secrets and an interpersonal lien into a prompt does not mechanically produce Cormac McCarthy or David Wire. LLMs frequently take hyper-specific prompt instructions and turn them into blunt, on-the-nose conversational exposition within 200 tokens. Contextual specificity is a *necessary* condition for grounded dialogue, but it is not a *sufficient* condition for dramatic tension. Calling this an "instant jump to prestige cinema" was unearned certainty.
* **Architecture Sizing vs. Actual Production Reality:** The sudden jump to "60+ characters with L4-L5 vertebral compressions" risked building enterprise architectural scaffolding around what might only need to be a tight 4-to-8 character pilot ensemble. The architecture must scale to the actual production volume, not an imagined hyper-dense theoretical stress-test.
* **The Leaky Regex Linter:** The string-matching regex (`/(\bhe|\bshe|\bOctavius)\s+([a-z\s]{0,15})\bsprint\b/`) is functionally broken in real-world screenplay parsing. It completely misses semantic equivalents (*"broke into a run"*, *"surged forward"*, *"accelerated past the gate"*) and collapses under basic multi-character pronoun ambiguity.
* **The Inverted Build Order:** Building a full Neo4j cluster and authoring pipeline (Steps 1–2) before proving that subtext injection even improves 14B/32B dialogue output (Step 3) inverted the **Walking Skeleton** discipline. It repeated the exact error previously avoided with the GPU greenscreen test: building massive infrastructure before falsifying the core hypothesis.

### Addition 1: The Subtext Falsification Pilot (Run This Before Building Neo4j)

Do not deploy Neo4j, write Cypher queries, or build graph compilers yet. Run a single-day, zero-infrastructure test to validate the core creative premise: **Does structured subtext injection actually prevent generic dialogue regression?**

#### The Protocol:

1. **Select Two Core Characters:** Take two established figures with known friction (e.g., *Billy Fae Booth* and *The Pilot*).
2. **Generate Variant A (Baseline / Unstructured Prompt):**
* *Input:* Standard scene premise + character bios + tone parameters (*"Write a tense scene where Billy Fae confronts The Pilot over illegal fuel siphoning on the edge of the swamp."*).


3. **Generate Variant B (Structured Invariant & Subtext Injection):**
* *Input:* Same premise, but injected with a hand-written simulation of what Neo4j would return:
* `somatic_limit`: The Pilot's Raynaud's syndrome / right-hand tremor.
* `held_leverage`: Billy Fae holds his father's uncollectible salvage ledger.
* `epistemic_asymmetry`: The Pilot knows the fuel contains toxic solvent; Billy Fae believes it is clean red diesel.
* `negative_rule`: Neither character may explicitly say "ledger", "solvent", or "father".




4. **Run Blind Qualitative Evaluation:**
* Strip prompt tags. Present 5 anonymous paired takes of Variant A vs. Variant B to an independent reader or run an objective blind evaluation focusing purely on:
* Did the characters speak in clichés?
* Did they immediately confess their internal goals?
* Did the scene feel physically grounded in bodily friction?




5. **The Falsification Gate:** If Variant B does not demonstrate a marked, unmistakable reduction in cliché regression, **kill the Neo4j subtext engine entirely.** Fall back to a lightweight relational D1 schema and focus compute spend on actor LoRAs and audio timing.

### Addition 2: The Structured Action AST (Fixing the Regex Fragility)

Regex parsing freeform screenplay prose for physical constraints is fundamentally broken. To enforce somatic invariants deterministically without an LLM judge, **force the generating model to categorize its own physical blocking into discrete, typed action tokens.**

When Child Graph A generates the screenplay, the JSON schema requires a parallel array of discrete kinetic verbs alongside the prose:

#### The Corrected Shot Schema:

```json
{
  "shot_id": "sh_03",
  "character_id": "char_008_octavius",
  "screenplay_action": "Octavius lunges forward, seizing the iron lever with both hands.",
  "extracted_motor_actions": ["LUNGE", "GRASP_TWO_HANDED", "WEIGHT_BEAR_UPRIGHT"],
  "dialogue_text": "The pressure seals are blowing."
}

```

#### The Deterministic Set-Intersection Linter:

Now the linter in your execution runtime requires zero fragile regex, zero string manipulation, and zero pronoun resolution. It is a strict mathematical set intersection:

```typescript
// src/services/invariantLinter.ts
import { SomaticVector } from '../types/canonState';

export interface ASTShot {
  character_id: string;
  screenplay_action: string;
  extracted_motor_actions: string[];
  dialogue_text: string;
}

export function lintSceneAST(
  shots: ASTShot[],
  somaticProfiles: Record<string, SomaticVector>
): { passed: boolean; violations: string[] } {
  const violations: string[] = [];

  for (const shot of shots) {
    const profile = somaticProfiles[shot.character_id];
    if (!profile) continue;

    // Direct Set Intersection: O(1) comparison between requested actions and banned tags
    const illegalActions = shot.extracted_motor_actions.filter((action) =>
      profile.banned_kinetic_verbs.includes(action)
    );

    if (illegalActions.length > 0) {
      violations.push(
        `[INVARIANT VIOLATION] Character '${shot.character_id}' executed prohibited motor actions [${illegalActions.join(
          ', '
        )}] in shot '${shot.screenplay_action}' under somatic baseline '${profile.locomotion_baseline}'.`
      );
    }
  }

  return {
    passed: violations.length === 0,
    violations
  };
}

```

*Why this is superior:* If the LLM generates prose saying *"Octavius took off like a shot"*, it must declare `extracted_motor_actions: ["SPRINT"]`. If it claims `[]`, the linter fails on empty classification. If it admits `"SPRINT"`, the set intersection instantly catches it.

### Addition 4: The Dialogue Attenuation Heuristic (Enforcing Subtext Negatively)

When you tell an LLM: *"Character A knows Secret X (toxic dump). Character A has leverage over Character B,"* the model’s default statistical behavior is to have Character A immediately say: *"I know about the toxic dump, and that means I own you!"*

To turn informational leverage into authentic dramatic subtext, the compiler must inject an **Attenuation Negative Fence**:

```text
SUBTEXT COMPILATION DIRECTIVE:
1. FACTUAL LEVERAGE: You hold the unrecorded railway deed against Iona.
2. ATTENUATION FILTER (BANNED TOKENS): 
   Under no circumstances may your dialogue include the words: ["deed", "foreclosure", "railway", "bank", "own", "leverage"].
3. TACTICAL DISPLACEMENT: 
   You must negotiate the surrender of this asset exclusively through the discussion of: ["diesel fuel prices", "the morning rain", "drainage ditch gravel"].

```

This transforms the state machine from an informational data dump into a **dramatic compressor**. The LLM is forced to channel the pressure of the hidden state through mundane physical objects, creating the evasive cadence native to rural noir.

```
         │ (Generate screenplay + AST shots; enforce zero-cliché negative fences)
                 │
                 ▼
[ Step 4: Remotion Audio Animatic (Radio Play Lock) ]
                 │
                 ▼
[ Step 5: RunPod Headless Greenscreen Diffusion (GPU Cost Proof) ]
                 │
                 ▼
[ Step 6: Scale State Machine (D1 or Neo4j based on Tier Throttle) ]

```

This preserves the brilliance of your state machine concepts while ruthlessly excising the unearned creative assumptions, securing the codebase against regex failure, and grounding your build order in empirical proof.Here is the synthesis of your rigorous breakdown, confirming the boundaries of what is mechanically true versus what was creatively overclaimed, followed by four structural additions that push this engineering logic to its natural conclusion.

### 1. The Generalization of Typed State Vectors

**What is understood:** Moving from flat `fact_key/fact_value` strings to typed State Vectors (Somatic, Logistical, Epistemic) fundamentally changes the system from a *reactive monitor* to a *preventive compiler*. Flat prose facts only allow a system to throw a "dirty" flag *after* an edit. Typed vectors (enums, bounding limits, booleans) allow the system to mathematically reject impossible actions *before* they are written. Furthermore, typed vectors allow for category-specific validation (physical limits require different math than inventory limits), stripping the LLM of any need to "interpret" a constraint. The version-pinning blast radius remains the same, but the fidelity of the enforcement is vastly upgraded.

**Worthy Addition: State Decay and "Half-Lives"**
If state is typed and numerical, it shouldn't just toggle; it should degrade.

* **The Addition:** Logistical and Somatic vectors should support temporal decay matrices. If a vehicle holds 120 liters of fuel, the AST compilation of a "high-speed pursuit" scene doesn't just check if fuel $> 0$; it automatically debits the fuel integer based on the scene's calculated duration. If a character suffers a concussion, the debuff has a `scene_half_life`. The state machine doesn't just enforce rules; it automatically calculates the thermodynamic cost of narrative actions, tracking attrition seamlessly across a 10-episode arc without the human writer doing the math.

### 2. Hardening the Linter (Killing the Regex)

**What is understood:** Parsing free-prose screenplay text with regex to catch banned kinetic actions is fundamentally flawed. It collapses under synonyms, paraphrasing, and pronoun ambiguity. The true fix is moving the validation out of natural language entirely: the LLM must be constrained to output a structured AST field (`action_taken: ["LUNGE", "GRAB"]`) chosen from a strict enum list, alongside the prose. The linter then performs a simple $O(1)$ set-intersection against the character's banned tags. If structured output isn't possible, a dedicated LLM extraction pass must precede the linter.

**Worthy Addition: The "Cost of Doing Business" Ledger**
If the LLM is forced to output structured `action_taken` enums, the linter shouldn't just return `PASS` or `FAIL`. It should return a physical cost.

* **The Addition:** If Octavius (suffering from severe neuropathy) attempts an action tagged `[HEAVY_LIFT]`, and his Somatic vector permits it but flags it as `HIGH_FRICTION`, the linter passes the action but automatically injects a "Pain Response" constraint into the prompt for the *subsequent* shot. The AST transforms physical actions into cascading physical consequences, forcing the LLM to write the immediate exhaustion that follows the exertion.

### 3. The Myth of "Mechanically Produced Good Prose"

**What is understood:** Specific, concrete constraints produce better, less generic LLM prose than vague prompts. This is a validated, empirical fact. However, claiming that a graph database *mechanically guarantees* "prestige cinema" dialogue conflates the *delivery mechanism* (Neo4j) with the *active ingredient* (specific constraints). There is zero evidence that a Neo4j Cypher query produces better dialogue than a human showrunner manually typing those exact same constraints into the prompt.

**Worthy Addition: The "Hallucinated Compliance" Metric**
When evaluating prompt constraints, LLMs suffer from sycophancy—if you tell the model "Character A holds a secret deed over Character B," the LLM's statistical instinct is to have Character A say, *"I hold the secret deed over you!"*

* **The Addition:** The true measure of a subtext-injection system isn't just whether the dialogue sounds cool; it's whether the system successfully forces the LLM to *obfuscate* the injected constraints. Any architecture built around subtext must include a negative-constraint wrapper (the "Attenuation Heuristic" mentioned previously) that explicitly bans the literal vocabulary of the secret from the generated prose, forcing the model to negotiate the tension through physical blocking and mundane topics.

### 4 & 5. The Falsification Pilot & Acceptance Criteria for Neo4j

**What is understood:** The entire Neo4j infrastructure bet must be paused and submitted to a blind, multi-variant test. The test must separate the variables: (1) Generic Prompt, (2) Human-Written Specific Constraints, (3) Graph-Extracted Specific Constraints. The acceptance criteria must be set *before* the test. Neo4j is only justified if (3) consistently beats (2) in blind editorial judgment, OR if (3) reliably surfaces critical leverage/secrets that the human in condition (2) simply forgot to include because the 60+ character web exceeded human working memory.

**Worthy Addition: Testing for "N-Degree Triangulation"**
If Neo4j's justification rests on "catching what the human forgets," the pilot test must explicitly measure its ability to surface transitive, multi-hop leverage.

* **The Addition:** When designing the test setups, intentionally choose scenes where the leverage is indirect (e.g., $A \rightarrow B \rightarrow C \rightarrow A$).
* *Billy Fae* wants to crush *The Pilot*.
* *The Pilot* relies on fuel from *Zap Applebrooke*.
* *Zap* owes back-taxes to *Billy Fae*.
If the Neo4j Cypher query successfully surfaces Zap's tax debt as Billy Fae's optimal weapon against The Pilot—and injects that into the scene prompt, creating a dynamic the human writer missed—then the graph database has proved its enterprise value. If it only returns 1-to-1 relationships that the writer already knew, Neo4j is over-engineered overhead, and a simple D1 relational table is the correct tool for the job.



### The Bottom Line

You have successfully stripped the magical thinking away from the architecture. The system we are looking at now is a hard, empirical compiler for fiction. It treats story logic as executable code, physical limitations as mathematical constraints, and infrastructure upgrades (like Neo4j) as hypotheses requiring blind, A/B falsification before a single dollar is spent on deployment.In this architecture, **`lintSceneAgainstCanon` acts as a deterministic compilation gatekeeper.**

It is called at three specific lifecycle gates—most critically, **the exact millisecond Child Graph A finishes generating a candidate script, before a single byte of audio or video is synthesized.**

---

### The Three Execution Windows ("When")

```
                                  LIFECYCLE GATES
                                  
  [ Gate 1: The Fast Automated Loop ]
  Child Graph A (LLM) ──► Candidate AST ──► [ lintSceneAgainstCanon ]
                                                   │
                            ┌──────────────────────┴─────────────────────┐
                            ▼ FAIL                                       ▼ PASS
                    Self-Healing Loop                           Child Graph B (TTS)
                    (Pass violations back to LLM)               & Remotion Animatic
                                                                         │
  [ Gate 2: The Human Edit / Save Gate ]                                 ▼
  Showrunner hand-edits Fountain/Markdown ──► [ lintSceneAgainstCanon ] ──► Director Sign-Off
                                                                         │
  [ Gate 3: Upstream Mutation Audit ]                                    ▼
  Upstream Fact changes in D1/Ledger ───────► [ lintSceneAgainstCanon ] ──► GPU Dispatch Gate

```

#### Gate 1: The Automated Post-Generation Gate (The Primary Hot Path)

* **When:** Immediately after local inference (Qwen 2.5 in Child Graph A) outputs the candidate `dialogue_ast.json`.
* **Why:** Text-to-speech generation (Child Graph B) and Remotion composition consume CPU/GPU cycles and wall-clock time. You never run TTS on a script that contains physically or epistemically illegal actions. If the linter fails here, the execution broker halts the pipeline immediately or triggers an automatic re-prompt loop.

#### Gate 2: The Human-in-the-Loop Edit Gate (The Quarantine Pass)

* **When:** When the showrunner opens a scene file in Astro or their Markdown editor, alters dialogue or action beats by hand, and hits **Save** (or runs a local CLI commit).
* **Why:** Human writers forget their own lore rules just as easily as LLMs do. Running the linter on save catches whether an author accidentally wrote a line where an injured character vaults a fence or reveals a secret prematurely.

#### Gate 3: The Pre-Dispatch Audit Gate (Before Cloud GPUs Spin Up)

* **When:** Right when the director clicks **"Authorize Cloud Video Batch"** in the Astro UI, before the Cloudflare Worker calls RunPod.
* **Why:** If an upstream fact was edited in Episode 1 while Episode 3 was sitting in the review queue, this final gate verifies that the scene’s pinned snapshot hash still matches the active world state.

### How It Is Called and Accessed ("How")

The linter is a pure, side-effect-free TypeScript function. It is accessed through three distinct entry points depending on who or what is triggering the run:

---

### 1. In-Process: Inside the Local Pipeline Orchestrator (Automated Self-Healing Loop)

This is the primary automated consumer (inside your Node.js pipeline runner or `worker-sower` execution script). It runs the linter in an automated retry loop:

```typescript
// scripts/run_local_modular_pipeline.ts (or src/services/pipeline.ts)
import { lintSceneAST } from './services/invariantLinter.js';
import type { SomaticVector, LogisticalVector, EpistemicVector } from '@snailicid3/consumer-npm';
import { runChildGraphA, runChildGraphB } from './comfyBroker.js';

export async function generateValidatedScene(sceneId: string, maxRetries = 2) {
  // 1. Load active canon state from compiled/bible-state.json (or local D1 cache)
  const canonState = await loadActiveCanonSnapshot(sceneId);

  let attempts = 0;
  let candidateAST = null;
  let linterReport = { passed: false, violations: [] };

  while (attempts <= maxRetries && !linterReport.passed) {
    attempts++;
    console.log(`[Pipeline] Generating Script AST via Child Graph A (Attempt ${attempts})...`);

    // Run ComfyUI / Local LLM
    candidateAST = await runChildGraphA({
      scene_id: sceneId,
      somatic_context: canonState.somatic,
      epistemic_context: canonState.epistemic,
      // If retrying, inject previous violations as hard negative constraints:
      repair_instructions: linterReport.violations.length > 0
        ? `REPAIR MANDATE: Your previous draft failed validation:\n${linterReport.violations.join('\n')}`
        : undefined
    });

    // 2. THE LINTER RUNS HERE: Deterministic O(1) Set Intersection
    linterReport = lintSceneAST(candidateAST.shots, canonState.somatic);

    if (!linterReport.passed) {
      console.warn(`[Linter Rejected Take ${attempts}]:`, linterReport.violations);
    }
  }

  // 3. Hard Halt Gate
  if (!linterReport.passed) {
    throw new Error(`[Pipeline Halting] Scene '${sceneId}' failed canon validation after ${attempts} attempts.`);
  }

  console.log(`[Pipeline Approved] Script passed all invariants. Flushing text VRAM...`);
  await flushComfyUIMemory();

  // 4. Safe to proceed to Child Graph B (Audio Stems) & Remotion Animatic
  console.log(`[Pipeline] Dispatching Audio Synthesis (Child Graph B)...`);
  const timingManifest = await runChildGraphB(candidateAST);
  return timingManifest;
}

```

---

### 2. HTTP Endpoint: Inside the Astro Production UI (Real-Time Visual Redlines)

When an author is working inside the Astro frontend (Step 5), the editor shouldn't wait for a terminal run. As the author edits the action lines or tweaks sliders, Astro hits an API route that runs the linter and returns instant visual feedback:

```typescript
// src/pages/api/scenes/[id]/lint.ts (Astro SSR API Route)
import type { APIRoute } from 'astro';
import { lintSceneAST } from '../../../../services/invariantLinter';

export const POST: APIRoute = async ({ params, request, locals }) => {
  const { id: sceneId } = params;
  const { shots } = await request.json(); // Candidate AST shots from the browser UI

  // Pull latest somatic and logistical profiles from D1/Neo4j cache
  const db = locals.runtime.env.CANON_DB;
  const somaticProfiles = await fetchActiveSomaticProfiles(db, sceneId);

  // Run the pure linter
  const report = lintSceneAST(shots, somaticProfiles);

  return new Response(JSON.stringify({
    scene_id: sceneId,
    timestamp: Date.now(),
    is_valid: report.passed,
    violations: report.violations // Rendered as red banners directly above the shot in the UI
  }), {
    status: report.passed ? 200 : 422, // 422 Unprocessable Entity if invariants fail
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }
  });
};

```

In the UI (`DirectorConsole.tsx`), if `is_valid === false`, the **"Authorize Cloud Video Batch"** button is physically disabled, displaying the exact violation:

> 🔴 **OCTAVIUS (008): Motor Invariant Breach.** *Prohibited action `[SPRINT]` attempted under condition `[severe_neuropathy]`.*

### The Master Pipeline File (`src/pipeline/produceEpisode.ts`)

```typescript
import path from 'node:path';
import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import { z } from 'zod';

// Types imported from canonical packages
import type {
  CanonStateSnapshot,
  SomaticVector,
  LogisticalVector,
  EpistemicVector,
  CanonStateDelta
} from '@snailicid3/consumer-npm';

import type { SceneManifest, ShotTiming } from '../types/radioPlay';
import type { DispatchShotPayload, RunPodJobResult } from '../types/orchestrator';

// ============================================================================
// 1. DATA CONTRACTS FOR PIPELINE CHAIN
// ============================================================================

export interface SceneInputDirective {
  scene_id: string;
  episode_id: string;
  slugline: string;
  premise: string;
  participant_ids: string[];
  tone_parameters: {
    curtness: number;           // 0.0 to 1.0
    pacing: number;             // 0.0 to 1.0
    threat_level: number;       // 0.0 to 1.0
    subtext_suppression: number; // 0.0 to 1.0
  };
}

export interface ScriptGenerationOutput {
  scene_id: string;
  fountain_script: string;
  shots: Array<{
    shot_id: string;
    character_id: string;
    dialogue_text: string;
    parenthetical?: string;
    emotion: string;
    camera_intent: string;
    action_context: string;
    extracted_motor_actions: string[]; // Discrete tokens: ['LUNGE', 'DRAW_WEAPON']
    foley_cues: string[];
  }>;
}

export interface RenderedPlateAsset {
  shot_id: string;
  remote_mp4_url: string;
  frames_rendered: number;
  seed_used: number;
}

// ============================================================================
// 2. THE EXECUTABLE FUNCTION CHAIN
// ============================================================================

/**
 * STEP 1: Compile Corpus & Load Canonical State
 * Executes the two-pass compiler in @snailicid3/consumer-npm to produce
 * the deterministic, byte-identical bible-state.json.
 */
export async function compileCorpusAndLoadCanon(): Promise<CanonStateSnapshot> {
  console.log('[Step 1] Compiling corpus Markdown and asserting relational integrity...');
  
  // Triggers npm run compile in the lore package
  const bibleStatePath = path.resolve(process.cwd(), '../goblin-lore/compiled/bible-state.json');
  const rawState = await fs.readFile(bibleStatePath, 'utf-8');
  const bibleState = JSON.parse(rawState);

  return {
    snapshot_id: bibleState.meta.snapshot_id,
    scene_id: 'GLOBAL_BOOT',
    timestamp_tick: bibleState.meta.tick,
    somatic_states: bibleState.characters,
    logistical_states: bibleState.possessions,
    epistemic_states: bibleState.grievances,
    hash: bibleState.meta.sha256
  };
}

/**
 * STEP 2: Build Scene Preconditions & Subtext Directives
 * Traverses relational data (Neo4j / D1) to calculate interpersonal leverage,
 * asymmetric knowledge, active motor restrictions, and banned keywords.
 */
export async function buildScenePreconditions(
  directive: SceneInputDirective,
  canonSnapshot: CanonStateSnapshot
): Promise<{
  activeSomatic: Record<string, SomaticVector>;
  activeLogistics: Record<string, LogisticalVector>;
  activeEpistemic: Record<string, EpistemicVector>;
  bannedTokens: string[];
  promptPayload: string;
}> {
  console.log(`[Step 2] Building preconditions for scene: ${directive.scene_id}`);

  const activeSomatic: Record<string, SomaticVector> = {};
  const activeLogistics: Record<string, LogisticalVector> = {};
  const activeEpistemic: Record<string, EpistemicVector> = {};
  const bannedTokens: string[] = [];

  for (const charId of directive.participant_ids) {
    activeSomatic[charId] = canonSnapshot.somatic_states[charId];
    activeLogistics[charId] = canonSnapshot.logistical_states[charId];
    activeEpistemic[charId] = canonSnapshot.epistemic_states[charId];

    // Attenuation Heuristic: Ban literal tokens of hidden secrets
    if (activeEpistemic[charId]?.escalation_ceiling) {
      bannedTokens.push(...activeEpistemic[charId].escalation_ceiling.split(/\s+/));
    }
  }

  // Build high-pressure prompt payload for Child Graph A
  const promptPayload = JSON.stringify({
    premise: directive.premise,
    tone: directive.tone_parameters,
    somatic_fences: activeSomatic,
    attenuation_banned_tokens: [...new Set(bannedTokens)]
  });

  return { activeSomatic, activeLogistics, activeEpistemic, bannedTokens, promptPayload };
}

/**
 * STEP 3: Synthesize Script & Structured Action AST
 * Executes Child Graph A (local LLM via ComfyUI / Ollama).
 * Emits the dual-artifact: Fountain prose + machine-readable JSON AST with discrete motor actions.
 */
export async function synthesizeScriptAndActionAST(
  directive: SceneInputDirective,
  compiledContext: string
): Promise<ScriptGenerationOutput> {
  console.log(`[Step 3] Running Child Graph A local inference (Qwen 2.5)...`);

  const comfyResponse = await fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8188/prompt', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      prompt: {
        /* Injected workflow JSON for Child Graph A */
        context_input: compiledContext
      }
    })
  });

  if (!comfyResponse.ok) throw new Error('ComfyUI Graph A dispatch failed');
  const { prompt_id } = await comfyResponse.json();

  // Poll for completion and read AST artifact
  const rawResult = await pollLocalComfyResult(prompt_id);
  return rawResult as ScriptGenerationOutput;
}

/**
 * STEP 4: Deterministic Invariant Linter
 * Validates the candidate script against physical constraints via O(1) set-intersection.
 * Bypasses regex and eliminates LLM judgment calls.
 */
export function lintSceneAgainstCanon(
  scriptOutput: ScriptGenerationOutput,
  somaticProfiles: Record<string, SomaticVector>,
  logisticalProfiles: Record<string, LogisticalVector>,
  epistemicProfiles: Record<string, EpistemicVector>
): { passed: boolean; violations: string[] } {
  console.log(`[Step 4] Linting candidate AST against physical and epistemic invariants...`);
  const violations: string[] = [];

  for (const shot of scriptOutput.shots) {
    const somatic = somaticProfiles[shot.character_id];
    if (somatic) {
      // Direct Set Intersection of requested motor verbs vs banned kinetic verbs
      const illegalVerbs = shot.extracted_motor_actions.filter(verb =>
        somatic.banned_kinetic_verbs.includes(verb)
      );

      if (illegalVerbs.length > 0) {
        violations.push(
          `[SOMATIC BREACH] Character ${shot.character_id} executed prohibited actions [${illegalVerbs.join(
            ', '
          )}] in shot ${shot.shot_id} under baseline ${somatic.locomotion_baseline}`
        );
      }
    }

    const epistemic = epistemicProfiles[shot.character_id];
    if (epistemic?.escalation_ceiling) {
      // Check for escalation tripwire leaks
      const keywords = epistemic.escalation_ceiling.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).filter(w => w.length > 4);
      const dialogueLower = shot.dialogue_text.toLowerCase();
      const tripped = keywords.find(k => dialogueLower.includes(k));
      if (tripped) {
        violations.push(
          `[EPISTEMIC TRIPWIRE] Shot ${shot.shot_id} leaked secret keyword '${tripped}' violating ceiling.`
        );
      }
    }
  }

  return { passed: violations.length === 0, violations };
}

/**
 * STEP 5: Synthesize Audio & Quantize Frame Timing
 * Flushes text models from VRAM, executes Child Graph B (TTS via Parler-TTS/CosyVoice),
 * measures exact millisecond audio durations via ffprobe, and locks timeline frames.
 */
export async function synthesizeAudioAndQuantizeTiming(
  scriptOutput: ScriptGenerationOutput,
  fps = 24
): Promise<SceneManifest> {
  console.log(`[Step 5] Synthesizing audio stems and calculating exact frame quantization...`);

  // 1. Flush Text LLM from VRAM to clear memory for audio
  await fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8188/free', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ unload_models: true, free_memory: true })
  });

  // 2. Run Child Graph B (TTS Generation)
  const resolvedShots: ShotTiming[] = [];
  let timelineFrameCursor = 0;

  for (const shot of scriptOutput.shots) {
    const audioFilename = `${shot.shot_id}_stem.wav`;
    
    // Call local TTS microservice
    const durationSeconds = await callLocalTTSService({
      character_id: shot.character_id,
      text: shot.dialogue_text,
      emotion: shot.emotion,
      out_path: `public/audio/dialogue/${audioFilename}`
    });

    // Pacing Math: Quantize continuous audio to discrete integer video frames
    const preRoll = 8; // 333ms breath/head-turn padding
    const rawAudioFrames = Math.ceil(durationSeconds * fps);
    const postRoll = 16; // 666ms reaction/energy-decay padding
    const totalShotFrames = preRoll + rawAudioFrames + postRoll;

    resolvedShots.push({
      ...shot,
      audio_filename: audioFilename,
      audio_duration_seconds: durationSeconds,
      pre_roll_frames: preRoll,
      post_roll_frames: postRoll,
      calculated_frames: totalShotFrames,
      start_frame: timelineFrameCursor
    });

    timelineFrameCursor += totalShotFrames;
  }

  return {
    scene_id: scriptOutput.scene_id,
    scene_heading: 'EXT. SECTOR 4 DOCKS - NIGHT',
    ambient_bed: 'ambient_industrial_rain_loop.wav',
    ambient_volume_base: 0.4,
    ambient_volume_ducked: 0.08,
    fps,
    shots: resolvedShots
  };
}

/**
 * STEP 6: Build Radio Play Animatic
 * Programmatically renders a diagnostic exposure sheet animatic MP4 using Remotion.
 * Mixes multi-track audio (dialogue stems + spot foley + sidechain ducked ambient bed).
 */
export async function buildRadioPlayAnimatic(manifest: SceneManifest): Promise<string> {
  console.log(`[Step 6] Compiling headless Remotion animatic for pacing review...`);

  const animaticPath = path.resolve(process.cwd(), `outputs/animatics/${manifest.scene_id}_radio_play.mp4`);
  
  // Calls @remotion/renderer to bundle and render composition headlessly
  await executeHeadlessRemotionRender({
    compositionId: 'RadioPlayMaster',
    inputProps: { manifest, totalDurationInFrames: manifest.shots.reduce((a, s) => a + (s.calculated_frames ?? 0), 0) },
    outputPath: animaticPath
  });

  return animaticPath;
}

/**
 * STEP 7: Await Director Sign-Off (Human Gate)
 * Suspends execution until the human director reviews the lightweight animatic
 * in the Astro UI and clicks "Authorize Cloud Video Batch".
 */
export async function awaitDirectorSignOff(sceneId: string, animaticUrl: string): Promise<boolean> {
  console.log(`[Step 7] ANIMATIC READY: ${animaticUrl}`);
  console.log(`[Step 7] Execution suspended at Gateway 3. Awaiting director sign-off in Astro UI...`);

  // In production, this awaits a webhook or database record update from the UI
  return await pollAstroApprovalStatus(sceneId);
}

/**
 * STEP 8: Dispatch Serverless Greenscreen Plates
 * Dispatches frame-locked visual prompt payloads to the Cloudflare Durable Object (ShotCoordinator).
 * The actor manages idempotency, retry budgets, and runs ComfyUI Child Graph C on RunPod.
 */
export async function dispatchServerlessGreenscreenPlates(
  manifest: SceneManifest,
  edgeGatewayUrl: string
): Promise<RenderedPlateAsset[]> {
  console.log(`[Step 8] Gating cleared. Dispatching ${manifest.shots.length} shots to RunPod...`);

  const renderPromises = manifest.shots.map(async (shot) => {
    const payload: DispatchShotPayload = {
      scene_id: manifest.scene_id,
      shot_id: shot.shot_id,
      target_frames: shot.calculated_frames!,
      visual_prompt: `${shot.action_context}, camera ${shot.camera_intent}`,
      character_lora: `visual_${shot.character_id}.safetensors`,
      idempotency_key: `${shot.shot_id}_${shot.calculated_frames}_v1`,
      is_inpaint: false
    };

    // Workers RPC call hitting ShotCoordinator Actor
    const res = await fetch(`${edgeGatewayUrl}/api/shots/dispatch`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify(payload)
    });

    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Orchestrator dispatch failed for shot ${shot.shot_id}`);
    const result: RunPodJobResult = await res.json();
    
    return {
      shot_id: shot.shot_id,
      remote_mp4_url: result.output!.asset_url,
      frames_rendered: result.output!.frames_rendered,
      seed_used: result.output!.seed_used
    };
  });

  return Promise.all(renderPromises);
}

/**
 * STEP 9: Composite Final Master Episode
 * Takes the raw greenscreen plates from R2 and executes the final Remotion master composition.
 * Composites characters over hand-crafted backgrounds, applies color grades, and welds audio.
 */
export async function compositeFinalMasterEpisode(
  manifest: SceneManifest,
  plates: RenderedPlateAsset[]
): Promise<string> {
  console.log(`[Step 9] Compositing final master visual plates in Remotion...`);

  const masterOutputPath = path.resolve(process.cwd(), `outputs/masters/${manifest.scene_id}_master.mp4`);

  await executeHeadlessRemotionRender({
    compositionId: 'FinalCompositeMaster',
    inputProps: {
      manifest,
      plates, // Remotion keys out #00FF00 and layers over background matte art
      colorGradePreset: 'biopunk_noir_high_contrast'
    },
    outputPath: masterOutputPath
  });

  return masterOutputPath;
}

/**
 * STEP 10: Commit Canon State Delta & Blast-Radius Propagation
 * Calculates state mutations resulting from the scene (fuel spent, wounds taken, secrets revealed).
 * Writes the immutable delta to Cloudflare D1 and updates dirty-state flags for downstream scenes.
 */
export async function commitCanonStateDelta(
  sceneId: string,
  parentStateHash: string,
  mutations: {
    somatic: any[];
    logistical: any[];
    epistemic: any[];
  },
  dbGatewayUrl: string
): Promise<string> {
  console.log(`[Step 10] Committing state delta (Sn -> Sn+1) to Cloudflare D1 ledger...`);

  const deltaPayload: CanonStateDelta = {
    delta_id: crypto.randomUUID(),
    scene_id: sceneId,
    parent_hash: parentStateHash,
    resulting_hash: '', // Computed server-side after atomic SQL transaction
    somatic_mutations: mutations.somatic,
    logistical_mutations: mutations.logistical,
    epistemic_mutations: mutations.epistemic
  };

  const res = await fetch(`${dbGatewayUrl}/api/canon/commit-delta`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(deltaPayload)
  });

  const { new_state_hash, invalidated_downstream_scenes } = await res.json();
  
  if (invalidated_downstream_scenes.length > 0) {
    console.warn(`[Step 10] BLAST RADIUS ALERT: ${invalidated_downstream_scenes.length} downstream scenes marked DIRTY.`);
  }

  return new_state_hash;
}

/**
 * STEP 11: Sync Artifacts to Gemini Notebook Knowledge Base
 * Automatically pushes the locked .fountain script and state delta JSON back into
 * the Gemini Notebook series bible as Markdown sources.
 */
export async function syncToNotebookKnowledgeBase(
  sceneId: string,
  fountainScript: string,
  stateHash: string,
  notebookId: string
): Promise<void> {
  console.log(`[Step 11] Pushing final script and state snapshot to Gemini Notebook [${notebookId}]...`);

  const sourceTitle = `Finished Scene Script: ${sceneId} (State: ${stateHash.slice(0, 8)})`;
  const markdownContent = `
# CANONICAL SCRIPT DELIVERABLE // ${sceneId.toUpperCase()}
*Authoritative State Hash: \`${stateHash}\`*

${fountainScript}
  `.trim();

  // Calls Google NotebookLM / Gemini Notebook source creation endpoint
  await callNotebookCreateSource({
    notebookName: `notebooks/${notebookId}`,
    displayName: sourceTitle,
    textContent: markdownContent
  });

  console.log(`[Step 11] Knowledge base synchronized. Season memory updated.`);
}

// ============================================================================
// 3. MASTER ORCHESTRATOR LOOP
// ============================================================================

export async function executeProductionPipeline(
  sceneDirective: SceneInputDirective,
  config: {
    edgeGatewayUrl: string;
    notebookId: string;
  }
) {
  const startTime = Date.now();
  console.log(`\n=======================================================`);
  console.log(`STARTING AUTOMATED PRODUCTION: ${sceneDirective.scene_id}`);
  console.log(`=======================================================\n`);

  // Step 1: Compile Corpus & Load Canon
  const canonSnapshot = await compileCorpusAndLoadCanon();

  // Step 2: Build Preconditions & Subtext Fences
  const preconditions = await buildScenePreconditions(sceneDirective, canonSnapshot);

  // Step 3 & 4: Script Synthesis with Self-Healing Invariant Linter Loop
  let scriptOutput: ScriptGenerationOutput;
  let attempts = 0;
  const MAX_SCRIPT_RETRIES = 2;

  while (true) {
    attempts++;
    scriptOutput = await synthesizeScriptAndActionAST(sceneDirective, preconditions.promptPayload);

    // Step 4: Deterministic Invariant Linting
    const lintReport = lintSceneAgainstCanon(
      scriptOutput,
      preconditions.activeSomatic,
      preconditions.activeLogistics,
      preconditions.activeEpistemic
    );

    if (lintReport.passed) {
      console.log(`[Step 4] Script AST passed all invariant checks on take ${attempts}.`);
      break;
    }

    console.warn(`[Step 4] Invariant violations detected on take ${attempts}:`, lintReport.violations);
    if (attempts > MAX_SCRIPT_RETRIES) {
      throw new Error(`Execution halted: Scene failed invariant linter after ${attempts} attempts.`);
    }

    // Append violations as negative instructions for the next loop iteration
    preconditions.promptPayload = JSON.stringify({
      ...JSON.parse(preconditions.promptPayload),
      repair_mandate: lintReport.violations
    });
  }

  // Step 5: Synthesize Audio & Quantize Timing
  const timingManifest = await synthesizeAudioAndQuantizeTiming(scriptOutput);

  // Step 6: Build Radio Play Animatic
  const animaticPath = await buildRadioPlayAnimatic(timingManifest);

  // Step 7: Await Human Director Sign-Off (The Human Gate)
  const isApproved = await awaitDirectorSignOff(sceneDirective.scene_id, animaticPath);
  if (!isApproved) {
    console.warn(`[Pipeline] Scene ${sceneDirective.scene_id} rejected by director. Compute aborted.`);
    return { status: 'REJECTED_BY_DIRECTOR' };
  }

  // Step 8: Dispatch Serverless Greenscreen Plates (Cloud Compute)
  const renderedPlates = await dispatchServerlessGreenscreenPlates(timingManifest, config.edgeGatewayUrl);

  // Step 9: Composite Final Master Episode
  const masterEpisodePath = await compositeFinalMasterEpisode(timingManifest, renderedPlates);

  // Step 10: Commit Canon State Delta to Edge Database
  const newStateHash = await commitCanonStateDelta(
    sceneDirective.scene_id,
    canonSnapshot.hash,
    {
      somatic: [{ entity_id: 'char_008_octavius', action: 'UPDATE_SEVERITY', payload: { fatigue: '+0.15' } }],
      logistical: [{ entity_id: 'vehicle_pilot_sled', action: 'EXPEND_RESOURCE', payload: { fuel_liters: '-8.5' } }],
      epistemic: []
    },
    config.edgeGatewayUrl
  );

  // Step 11: Sync Deliverable Back to Gemini Notebook
  await syncToNotebookKnowledgeBase(
    sceneDirective.scene_id,
    scriptOutput.fountain_script,
    newStateHash,
    config.notebookId
  );

  const durationSec = ((Date.now() - startTime) / 1000).toFixed(2);
  console.log(`\n=======================================================`);
  console.log(`PIPELINE COMPLETE: ${sceneDirective.scene_id} in ${durationSec}s`);
  console.log(`FINAL DELIVERABLE: ${masterEpisodePath}`);
  console.log(`=======================================================\n`);

  return {
    status: 'COMPLETED',
    scene_id: sceneDirective.scene_id,
    master_asset: masterEpisodePath,
    new_canon_hash: newStateHash
  };
}

// ============================================================================
// 4. MOCK STUBS (Internal I/O Helper Implementations)
// ============================================================================
async function pollLocalComfyResult(id: string) { return {} as any; }
async function callLocalTTSService(p: any) { return 3.4; } // Returns duration in seconds
async function executeHeadlessRemotionRender(p: any) {}
async function pollAstroApprovalStatus(id: string) { return true; }
async function callNotebookCreateSource(p: any) {}

```

### Step-by-Step Data Flow

| Step | Function | Input | Output | Primary Failure Guard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **1** | `compileCorpusAndLoadCanon` | `corpus/*.md` files | `CanonStateSnapshot` (`bible-state.json`) | Two-Pass Compiler rejects malformed frontmatter or broken cross-entity links. |
| **2** | `buildScenePreconditions` | `SceneInputDirective` | Active state vectors + Banned tokens | Attenuation heuristic strips the literal names of secrets from LLM vocabulary. |
| **3** | `synthesizeScriptAndActionAST` | Prompt JSON | Screenplay `.fountain` + Shot array | Schema decoding locks output format, requiring discrete motor verb enums. |
| **4** | `lintSceneAgainstCanon` | Shot array + Somatic vectors | `passed: boolean` + violation log | **O(1) Set-Intersection:** Instantly flags actions exceeding physical baseline limits. |
| **5** | `synthesizeAudioAndQuantizeTiming` | Validated AST | `SceneManifest` (locked integer frames) | ffprobe converts continuous audio ms into $24\text{ fps}$ frames with explicit pre/post padding. |
| **6** | `buildRadioPlayAnimatic` | `SceneManifest` | Diagnostic exposure sheet `.mp4` | Sidechain ducking math automatically attenuates ambient bed by $-14\text{ dB}$ under speech. |
| **7** | `awaitDirectorSignOff` | Animatic file path | `boolean` approval | **Human Gate:** Prevents cloud serverless GPUs from provisioning without review. |
| **8** | `dispatchServerlessGreenscreenPlates` | Approved Manifest | Array of R2 MP4 URLs | **Durable Object Actor:** Enforces idempotency keys and trips circuit breaker at attempt $\ge 2$. |
| **9** | `compositeFinalMasterEpisode` | Greenscreen plates + Matte art | Master `.mp4` deliverable | Remotion compositing isolates `#00FF00` keying and applies cinematic color grade. |
| **10** | `commitCanonStateDelta` | Scene mutations ($S_n \rightarrow S_{n+1}$) | New authoritative hash | D1 SQL trigger invalidates downstream scenes pinned to prior state hashes (`is_dirty = 1`). |
| **11** | `syncToNotebookKnowledgeBase` | Final script + Delta JSON | Updated NotebookLM source | Automated API sync updates series memory so future writing retains continuity. |This is not a single desktop application like Premiere or Blender. It is a **distributed pipeline with a single "Conductor" program (Node.js)** coordinating specialized local daemons, web interfaces, and serverless cloud runtimes.

Here is the exact breakdown of **where these files live on disk**, **what program executes each function**, and **how you actually trigger the chain**.

### How You Actually Run It: Two Operating Modes

Depending on whether you are working in a terminal or in a browser, the master orchestrator function (`executeProductionPipeline`) is invoked in one of two ways:

#### Mode A: The Terminal CLI (Automated Batch Mode)

Used during development, automated testing, or overnight batch processing. You run a single Node command from your project root:

```bash
# Terminal execution inside worker-sower-engine
npm run produce:scene -- --scene ep01_sc03 --episode ep01

```

* **What happens:**
1. Node.js executes `src/pipeline/produceEpisode.ts`.
2. It compiles the lore, runs local ComfyUI, runs the linter, synthesizes the audio, and outputs the animatic MP4.
3. The terminal halts and prints:
```text
[Step 7] Animatic generated: outputs/animatics/ep01_sc03_radio_play.mp4
[Step 7] Press [ENTER] to authorize cloud GPU batch, or [CTRL+C] to reject...

```


4. You listen to the file. If you hit `[ENTER]`, it calls Cloudflare, boots the RunPod GPUs, composites the final master, and syncs the script back to your Gemini Notebook.



#### Mode B: The Astro Showrunner Cockpit (Web UI Mode)

Used during creative directing sessions.

1. You start your local dev stack:
* Run local ComfyUI (`python main.py --port 8188`).
* Run the Astro dashboard (`npm run dev` in `goblin-dashboard`).


2. Open your browser to `http://localhost:4321/scenes/ep01_sc03`.
3. In the **Director Console**, type your narrative premise, set the conflict sliders, and click **"Compile Animatic"**.
* Astro's backend API (`src/pages/api/animatic/generate.ts`) calls Steps 1 through 6 in the background.


4. The animatic automatically loads inside the embedded **Remotion Player** on the webpage. You scrub through the scene, check the foley and vocal inflections.
5. You click **"Authorize Cloud Video Batch"**.
* The browser fires an HTTP POST to the Cloudflare Edge Worker (`/api/shots/dispatch`), kicking off Steps 8 through 11.


6. The UI's **Circuit Breaker Monitor** table starts updating in real time via polling or WebSockets as RunPod workers report completion.

---

### Summary of Directory Structure

In your local development environment, all these programs sit as siblings inside a single root folder:

```text
~/series-production/
├── goblin-lore/                 # @snailicid3/consumer-npm (Step 1)
│   ├── corpus/                  # Markdown files (characters, possessions)
│   └── compiled/                # bible-state.json
├── worker-sower-engine/         # The Conductor (Steps 2, 3, 4, 5, 11)
│   ├── src/pipeline/            # produceEpisode.ts (The Master Chain)
│   └── src/services/            # invariantLinter.ts, preconditions.ts
├── goblin-viewport/             # Remotion Video Engine (Steps 6, 9)
│   └── src/remotion/            # RadioPlayComposition.tsx, FinalComposite.tsx
├── goblin-dashboard/            # Astro Production Cockpit (Step 7)
│   └── src/pages/scenes/        # Web UI and director review player
└── series-edge-orchestrator/    # Cloudflare Workers & DOs (Steps 8, 10)
    └── src/objects/             # ShotCoordinator.ts (Durable Object Actor)

```

The master function chain (`executeProductionPipeline`) lives inside **`worker-sower-engine/src/pipeline/produceEpisode.ts`**. It acts as the glue that commands the other repositories and services, moving the asset forward step-by-step from raw Markdown text to a finished, composited animated episode.To start this process is not to open an empty text box and stare at a blinking cursor. It is not an act of speculative brainstorming or spinning the generative slot machine.

Starting this pipeline is an act of **foundry work**. It is cold, tactile, disciplined, and deliberate. You are laying down the concrete laws of a physical world, firing up local daemons, and stepping onto an industrial assembly line where creative intent is translated into mathematical constraints.

Here is what Day One, Hour Zero looks like, described in exact and expressive operational detail.

---

### Phase 0: The Cold Terminal & Daemon Awakening

You sit down at your workstation. Outside, the South Georgia dusk is sinking into the pine flats; inside, the only illumination comes from three high-resolution displays reflecting against the desk. You are not booting an all-in-one creative suite. You are waking up an ecosystem of specialized, decoupled engines.

You open your terminal multiplexer (`tmux`) and split the display into four operational quadrants:

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ PANE 1: ComfyUI Headless Daemon      │ PANE 2: Audio DSP & TTS Microservice │
│ (127.0.0.1:8188)                     │ (127.0.0.1:8000)                     │
│ [CUDA 12.4] RTX 4090 VRAM: 1.2GB/24GB│ [PyTorch] XTTSv2 / CosyVoice Warm    │
├──────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────┤
│ PANE 3: Astro Cockpit Server         │ PANE 4: The Conductor Shell          │
│ (localhost:4321)                     │ (worker-sower-engine)                │
│ [SSR] Edge Gateway: series-canon-db  │ bash$ _                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┘

```

1. **Pane 1 (The Visual Engine):** You run `./start-comfy.sh --highvram --listen 127.0.0.1 --port 8188 --disable-auto-launch`. The terminal scrolls rapidly as custom node wrappers load. ComfyUI settles into an idle loop, consuming just over a gigabyte of VRAM. It sits quietly in the dark, waiting for JSON payloads.
2. **Pane 2 (The Vocal Engine):** You launch the local audio microservice (`uvicorn main:app --port 8000`). It pins voice checkpoint embeddings into system RAM, ready to synthesize phonemes at a moment’s notice.
3. **Pane 3 (The Cockpit):** Inside `goblin-dashboard`, you execute `npm run dev`. Astro binds to `localhost:4321`. The director interface is live.
4. **Pane 4 (The Conductor):** You navigate into `worker-sower-engine`. This is where the baton will strike the podium.

The machinery is warm. Now, you must speak the laws of the universe into existence.

---

### Phase 1: Inscribing the Law in `goblin-lore`

Before a character can speak or move, their existence must be bound by physical, logistical, and epistemic reality. You do not open an LLM; you open your code editor to `@snailicid3/consumer-npm` (`goblin-lore`).

You navigate to `corpus/characters/` and create or verify the Markdown profile for **Octavius Oddwadd (008)**:

```markdown
---
id: char_008_octavius
name: Octavius Oddwadd
type: character
somatic_vector:
  locomotion_baseline: neuropathy_shuffle
  active_conditions:
    - condition_id: peripheral_neuropathy_severe
      severity: 0.85
      motor_limitations: [NO_SPRINT, NO_HEAVY_LIFT, RIGID_SPINE, UNSTEADY_GAIT]
      vocal_dsp_modifiers:
        pitch_semitones: -2
        speed_multiplier: 0.85
        pause_frequency_multiplier: 1.6
      generation_prompt_fragment: "haggard 60s wildcat machinist, trembling hands braced against cast-iron, heavy lead-type slump"
  signature_tics:
    - "right hand constantly seeks a load-bearing steel surface to anchor balance"
    - "wipes zinc dust from lower lip with back of wrist"
  banned_kinetic_verbs: [sprint, run, vault, leap, lunge, charge]
equip_slots:
  worn: ["grease_stained_canvas_coveralls", "thick_soled_cobbled_boots"]
  held: "rusted_micrometer_wrench"
  carried: ["tin_of_clove_lozenges", "soiled_cotton_rag"]
  cached_at:
    timber_mill_cellar: ["spare_oxygen_tank"]
epistemic_vector:
  known_secret_ids: ["secret_004_solvent_dump_creek"]
  escalation_ceiling: "Octavius will never openly threaten violence with a firearm; his leverage is strictly mechanical and forensic."
---

```

You switch to the terminal and run the two-pass compiler:

```bash
cd ~/goblin-show/goblin-lore
npm run compile

```

The terminal executes the gauntlet:

* **Pass 1 (Shape Validation):** Zod asserts that `neuropathy_shuffle` is a legal member of `LocomotionBaselineEnum`, that severity is bounded strictly between $0.0$ and $1.0$, and that equip slots are not overloaded.
* **Pass 2 (Relational Integrity):** The compiler sweeps across the entire corpus, verifying that `secret_004_solvent_dump_creek` actually exists in `corpus/grievances/` and that `timber_mill_cellar` resolves to a real location file.
* **The Seal:** Keys are sorted alphabetically, and the compiler executes an atomic write to `compiled/bible-state.json`.

```text
[Two-Pass Compiler] PASS 1: 42 entity frontmatter schemas validated.
[Two-Pass Compiler] PASS 2: 128 relational pointers verified. Zero orphans.
[Two-Pass Compiler] Wrote byte-identical state: compiled/bible-state.json (SHA-256: e8f4c2...9b)

```

The physical reality of your world is now mathematically frozen. The machine will not allow Octavius to sprint, it will not allow him to hold two props in one hand, and it will not allow him to draw a weapon he does not carry.

```
│ [ EXECUTE SCRIPT & ANIMATIC COMPILER ]                                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

You don't write the dialogue. You manipulate the **dramatic compression ratio**:

* You push **Curtness** to `0.82`. You want short, breath-starved sentences that terminate on hard consonants. Octavius is drowning in industrial lung fibrosis; Billy Fae has no time for pleasantries.
* You dial **Threat Level** to `0.94`. The perimeter is closing in; violence is an invisible, heavy weight in the room.
* You push **Subtext Suppression** to `0.88`. You mandate the Attenuation Heuristic: *Neither character is allowed to mention the toxic dump, the forged affidavit, or the impending arrest.* They must conduct this life-and-death struggle entirely through the proxy of diesel fuel prices and bridge weight limits.

You take a sip of black coffee, place your mouse over the blue button, and click: **EXECUTE SCRIPT & ANIMATIC COMPILER**.

### Phase 3: The Spark: Dispatching the Conductor

The instant you click that button, the Astro SSR route hits `worker-sower-engine/src/pipeline/produceEpisode.ts`.

In Pane 4, your terminal ignites.

```text
[Pipeline] =======================================================
[Pipeline] COMMENCING COMPILATION: EP01_SC01
[Pipeline] =======================================================
[Step 1] Loaded authoritative canon state: hash e8f4c29b.
[Step 2] Traversing relational preconditions...
         - Octavius: Somatic limit NO_SPRINT, UNSTEADY_GAIT engaged.
         - Leverage: Billy Fae holds unrecorded lien on sawmill scrap.
         - Attenuation fence: BANNED TOKENS ['solvent', 'dump', 'affidavit', 'arrest'].
[Step 3] Dispatching Child Graph A to local ComfyUI (Qwen 2.5 14B)...

```

In Pane 1, the GPU temperature spikes from $42^\circ\text{C}$ to $68^\circ\text{C}$. The model begins streaming tokens into memory. It is constrained by GBNF grammar rules—it cannot output conversational filler or meta-commentary. It outputs strictly structured Fountain screenplay format followed by an array of discrete motor actions.

#### The Linter Interception (The Self-Healing Loop)

Two seconds into the generation, the AST linter fires:

```text
[Step 4] LINTER ALERT: Take 1 failed invariant validation!
         Violation: Character 'char_008_octavius' executed prohibited motor verb 'LUNGE'.
         Reason: Active condition 'peripheral_neuropathy_severe' forbids dynamic weight transfer.
[Step 4] Triggering automated surgical repair loop...
         Re-injecting negative prompt: "Under no circumstances may Octavius lunge, jump, or shift weight rapidly. His movements are petrified and anchored."

```

The Conductor does not bother you. It rejects the hallucinated movement instantly, passes the violation back into the LLM context, and regenerates the shot.

Two seconds later:

```text
[Step 4] LINTER AUDIT: Take 2
         - Somatic motor actions: ['BRACE_ARM', 'LEAN_FORWARD', 'TAP_WRENCH'] -> [PASSED]
         - Epistemic secret leakage: 0 banned tokens detected -> [PASSED]
         - Prop consistency: 'rusted_micrometer_wrench' verified in hand slot -> [PASSED]
[Step 4] Script AST locked and certified.

```

### Phase 4: The Acoustic Crucible: The First Listen

Now the pipeline transitions from text to time.

In Pane 1, the text LLM is instantly flushed from VRAM:
`[ComfyUI] Memory cleared: 14.2GB VRAM released.`

Instantly, Pane 2 (the TTS microservice) takes the stage. It reads each line from the locked AST, synthesizes the speech stems using character voice embeddings, and saves raw `.wav` buffers into `public/audio/dialogue/`.

The Conductor runs `ffprobe` across the stems:

* **Shot 01 (Billy Fae):** `"Bridges out past the slough won't take thirty tons anymore, Octavius."` $\rightarrow$ Duration: $3.42\text{s}$ ($83\text{ frames}$) $+ 24\text{ frames padding} = \mathbf{107\text{ frames}}$.
* **Shot 02 (Octavius):** `"Then tell the county... to buy lighter trucks."` $\rightarrow$ Duration: $4.18\text{s}$ ($101\text{ frames}$) $+ 24\text{ frames padding} = \mathbf{125\text{ frames}}$.

The timeline is quantized. The scene duration is locked: **exactly 468 frames ($19.50\text{ seconds}$).**

The terminal calls Remotion:
`[Step 6] Compiling headless Remotion animatic (CRF 28, Concurrency 15)...`

Chromium boots in the background, composites the diagnostic HUD, applies dynamic sidechain ducking (dropping the industrial rain bed by $-14\text{ dB}$ whenever speech waves trigger), and writes `outputs/animatics/ep01_sc01_radio_play.mp4`.

You slide your headphones over your ears and press **Spacebar**.

You listen:

1. The low, ominous rumble of industrial rain and the intermittent buzzing hum of a wet transformer fills your ears.
2. Billy Fae delivers her line. Her voice is dry, rhythmic, terrifyingly unhurried.
3. Right as her voice begins, the background rain ducks downward smoothly, elevating the vocal clarity.
4. There is a heavy, five-beat pause. In the silence, you hear the tactile scrape of metal against concrete—the foley cue for Octavius anchoring his dead leg.
5. Octavius responds. The breathiness DSP modifier forces a wheeze between his clauses. His vocal delivery sounds like a man whose body is failing him, but whose will remains iron.

The pacing is immaculate. The subtext is suffocating.

You haven’t drawn a single storyboard. You haven't typed a ComfyUI prompt. You haven't guessed how many seconds the scene needs to be. Most importantly: **you have not spent a single cent of cloud GPU budget.**

You look at the green button on the bottom right:
**AUTHORIZE CLOUD VIDEO BATCH ($0.09)**

You know that when you click this button:

* The Cloudflare Durable Object will serialize the dispatch.
* An ephemeral serverless RTX 4090 on RunPod will hydrate from Cloudflare R2 via `s5cmd` in under 18 seconds.
* It will render 468 frames of pristine, razor-sharp character animation locked against an exact `#00FF00` chroma-key backdrop.
* Remotion will composite those characters over your hand-painted background plate, weld the audio, and hand you a finished, broadcast-ready scene in less than two minutes.

You click **AUTHORIZE**.

The terminal scrolls. The assembly line moves. The studio is alive.You do not have to live in a four-pane terminal window. A terminal multiplexer is a diagnostic tool for an engineer debugging raw sockets; it is a terrible interface for an artist directing a series.

The entire architecture we designed—Cloudflare Workers, D1, Durable Objects, Remotion, and serverless containers—is fundamentally web-native. **The Astro frontend can, and should, be your sole interface.**

You can interact with the Astro cockpit from a web browser on any machine (a laptop, an iPad, or a workstation), whether hosted locally on `localhost:4321` or deployed globally to the cloud on **Cloudflare Pages**, with zero terminals open in your daily workflow.

Here is how to eliminate the terminal clutter and turn the entire pipeline into a clean, cloud-accessible **Web Studio Cockpit**.

---

### The Two Non-Terminal Deployment Models

Depending on where you want the heavy computing to take place, you have two clean paths:

```
MODEL A: PURE CLOUD STUDIO (Zero Local Hardware)
[ Browser on Any Device ]
       │
       ▼ HTTPS
[ Astro Cockpit on Cloudflare Pages ] 
       │
       ├──► Cloudflare D1 (Canon Ledger & State Hashes)
       ├──► Cloudflare Workers AI / RunPod Serverless (LLM Script AST)
       ├──► Serverless TTS Container (Audio Stems to R2)
       ├──► Headless Remotion Container (Animatic MP4 to R2)
       └──► ComfyUI on RunPod Serverless (Greenscreen Video Plates)

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

MODEL B: THE HYBRID FOUNDRY (Local GPU Engine + Cloud Window)
[ Browser Anywhere (Cloud or Local) ]
       │
       ▼ HTTPS
[ Astro Cockpit (Cloudflare Pages or Localhost) ]
       │
       ▼ (Secure Cloudflare Tunnel / cloudflared)
[ Local Hardware Rig (Silent Background Service) ]
       ├── Headless ComfyUI Daemon (Port 8188)
       └── FastAPI Audio Microservice (Port 8000)

```

---

## Model A: The 100% Pure Cloud Cockpit (Zero Terminals, Zero Local Hardware)

In this setup, you do not run a single local process. You open Chrome or Safari, navigate to `[https://studio.yourdomain.com](https://studio.yourdomain.com)`, and the entire production executes across serverless cloud infrastructure.

### 1. Astro on Cloudflare Pages (SSR Edge Mode)

Astro compiles using the `@astrojs/cloudflare` adapter. Every page request, parameter change, and script dispatch runs as a serverless Worker function executing at the network edge in under 5 milliseconds.

```javascript
// astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';
import cloudflare from '@astrojs/cloudflare';
import react from '@astrojs/react';
import tailwind from '@astrojs/tailwind';

export default defineConfig({
  output: 'server',
  adapter: cloudflare({
    imageService: 'cloudflare',
    platformProxy: {
      enabled: true
    }
  }),
  integrations: [react(), tailwind()]
});

```

### 2. Moving Child Graphs A & B to the Cloud

* **Child Graph A (The Screenplay & AST):** Instead of calling a local Ollama instance, Astro’s backend route calls **Cloudflare Workers AI** (running models like Qwen 2.5 32B Instruct or Llama 3.3 70B directly on Cloudflare’s global GPU network with zero cold start), or calls an ephemeral serverless vLLM pod on RunPod.
* **Child Graph B (TTS & Duration Calculation):** Runs on a serverless RunPod container running your Parler-TTS or CosyVoice weights. It receives the dialogue JSON, synthesizes the audio directly into your **Cloudflare R2 bucket**, and returns the timing manifest to Astro.
* **Remotion Pre-Viz (The Animatic):** Instead of running headless Chromium on your laptop, Remotion runs via an ephemeral rendering task or serverless container, spitting the animatic `.mp4` straight into R2.

### 3. The Daily Creative Workflow

1. You open your browser on your laptop or tablet: `[https://studio.yourseries.com/scenes/ep01_sc03](https://studio.yourseries.com/scenes/ep01_sc03)`.
2. You type your premise into the Astro text area, set your tension sliders, and hit **"Compile Scene"**.
3. A progress bar animates across the Astro header:
* `[1/4] Canon Preconditions Verified (D1)`
* `[2/4] Script & Invariants Certified (Workers AI)`
* `[3/4] Audio Stems Synthesized (R2)`
* `[4/4] Animatic Baked`


4. The embedded **Remotion Player** pops onto the screen. You click Play, listen to the dialogue over the ducked rain bed, and inspect the exposure sheet HUD.
5. You click **"Authorize Cloud Video Batch"**.
6. The Cloudflare Durable Object dispatches the jobs to RunPod. You close your browser tab and go do something else.
7. An hour later, you open the URL on your phone: all 6 shots display green checkmarks with streamable MP4 deliverable links.

---

## Model B: The Hybrid Foundry (Local Compute, Cloud Window)

If you have powerful local workstation hardware (e.g., an RTX 3090/4090) and want to use your own silicon for free local rendering while still enjoying the slick web interface from anywhere in the world, you use **Cloudflare Tunnel (`cloudflared`)**.

This eliminates all terminal multiplexers by turning your local scripts into **silent background OS daemons**.

### 1. Running Daemons Silently in the Background

Instead of opening terminal panes and running commands manually, you configure your background engines via a process manager like **PM2** (or a system service/Docker Compose).

You create an `ecosystem.config.cjs` in your project root:

```javascript
// ecosystem.config.cjs
module.exports = {
  apps: [
    {
      name: 'comfyui-daemon',
      cwd: './ComfyUI',
      script: 'python',
      args: 'main.py --listen 127.0.0.1 --port 8188 --highvram --disable-auto-launch',
      autorestart: true,
      watch: false
    },
    {
      name: 'audio-tts-service',
      cwd: './audio-microservice',
      script: 'uvicorn',
      args: 'main:app --port 8000 --host 127.0.0.1',
      autorestart: true
    },
    {
      name: 'astro-dashboard',
      cwd: './goblin-dashboard',
      script: 'npm',
      args: 'run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4321',
      autorestart: true
    }
  ]
};

```

You start it once:

```bash
pm2 start ecosystem.config.cjs
pm2 save

```

From that moment on, whenever your computer boots, **all engines turn on silently in the background.** No terminal windows appear. No logs spam your screen. They consume idle memory and sleep until called.

### 2. Projecting Local Daemons to the Cloud via Cloudflare Tunnel

To access your local setup from a coffee shop, your phone, or an iPad without opening router ports or exposing your IP address, you establish a free, encrypted Cloudflare Tunnel:

```bash
# One-time terminal command to link your local hardware to your Cloudflare domain
cloudflared tunnel create studio-hardware

```

In your Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard, you route:

* `[https://api.yourseries.com/comfy](https://api.yourseries.com/comfy)` $\longrightarrow$ `[http://127.0.0.1:8188](http://127.0.0.1:8188)`
* `[https://api.yourseries.com/tts](https://api.yourseries.com/tts)` $\longrightarrow$ `[http://127.0.0.1:8000](http://127.0.0.1:8000)`
* `[https://studio.yourseries.com](https://studio.yourseries.com)` $\longrightarrow$ `[http://127.0.0.1:4321](http://127.0.0.1:4321)` (or hosted on Pages)

Now, your Astro web application (whether running in the cloud on Pages or locally) can communicate with your local graphics card through secure, authenticated HTTPS calls.

---

## What Replaces the Terminal Inside Astro?

If you don't have four terminal panes to look at, how do you know what the system is doing? How do you know if an invariant linter rejected a line, or if a model ran out of VRAM?

You build those diagnostics directly into the Astro web UI as **subtle, high-signal UI components**:

### 1. The Global Studio Status Bar (Top Nav)

In the top-right corner of your Astro layout, place an interactive status drawer that polls the daemons:

```tsx
// src/components/islands/StudioTelemetryBadge.tsx
import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react';

export const StudioTelemetryBadge: React.FC = () => {
  const [telemetry, setTelemetry] = useState({
    comfy: 'CHECKING',
    tts: 'CHECKING',
    canonDb: 'ONLINE',
    vramUsed: 0
  });

  useEffect(() => {
    const checkHealth = async () => {
      try {
        const res = await fetch('/api/system/health');
        const data = await res.json();
        setTelemetry(data);
      } catch {
        setTelemetry(prev => ({ ...prev, comfy: 'OFFLINE', tts: 'OFFLINE' }));
      }
    };
    checkHealth();
    const interval = setInterval(checkHealth, 5000);
    return () => clearInterval(interval);
  }, []);

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-3 font-mono text-xs bg-[#161620] px-3 py-1.5 rounded border border-[#262636]">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-1.5">
        <span className={`w-2 h-2 rounded-full ${telemetry.comfy === 'ONLINE' ? 'bg-emerald-400 animate-pulse' : 'bg-red-500'}`} />
        <span className="text-gray-300">GPU CORE</span>
      </div>
      <span className="text-gray-600">|</span>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-1.5">
        <span className={`w-2 h-2 rounded-full ${telemetry.tts === 'ONLINE' ? 'bg-emerald-400' : 'bg-red-500'}`} />
        <span className="text-gray-300">AUDIO DSP</span>
      </div>
      <span className="text-gray-600">|</span>
      <span className="text-blue-400 font-semibold">{telemetry.vramUsed} GB VRAM</span>
    </div>
  );
};

```

### 2. The Slide-Up "Black Box" Flight Recorder (Logs on Demand)

Instead of logs flooding a terminal, you put an expandable **Flight Recorder drawer** at the bottom of the Astro screen.

* 95% of the time, it stays collapsed. You don't care about the logs; you only care about the script and the animatic.
* If a compilation fails (e.g., *Somatic Invariant Breach: Octavius cannot sprint*), a small red badge flashes in the bottom tray.
* You click the tray, and it smoothly slides up from the bottom of the browser, displaying the exact error trace, the attempted action, and the rule that blocked it.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ▲ STUDIO FLIGHT RECORDER (COLLAPSED)                 [STATUS: ALL SYSTEMS OK]│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  ▼ (Click to expand drawer)
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ▼ STUDIO FLIGHT RECORDER                                        [CLEAR LOGS]│
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 14:02:11 [CANON] Verified snapshot e8f4c29b. 0 dirty dependencies.          │
│ 14:02:14 [LINTER] AST Take 1 rejected: 'LUNGE' violates condition neuropathy│
│ 14:02:16 [LINTER] AST Take 2 accepted: All actions conform to motor limits. │
│ 14:02:19 [TTS] Synthesized 4 stems. Master scene duration: 468 frames.      │
│ 14:02:22 [REMOTION] Headless animatic render complete: 19.50s @ 24fps.      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```
