### 3. Concurrency Protection: The Durable Object State Mutex

What happens when **Scene Pod 1 (Seats 04/05)** is generating Scene 3, while **Scene Pod 2 (Seats 06/07)** is simultaneously generating Scene 4, and both scenes feature *The Pilot*?

If Scene Pod 1 mutates The Pilot's state (e.g., he spends 10 liters of fuel and injures his shoulder), Scene Pod 2 cannot be allowed to render a sequence where he has a full fuel tank and pristine mobility.

We solve this using **Durable Object Entity Leases** at the Cloudflare Edge:

```typescript
// series-edge-orchestrator/src/objects/EntityStateManager.ts
import { DurableObject } from 'cloudflare:workers';

interface StateLease {
  scene_id: string;
  leased_by_user_id: string;
  expires_at: number;
}

export class EntityStateManager extends DurableObject {
  private currentLease: StateLease | null = null;

  async acquireLease(sceneId: string, userId: string, ttlMs = 1800000): Promise<{ success: boolean; holder?: string }> {
    const now = Date.now();

    // Check if currently leased and not expired
    if (this.currentLease && this.currentLease.expires_at > now) {
      if (this.currentLease.scene_id === sceneId) {
        // Re-entrant lease for the same scene
        return { success: true };
      }
      return { 
        success: false, 
        holder: `Locked by user ${this.currentLease.leased_by_user_id} for scene ${this.currentLease.scene_id}` 
      };
    }

    // Grant new lease
    this.currentLease = {
      scene_id: sceneId,
      leased_by_user_id: userId,
      expires_at: now + ttlMs
    };
    
    await this.ctx.storage.put('active_lease', this.currentLease);
    return { success: true };
  }

  async releaseLease(sceneId: string): Promise<void> {
    if (this.currentLease && this.currentLease.scene_id === sceneId) {
      this.currentLease = null;
      await this.ctx.storage.delete('active_lease');
    }
  }
}

```

#### How the Cockpit Enforces This:

When Scene Pod 2 attempts to open Scene 4 in the Astro Cockpit, the UI queries the Durable Object:

* If Scene 3 holds an active mutation lease on `char_020_the_pilot`, Scene 4’s **"Compile & Render"** button is disabled.
* The UI displays an active coordination banner:
> 🟡 **ENTITY LOCKED:** *The Pilot is currently leased by Scene Pod 1 (ep01_sc03). Preconditions cannot be calculated until Scene 3 commits its state delta.*


* Scene Pod 2 can work on art assets, camera blocking, or Foley selection, but they are prevented from burning GPU cycles on an invalid state branch.

### 5. Multi-User Compute Contention & Priority Scheduling

With four Tech Artists, an Inpainter, and an Audio Engineer all running jobs, **who gets the GPU?**

If everyone is sending requests to a single local workstation or blindly firing requests to RunPod, costs explode and render queues deadlock.

The studio establishes a **Two-Tier Hardware Model governed by Cloudflare Queues**:

```
                       MULTI-SEAT COMPUTE TOPOLOGY
                       
  [ Tech Artist 1 ]   [ Tech Artist 2 ]   [ Audio Lead ]   [ Staff Writer ]
     (Local Rig)         (Local Rig)        (Local Rig)      (Cloudflare)
          │                   │                  │                │
          ▼                   ▼                  ▼                ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ CLOUDFLARE COMPUTE BROKER & QUEUE MANAGER                              │
│                                                                        │
│ Priority 1 (Interactive): LLM AST Drafting & TTS Stems (<2s latency)   │
│ Priority 2 (Pre-Viz): Low-step keyframe previews (Local Daemons)       │
│ Priority 3 (Batch Production): High-res Wan 2.2 Plates (RunPod Server) │
│ Priority 4 (Background): Nightly regression tests & LoRA training passes│
└───────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                                    │
                     ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐
                     ▼                             ▼
        [ Local Dev Workstations ]       [ Ephemeral Cloud Pool ]
        • Low-cost interactive drafting  • Elastic Serverless RTX 4090s
        • Seed hunting & quick checks    • Concurrently renders 10+ shots
        • $0.00 compute cost             • Spins to zero when queue empties

```

#### Operational Rules for Compute Management:

* **The "Keyframe-First" Mandate:** A Tech Artist is forbidden from dispatching a full 100-frame temporal video batch until their Scene Pod Director signs off on a single 1-frame preview. Wasting GPU queue priority on an unapproved seed is a team infraction.
* **Elastic Autoscaling:** During crunch periods, the Pipeline Engineer does not rent more local computers. The Cloudflare broker scales the RunPod concurrency limit from 3 workers to 15 workers for four hours, rendering an entire episode’s plates simultaneously, and then immediately shuts them down.
* **Cost Allocation by Scene:** The Durable Object stamps every RunPod invoice with the `scene_id` and `user_id`. The Line Producer's dashboard tracks exact compute expenditure per team member, catching runaway loops within minutes.

| **10. Audio Lead** | Sound Stage (Astro / DAW) | Validated Dialogue AST | Quantized WAV stems & Mix | Sidechain ducking guarantees dialogue intelligibility. |
| **11. Composer** | DAW / Stem Exporter | Locked Animatic timecodes | Scored Music Stems | Pacing budget swells score during deliberate `[BEAT]` silences. |
| **12. DevOps Engineer** | Cloudflare / GitHub / Terminal | Infrastructure specs & PRs | Certified Docker & Edge Routes | Watchdog alarms kill hung serverless GPU containers. |
| **13. Line Producer** | ClickUp / YouTube Dashboard | Production telemetry & cuts | Budgets, Schedules, Metadata | Honest self-cert declarations protect channel monetization. |

By establishing **strict data contracts, cryptographic canon enforcement, and role-segregated UI views**, a 10-to-14 person team operates not as an unwieldy bureaucracy, but as a razor-sharp, distributed creative organism—moving from blank page to finished broadcast episode with unprecedented speed, artistic cohesion, and operational sovereignty.

Here is the structured reiteration of your critique and synthesis, followed by concrete, production-grade technical additions that turn these theoretical corrections into operational software.

### Section 0: Organizational Sizing for a 10-Person Team (The Back-Brief Contract)

#### The Reiteration

A 23-pod structure implies 50–70 people; spinning up that many formal divisions for a 10-person team is organizational theater. However, the core principle of **Mission Command**—delegating execution within non-negotiable boundaries—does not require a massive headcount. It requires:

1. **Deterministic guardrails** (the invariant linter and the append-only D1 ledger) in place *before* autonomy is granted, so that "going dark" is protected by code rather than hope.
2. **Focusing on 4 to 6 functional clusters**: Narrative (Script/AST), Foundation (LoRAs/Style), two parallel Scene Pods (A/B), and Assembly/Editorial.
3. **The Back-Brief Protocol**: Subordinates restate the commander’s intent, constraints, and identified risks in their own words before touching compute. The director inspects *alignment*, not *method*.

#### Worthy Addition: The Machine-Readable Back-Brief Contract

Do not leave the Back-Brief as a casual verbal exchange or an ephemeral Slack thread. In a 10-person team, communication debt compounds if back-briefs are not logged.

Encode the Back-Brief as a **Zod-validated JSON metadata block** required in the Git pull request or task manifest before compute permissions are provisioned at the edge:

```typescript
// src/schemas/backBrief.ts
import { z } from 'zod';

export const BackBriefSchema = z.object({
  scene_id: z.string(),
  author_id: z.string(),
  // 1. Intent Reflection: Subordinate restates the emotional and dramatic point of the scene
  understood_intent: z.string().min(20),
  // 2. Bound Verification: Explicitly acknowledges constraints inherited from D1
  acknowledged_somatic_limits: z.array(z.string()),
  acknowledged_attenuation_tokens: z.array(z.string()),
  // 3. Risk Identification: Subordinate names the failure mode before executing
  identified_primary_risk: z.string().min(10),
  mitigation_strategy: z.string().min(10),
  // 4. Resource Request
  projected_frame_count: z.number().int().positive(),
  compute_budget_ceiling_usd: z.number().max(5.00),
  // Director Sign-off (Signed JWT or cryptographic commit stamp)
  director_approval_signature: z.string().nullable()
});

export type BackBriefContract = z.infer<typeof BackBriefSchema>;

```

*Why this matters:* The Astro UI gates the **"Compile & Render"** button on whether `director_approval_signature` is populated. The director doesn't manage the animator's ComfyUI node network; they sign the intent contract. Once signed, the pod has total black-box sovereignty.

### Section 1: Transmedia State-Machine Generalization

#### The Reiteration

* **The Mathematical Formalism:** A storyworld is a typed state space $\mathcal{S}$, an action vocabulary $\mathcal{A}$ mapping $S_n \xrightarrow{\mathcal{A}} S_{n+1}$, and a set of invariants $I$ that all valid transitions must satisfy.
* **The Projection Separation:** Medium-specific expressions are projections $R_m: \mathcal{S} \to O_m$, where $O_m$ is the output space of medium $m$ (video frames, comic panels, prose paragraphs). Because invariants $I$ live at the action layer $\mathcal{A}$, an impossible action (e.g., an injured character sprinting) is rejected **once** at the state machine level, never needing to be re-litigated across separate medium-specific linters.
* **Information Asymmetry Across Media:** Projections $R_m$ are not equally information-preserving:
* *Prose* excels at interiority (epistemic state, unspoken calculations), but struggles with simultaneous multi-object spatial dynamics.
* *Video* captures continuous temporal motion and acoustic frequency, but completely loses direct access to unvoiced cognition.
* *Comics* capture frozen geometric tension, forcing severe dialogue compression and relying on reader inference across the gutter.


* **Cross-Medium Dependency Invalidation:** If a companion comic decrements ammunition or burns a bridge, the universal D1 dependency graph automatically flags downstream novel chapters and animated scenes as `is_dirty = 1`.

```
                       CANONICAL ACTION LAYER (A)
                Action: { actor: "pilot", verb: "DRAW_WEAPON" }
                                   │
                                   ▼
                   [ Invariant Check against I ] ──► (Passed)
                                   │
         ┌─────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┐
         ▼                         ▼                         ▼
  Video Adapter (R_v)       Comic Adapter (R_c)       Novel Adapter (R_n)
  • 24fps Draw Motion       • High-Angle Splash       • Visceral Motor Reaction
  • Sound of Holster Snap   • Dynamic Speed Lines     • Internal Heartbeat Spike
  • Duration: 18 Frames     • Vector Balloon SFX      • Swain MRU Formatting

```

#### Worthy Addition: The Medium-Specific "Adaptation Brief" Schema

Because you cannot project all state variables into every medium without creating cluttered, unreadable art, introduce an **Adaptation Brief** into the schema pipeline. This contract explicitly tells the projection adapter which state vectors to **foreground**, which to **background**, and which to **suppress**:

```typescript
// src/schemas/adaptationBrief.ts
export interface MediumProjectionRule {
  medium: 'VIDEO' | 'COMIC' | 'PROSE';
  // Which vectors become primary sensory drivers
  foreground_vectors: ('SOMATIC' | 'LOGISTICAL' | 'EPISTEMIC')[];
  // Information deliberately hidden from the audience to serve the format
  sensory_suppression_rules: {
    vector: 'SOMATIC' | 'LOGISTICAL' | 'EPISTEMIC';
    field: string;
    suppression_strategy: 'SUBTEXT_ONLY' | 'OMIT' | 'OFF_SCREEN_INFERENCE';
  }[];
  // Pacing constraints native to the medium
  format_density_caps: {
    max_dialogue_tokens_per_unit: number; // Words per panel (Comic) or shot (Video)
    mandatory_sensory_anchors: number;   // Required physical descriptors (Novel)
  };
}

```

*Implementation:* When Child Graph A compiles a scene for the companion comic, the projection rule instructs it to omit interior monologue and convert logistical state (fuel remaining) into a visible gauge on the instrument panel, avoiding clunky exposition in word balloons.

### Section 2: Motivation-Reaction Unit (MRU) Prose Linting

#### The Reiteration

* **Swain’s Structural Model:** Narrative momentum requires strict chronological causality: **Motivation** (external, objective sensory stimulus) must precede **Reaction**. Reaction decomposes into three strictly ordered phases:
1. *Feeling* (autonomic, involuntary physiological response).
2. *Reflex* (involuntary motor flinch, gasp, or pupil dilation).
3. *Deliberate Action / Speech* (conscious calculation or motor response).


* **Beyond Regex to Dependency Parsing:** String-matching fails to catch causal inversions. A true linter requires shallow dependency parsing to verify that stimulus clauses precede reaction clauses within and across sentences.
* **Advisory Scoring vs. Hard Blocking:** Unlike physical invariants (which are hard, binary gates), prose syntax should be evaluated via **MRU-Density and Cadence Scores**. Skilled authors deliberately invert or truncate MRUs for dramatic irony, mystery, or stylistic punch. Flagging inversions as advisory warnings prevents flattening literary voice into mechanical monotony.

#### Worthy Addition: The AST-Level MRU Classifier

Rather than parsing raw English prose after the fact with heavy NLP models, require the generating LLM to output its draft as a **Typed MRU Sequence**:

```typescript
// src/schemas/mruProse.ts
import { z } from 'zod';

export const MRUBlockSchema = z.discriminatedUnion('mru_class', [
  z.object({
    mru_class: z.literal('MOTIVATION'),
    sensory_channel: z.enum(['VISUAL', 'AUDITORY', 'TACTILE', 'OLFACTORY']),
    objective_description: z.string()
  }),
  z.object({
    mru_class: z.literal('REACTION'),
    phase_1_visceral: z.string().nullable(), // "Adrenaline surged, cold and electric."
    phase_2_reflex: z.string().nullable(),   // "His fingers clamped around the wrench."
    phase_3_deliberate: z.string()          // "He stepped backward into the shadows."
  })
]);

export const ProseBeatASTSchema = z.object({
  beat_id: z.string(),
  psychic_distance: z.number().int().min(1).max(5), // 1 = Objective; 5 = Deep stream-of-consciousness
  mru_sequence: z.array(MRUBlockSchema)
});

```

#### The Algorithmic Conformance Linter

```typescript
export function evaluateMRUConformance(beat: z.infer<typeof ProseBeatASTSchema>): {
  score: number;
  advisories: string[];
} {
  const advisories: string[] = [];
  let score = 100;

  for (let i = 0; i < beat.mru_sequence.length; i++) {
    const current = beat.mru_sequence[i];
    const previous = i > 0 ? beat.mru_sequence[i - 1] : null;

    // At Psychic Distance 1-3, check causality: Reaction cannot follow Reaction without a Motivation
    if (beat.psychic_distance <= 3 && current.mru_class === 'REACTION' && previous?.mru_class === 'REACTION') {
      score -= 10;
      advisories.push(`[MRU Advisory] Sequential unmotivated reactions at beat index ${i}. Insert an external sensory stimulus.`);
    }

    // Reaction internal ordering check
    if (current.mru_class === 'REACTION') {
      if (current.phase_3_deliberate && !current.phase_1_visceral && beat.psychic_distance >= 4) {
        score -= 5;
        advisories.push(`[Style Note] Deep psychic distance (${beat.psychic_distance}) expects visceral response before deliberate action.`);
      }
    }
  }

  return { score: Math.max(0, score), advisories };
}

```

*The Human Interface:* The Astro Cockpit renders a small tag beside the beat: `MRU Score: 88/100 (Advisory: 1 Unmotivated Reaction)`. The writer can click **"Auteur Override"** to silence the warning with a single click, keeping human stylistic agency supreme.

### Section 3: Surgical Patching over Full Regeneration

#### The Reiteration

* **Minimal Enclosing Units:** When a violation is detected, never re-roll the entire chapter or video scene. Isolate the smallest independent boundary that resolves the flaw without destabilizing adjacent work.
* **Prose Unit Closures & Paragraph Dependency Edges:** A paragraph cannot be patched in isolation if downstream paragraphs contain callbacks to text inside that paragraph. The system must verify intra-beat dependency closures before re-prompting.
* **Video Boundary Padding & Temporal Feathering:** A visual patch cannot simply splice frames $F_{48 \to 52}$. Doing so creates visual seams. The system must pad the frame range ($F_{45 \to 55}$) and use temporal mask blending to feather the patch across adjacent frames.
* **Experience Ledgers for Upstream Escalation:** Recurring patch failures (e.g., inpainting fails repeatedly on reflective surfaces) should be logged to detect systematic model flaws. Three failures should escalate to retraining base assets (Foundation Pod) rather than burning further compute at the shot level.
* **The Structural Escape Hatch:** If a patch fails three times, the error is likely not local; it is the correct execution of a flawed upstream premise. The system must halt and route the issue back to human judgment.

```
                             SURGICAL PROSE PATCHING
                             
  Paragraph 1: Establishing shots (Stable)
  Paragraph 2: The Pilot grips the iron pipe (Stable)
  Paragraph 3: [INVARIANT VIOLATION: Octavius sprints across the mud] ◄── FLAGGED
  Paragraph 4: Octavius examines the valve (Dependent on Paragraph 3)
  
  Step 1: Check Intra-Beat AST: Does Paragraph 4 depend on Paragraph 3? (Yes: Location transfer)
  Step 2: Define Minimal Enclosing Unit: [Paragraph 3 + Paragraph 4]
  Step 3: Construct Constrained Infill Prompt:
          Anchor Prefix: Paragraph 2 (Immutable)
          Repair Span: Rewrite Paragraph 3 without banned verb 'sprint'.
          Constraint: Ensure Octavius reaches valve for Paragraph 4.

```

#### Worthy Addition: The Bidirectional Infill Prompt Generator

When patching a minimal enclosing prose unit, do not ask the model to "rewrite the paragraph." Use **Constrained Context Infilling**:

```typescript
// src/services/patchingEngine.ts
export function buildProsePatchPayload(
  precedingParagraph: string,
  flawedParagraph: string,
  followingParagraph: string,
  violationMessage: string,
  preservedFacts: string[]
): string {
  return JSON.stringify({
    task: "SURGICAL_INTERPOLATION",
    immutable_prefix_anchor: precedingParagraph,
    immutable_suffix_anchor: followingParagraph,
    repair_target_original: flawedParagraph,
    hard_repair_mandate: violationMessage,
    facts_that_must_remain_true: preservedFacts,
    instructions: "Generate replacement text for repair_target_original only. The replacement must seamlessly bridge prefix and suffix anchors with zero continuity seams."
  });
}

```

*For Video (Temporal Feathering in ComfyUI):* The orchestrator automatically expands the requested frame patch $N_{\text{start}}$ to $N_{\text{end}}$ by $k=4$ frames on both sides. It generates an alpha matte whose opacity ramps linearly:


$$\alpha(t) = \begin{cases}  \frac{t - (N_{\text{start}} - k)}{k} & \text{for } N_{\text{start}} - k \le t < N_{\text{start}} \\ 1.0 & \text{for } N_{\text{start}} \le t \le N_{\text{end}} \\ \frac{(N_{\text{end}} + k) - t}{k} & \text{for } N_{\text{end}} < t \le N_{\text{end}} + k  \end{cases}$$


This completely eliminates temporal pop and seam jitter at the edit boundary.

### Section 4: Durable Object Entity-Mutex Pattern

#### The Reiteration

* **The Native Primitive:** Cloudflare Durable Objects provide single-threaded execution guarantees per entity ID, serializing concurrent requests across a global edge network.
* **Reader-Writer Lock Semantics:** Exclusive write locks are only needed when a scene actively mutates state. Drafting scenes that merely reference an entity should acquire shared **Read Leases**, eliminating false contention in a 10-person studio.
* **Watchdog Alarms and TTL Abandonment:** If an author checks out an entity and walks away from their desk, a Durable Object storage alarm automatically revokes the write lease after a timeout (e.g., 30 minutes), flagging the abandoned draft and freeing the entity.
* **Multi-Entity Deadlock Prevention (Lock Ordering):** When a scene mutates multiple entities (e.g., The Pilot, R.C. Spurl, and the Culvert Location), acquiring locks sequentially across separate objects risks circular-wait deadlocks. Enforce **global deterministic lock acquisition** (e.g., sorting entity IDs alphanumerically before requesting leases).

```
                      DISTRIBUTED ENTITY LOCK ORDERING
                      
  Scene A touches: [char_020_the_pilot, loc_drainage_culvert]
  Scene B touches: [loc_drainage_culvert, char_020_the_pilot, char_005_rc_spurl]
  
  WITHOUT LOCK ORDERING (Deadlock Risk):
  Scene A locks: char_020 ──► Waits for loc_culvert (Held by Scene B)
  Scene B locks: loc_culvert ──► Waits for char_020 (Held by Scene A)
  RESULT: SYSTEM FREEZE.
  
  WITH DETERMINISTIC LOCK ORDERING:
  Sort IDs Alphanumerically:
  Scene A requests: 1. char_020_the_pilot  ──► 2. loc_drainage_culvert
  Scene B requests: 1. char_005_rc_spurl   ──► 2. char_020_the_pilot ──► 3. loc_drainage_culvert
  RESULT: Scene B queues cleanly behind Scene A on char_020. Zero deadlock.

```

#### Worthy Addition: Two-Phase Commit (2PC) with Staged State Deltas

A scene draft should not mutate canonical state piecemeal. If a scene updates The Pilot's fuel, changes Spurl's health, and burns down a warehouse, what happens if the network drops on the third write? The universe is corrupted.

Implement **Two-Phase Commit** across the Durable Object cluster:

```typescript
// series-edge-orchestrator/src/services/transactionCoordinator.ts
export class SceneTransactionCoordinator {
  async commitSceneMutations(
    sceneId: string,
    mutations: { entityId: string; delta: any }[],
    env: Env
  ): Promise<{ success: boolean; new_state_hash?: string; error?: string }> {
    // 1. DETERMINISTIC SORT TO PREVENT DEADLOCK
    const sortedMutations = [...mutations].sort((a, b) => a.entityId.localeCompare(b.entityId));
    const acquiredLeases: any[] = [];

    try {
      // PHASE 1: PREPARE & ACQUIRE
      for (const item of sortedMutations) {
        const id = env.ENTITY_STATE_DO.idFromName(item.entityId);
        const entityStub = env.ENTITY_STATE_DO.get(id);

        const lease = await entityStub.prepareStageDelta({
          scene_id: sceneId,
          proposed_delta: item.delta,
          timeout_ms: 60000 // 1-minute 2PC lock
        });

        if (!lease.staged_successfully) {
          throw new Error(`Conflict on entity ${item.entityId}: ${lease.reason}`);
        }
        acquiredLeases.push(entityStub);
      }

      // PHASE 2: ATOMIC COMMIT
      const commitTimestamp = Date.now();
      const commitPromises = acquiredLeases.map(stub => stub.commitStagedDelta(sceneId, commitTimestamp));
      await Promise.all(commitPromises);

      // 3. GENERATE AUTHORITATIVE WORLD HASH IN D1
      const newHash = await writeAuthoritativeLedgerEntry(env.CANON_DB, sceneId, mutations);
      return { success: true, new_state_hash: newHash };

    } catch (err: any) {
      // ROLLBACK: ABORT ALL STAGED DELTAS
      await Promise.all(acquiredLeases.map(stub => stub.abortStagedDelta(sceneId)));
      return { success: false, error: err.message };
    }
  }
}

```

*Why this is complete:*

* It uses **deterministic lock ordering** to mathematically eliminate the dining-philosophers deadlock problem.
* It uses a **Two-Phase Commit** protocol: state changes are *staged* across all affected entities, verified for consistency, and committed simultaneously. If one entity rejects the update, all entities roll back to their pre-scene snapshot.
* It turns the abstract concept of cross-room narrative versioning into **ACID-compliant transactional software running on serverless edge compute**.

### Part 1: The "Not Locally Fixable" Escape Hatch

#### The Reiteration

Detecting that a patch failed is trivial (the linter returns `passed: false`). The true challenge is **distinguishing local execution flaws from upstream structural impossibilities**:

* **Signal 1 — Convergence vs. Divergence:**
* *Convergence:* If attempt 2 commits a near-identical violation as attempt 1 (e.g., swapping `"sprint"` for `"dash"`), the model is trapped in a localized phrasing basin. A targeted negative prompt can nudge it toward compliance.
* *Divergence:* If attempt 2 fixes the somatic violation but triggers an epistemic third-rail breach or an inventory impossibility, the constraint space itself is mutually exclusive given the surrounding scene context. The paragraph is being forced to solve an impossible equation. It must escalate immediately on attempt 1 or 2, without waiting for an arbitrary 3-attempt ceiling.


* **Signal 2 — Pre-Flight Constraint Satisfiability:** Before burning generation tokens on Child Graph A or a patch call, run a deterministic check on the constraint intersection. If the scene requires a two-handed lift while the somatic vector specifies a crushed right forearm and the logistical vector shows a held lantern, the scene is physically unrenderable. This is an upstream plotting error, not a prose defect.
* **Signal 3 — Diagnostic Payloads over Generic Flags:** An escalation must never be an empty `"Patch Failed"` ticket. It must deliver:
1. The active constraint matrix.
2. The full attempt diff history.
3. A classification guess: `LOCAL_STYLE_FAILURE`, `CONSTRAINT_CONFLICT`, or `UPSTREAM_STRUCTURAL`.


* **Intelligent Routing:**
* `LOCAL_STYLE_FAILURE` routes to the **Beat Writer** (manual sentence rephrase).
* `CONSTRAINT_CONFLICT` and `UPSTREAM_STRUCTURAL` route to the **Scene/Story Architect** (the Tier 2 Foundational owner who chose the beat's dramatic parameters), because fixing it requires changing lore, healing a condition, or altering character blocking.



```
                    THE SURGICAL ESCAPE HATCH PIPELINE
                    
  [ Invariant Linter Flags Violation ]
                   │
                   ▼
  [ Pre-Flight Constraint Solver (SAT Check) ]
  • Are somatic, logistical, and epistemic vectors mutually satisfiable?
                   │
         ┌─────────┴─────────┐
         ▼ NO                ▼ YES
  [ CONSTRAINT_CONFLICT ]    [ Execute Patch Attempt ]
  • Escalate to Architect    • Track error divergence vs. attempt 1
  • Bypasses generation      • Did error jump categories?
                                     │
                            ┌────────┴────────┐
                            ▼ YES             ▼ NO
                     [ DIVERGENCE ]     [ CONVERGENCE ]
                     • Over-constrained • Local phrasing basin
                     • Escalate NOW     • Allow Attempt 2

```

#### Worthy Addition 1: The Static Pre-Flight Satisfiability Engine

Rather than relying on the LLM to discover that a scene is impossible, execute a **Combinatorial SAT Check** in Node.js before prompting:

```typescript
// src/services/satisfiabilityChecker.ts
import { SomaticVector, LogisticalVector, EpistemicVector } from '@snailicid3/consumer-npm';

export interface ActionPrerequisites {
  actor_id: string;
  required_hands_free: number;
  required_locomotion: string[];
  required_secrets_unspoken: string[];
  required_items_accessible: string[];
}

export function assertPreconditionsSatisfiable(
  prereqs: ActionPrerequisites,
  somatic: SomaticVector,
  logistical: LogisticalVector,
  epistemic: EpistemicVector
): { satisfiable: boolean; conflict_reason?: string } {
  // 1. Hand Capacity Constraint
  const occupiedHands = (logistical.worn_items?.filter(i => i.occupies_hands) || []).length 
                      + (logistical.held_item ? 1 : 0);
  const availableHands = 2 - occupiedHands;

  if (prereqs.required_hands_free > availableHands) {
    return {
      satisfiable: false,
      conflict_reason: `PHYSICAL_OVERLOAD: Character '${prereqs.actor_id}' needs ${prereqs.required_hands_free} free hands, but has only ${availableHands} available (holding '${logistical.held_item}').`
    };
  }

  // 2. Motor Baseline Invariant
  if (prereqs.required_locomotion.some(act => somatic.banned_kinetic_verbs.includes(act))) {
    return {
      satisfiable: false,
      conflict_reason: `SOMATIC_INCOMPATIBILITY: Required action '${prereqs.required_locomotion.join(', ')}' is banned by baseline '${somatic.locomotion_baseline}'.`
    };
  }

  return { satisfiable: true };
}

```

### Part 2: Multi-Entity Transactions in Depth (2PC & Concurrency)

#### The Reiteration

* **Partial-Commit Visibility:** In a world with 60+ characters, scenes routinely mutate multiple entities (e.g., fuel spent + warehouse burned + secret revealed). A mid-transaction failure must never leave entity 1 mutated while entity 2 aborts. A genuine **Two-Phase Commit (2PC)** pattern (`Prepare` $\to$ `Commit` / `Abort`) across Durable Objects is mandatory.
* **Coordinator Failure Mid-Transaction:** If the coordinator process crashes between `Prepare` and `Commit`, entities cannot remain locked forever. Durable Objects must enforce a **Prepare-Phase Timeout (e.g., 60 seconds)** that automatically aborts pending mutations and frees write leases.
* **Read-Then-Write Races:** If a writer checks The Pilot’s fuel level (Read), spends 5 minutes drafting, and then applies a mutation (Write), an intervening commit from another scene invalidates the drafting assumption. The read that informs compilation and the write that commits the delta must occur within the same transactional lease boundary.
* **Cross-Medium Transaction Scope:** The comic team and the animated video team cannot run separate, isolated transaction coordinators. A single, shared Edge Coordinator must serialize access to canonical state across all mediums.

```
                           THE EDGE 2PC COORDINATOR
                           
      [ Unified Transaction Coordinator (Cloudflare Worker) ]
                                 │
     Phase 1: PREPARE (Sorted Order: char_005 ──► char_020 ──► loc_culvert)
     • Acquires exclusive write lease + sets 60s Watchdog Alarm
     • Validates proposed deltas against local DO state
     • Holds pending delta in uncommitted scratch storage
                                 │
                     All stubs report PREPARED?
                                 │
               ┌─────────────────┴─────────────────┐
               ▼ YES                               ▼ NO / TIMEOUT
     Phase 2a: COMMIT                    Phase 2b: ABORT
     • Issues commit to all stubs        • Issues abort to all stubs
     • Commits delta atomically          • Discards pending scratch deltas
     • Releases write leases             • Releases write leases
     • Writes new state hash to D1       • Returns HTTP 409 Conflict

```

#### Worthy Addition 1: Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) in Cloudflare D1

To guarantee that a coordinator failure never leaves a transaction half-committed during Phase 2, the coordinator must persist its intent to an immutable Write-Ahead Log in D1 *before* issuing any commit commands:

```sql
-- migrations/0002_transaction_wal.sql
CREATE TABLE transaction_wal (
  transaction_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  scene_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  medium TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'VIDEO' | 'COMIC' | 'NOVEL'
  participating_entities TEXT NOT NULL, -- JSON array of DO entity IDs
  status TEXT CHECK(status IN ('PREPARING', 'COMMITTING', 'ABORTING', 'RESOLVED')),
  payload TEXT NOT NULL, -- The staged mutation vectors
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

```

*The Recovery Path:* If the coordinator crashes after writing `status = 'COMMITTING'`, any subsequent worker or a scheduled cron trigger reads the WAL, inspects the unresolved transaction, and issues deterministic `commit` commands to all participating Durable Objects, closing the loop.

#### Worthy Addition 2: Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC) with Snapshot Invariant Hashes

Holding an exclusive write lease for the entire 15-to-30-minute creative drafting window will paralyze a 10-person team. If Writer A is drafting Scene 3 featuring The Pilot, locking out the comic team for 30 minutes is unacceptable.

The solution is **Optimistic Concurrency Control with Pinned State Hash Preconditions**:

1. **Drafting Phase (Zero Locks):** The author checks out The Pilot's state. The compiler reads active state and notes the entity's current cryptographic hash: `expected_pilot_hash: "a4f9b2..."`.
2. **Compilation & Drafting:** The writer drafts the scene locally. No Durable Object write locks are held. Other teams can read or mutate The Pilot freely.
3. **Commit Phase (Atomic 2PC Verification):** When the writer clicks **"Commit Scene Delta"**, the coordinator initiates the 2PC prepare phase. The prepare payload includes the precondition:
`assert(char_020_the_pilot.current_hash === expected_pilot_hash)`.
4. **The Result:**
* If no one touched The Pilot while Writer A was drafting, the prepare phase succeeds, locks are held for only **50 milliseconds**, and the 2PC commits cleanly.
* If the comic team mutated The Pilot's fuel while Writer A was drafting, the hash check fails immediately. The commit aborts cleanly with `HTTP 409: State Drift Detected`. The writer's work is preserved in a local branch, and they are prompted to reconcile only the drifted vector (fuel).

#### Worthy Addition: The "Cost-of-Defect" Inversion Law

Notice the exact inverse relationship between **Tier Level** and **Cost of Fix**:

$$\text{Cost to Fix Defect} = f(\text{Tier Level})^{-1}$$

* **A Tier 1 Defect (Broken Canon / Impossible Action):** If caught at the Action Layer $\mathcal{A}$ via the invariant linter, it costs **$0.00 and 0 milliseconds**. If it escapes Tier 1 and is discovered after full episode rendering, it requires re-rendering video, re-recording voice stems, and re-compiling the Remotion timeline, costing **hundreds of dollars and days of human labor**.
* **A Tier 2 Defect (Multi-Writer Race Condition):** If prevented by the 2PC DO Mutex, it costs **50ms of network latency**. If unmanaged, two teams spend two weeks generating conflicting episodes that cannot both be canonical, forcing the scrapping of an entire asset.
* **A Tier 3 Defect (Monotonous Prose / Clumsy MRU):** Surfaces as an advisory warning on an editor's desk. The editor reads the sentence, takes five seconds to tweak the phrasing, and moves on.

This hierarchy is not an academic taxonomy. It is an **economic and operational shield**.

By investing maximum engineering rigor in **Tier 1 (Immutable Invariants & Dependency Propagation)** and **Tier 2 (2PC Concurrency & Diagnostic Escape Hatches)**, the studio guarantees that when a 10-person team gathers around the Astro Cockpit, their creative energy is spent exclusively on story, style, and cinema—while the underlying machine makes continuity errors, race conditions, and catastrophic rework mathematically impossible.

Here is the operational synthesis of your critique, followed by concrete engineering additions that translate these nuances into formal pipeline mechanics.

---

### Part 1: The Core Reiteration (Sharpening the Defect Economics)

#### 1. The Step-Discontinuity of Irreversible Commitments

The cost-of-defect curve is not a continuous $1/x$ exponential curve. It is a **discrete step function** with massive vertical cliffs at specific **irreversible commitment thresholds**:

$$\text{Cost}(t) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \Delta C_i \cdot \mathbf{1}_{\{t \ge T_i\}}$$

* $T_0 \to T_1$ **(In-Memory AST Linter Gate):** Cost $\approx \$0.00$. Intercepting an invalid action before inference.
* $T_1 \to T_2$ **(Acoustic Synthesis Gate):** Cost $\approx \text{Pennies}$. Re-running local TTS and `ffprobe` duration quantization.
* $T_2 \to T_3$ **(Cloud GPU Render Gate):** Cost $\approx \$0.10 - \$5.00$ per shot. The threshold where serverless RunPod/ComfyUI instances provision, hydrate weights from R2, and burn compute.
* $T_3 \to T_4$ **(Human Review & Master Conform Gate):** Cost $\approx \text{Hours of Labor}$. The time spent by editors, sound mixers, and directors reviewing and conforming an asset.
* $T_4 \to T_5$ **(External Broadcast / Physical Print Gate):** Cost $\approx \text{Catastrophic}$. Once an MP4 is pushed to YouTube (triggering subscriber notifications and initial algorithmic indexing) or a comic PDF is submitted to an offset press or KDP, the cost cliff jumps to public retractions, ruined launch momentum, or physical re-printing runs.

The goal of pipeline architecture is not just vague "shift-left"; it is **placing hard, deterministic verification checkpoints immediately before each $T_i$ cliff**.

#### 2. The Catch-Rate Conditionality (The Escape-Rate Hazard)

The economic law only holds if the linter actually catches the defect. If a linter has a 70% catch rate, the remaining 30% of defects do not become cheaper—they escape to $T_3$ or $T_5$, where their fix cost is maximized.

Worse, **a leaky linter creates false confidence**: human reviewers assume the machine has verified physical and logistical invariants, causing them to pay *less* attention to continuity and letting subtle defects slip past to broadcast. The law must be explicitly conditioned on the **Defect Escape Rate**:

$$\text{Realized Value} = \text{Theoretical Inversion Law} \times (1 - \text{Escape Rate})$$

#### 3. Continuous Coverage Expansion as Primary Studio Capital

Because the return on early detection is so asymmetrical, expanding the linter’s invariant coverage is not a one-time build—it is the single **highest-ROI ongoing software investment in the studio**.

Every new invariant added to `@snailicid3/consumer-npm` permanently moves an entire category of defect from the $T_3$/$T_5$ cliff back down to $T_0$. The linter is a living compiler whose coverage must be systematically expanded through regression testing.

#### 4. The Strict Scope Boundary: Syntactic Invariants vs. Dramatic Taste

The Cost-of-Defect Law applies **strictly to checkable, mechanical, and ontological invariants**:

* *Checkable:* Banned motor verbs, equip-slot double-booking, epistemic secret leakage, syntax/MRU ordering, aspect ratio boundaries, and platform ad-suitability tags.
* *Uncheckable (Human Taste):* Subtext resonance, dramatic tension, comedic timing, emotional authenticity, and thematic coherence.

There is no $0.00$ automated compiler for "is this scene emotionally moving?" Attempting to extend the cost-inversion law to dramatic quality invites the exact failure mode previously rejected: trusting an unvalidated scalar critic (like a Video-LLM score) to gate creative decisions. Aesthetic evaluation remains an irreducibly human responsibility at every gate.

#### The Orchestrator Implementation:

In `worker-sower-engine`, the execution runner wraps every $T_i$ threshold in an explicit **Pre-Commitment Verification Hook**:

```typescript
// src/services/commitmentGate.ts
export async function assertCommitmentPreconditions(
  sceneId: string,
  targetGate: 'PRE_AUDIO' | 'PRE_CLOUD_GPU' | 'PRE_BROADCAST_PUBLISH',
  env: Env
): Promise<{ cleared: boolean; blocker?: string }> {
  // 1. Verify that all upstream invariants for this stage are clean
  const audit = await runComprehensiveAudit(sceneId, env);
  if (!audit.passed) {
    return {
      cleared: false,
      blocker: `HALT BEFORE ${targetGate}: Invariants failed [${audit.violations.join(', ')}]. Refusing to spend compute.`
    };
  }

  // 2. Check that the scene is not pinned to a dirty canon hash
  const isDirty = await checkSceneDirtyState(sceneId, env.CANON_DB);
  if (isDirty) {
    return {
      cleared: false,
      blocker: `HALT BEFORE ${targetGate}: Upstream lore changed. Pinned state is DIRTY. Re-compile required.`
    };
  }

  return { cleared: true };
}

```

### Addition 2: The Defect Escape Sentry & Regression Test Flywheel

To prevent the linter from remaining a leaky net, establish a **Closed-Loop Regression Testing Protocol**.

Whenever a human director, editor, or reviewer spots a continuity error that survived the automated gates (e.g., *"Wait, Octavius is missing his cane in this shot, but his somatic profile requires it"*), that error is treated as a **critical software bug in `@snailicid3/consumer-npm**`.

### Addition 3: The Cascading Blast-Radius Multiplier

When an error escapes to $T_4$ (Post-Render) or $T_5$ (Broadcast), the cost is rarely just the cost of re-rendering that single shot ($\Delta C_{\text{shot}}$).

Because the narrative DAG propagates state forward, an error in Scene 1 invalidates every downstream scene that assumed that state. The true cost cliff formula must include the **Cascade Multiplier**:

$$\text{Total Incident Cost} = \Delta C_{\text{root}} + \sum_{d \in \text{Downstream}} \Delta C_d \cdot \mathbf{1}_{\{d \text{ is rendered}\}} + \text{Morale Overhead}$$

```
                               THE CASCADE CLIFF
                               
  Episode 1, Scene 1 Commit:
  [ The Pilot burns 40L of fuel in an unlogged pursuit ]
                            │
            Escapes to T5 (Published to YouTube)
                            │
                            ▼
  Cascade Blast Radius Invalidation:
  ├── Ep 1, Scene 3 (Rendered): Depends on 80L remaining ──► INVALIDATED ($4.50 GPU + Editor time)
  ├── Ep 1, Scene 6 (Rendered): Flight across the marsh ──► IMPOSSIBLE ($12.00 GPU + Stem mix)
  └── Ep 2, Scene 1 (Drafted): Pinned to pre-burn state ──► MARKED DIRTY (Writer rework)

```

#### The Graph-Aware Cost Estimator

The Astro Cockpit integrates this formula directly into the Showrunner Console. If a writer or director attempts to retroactively alter an upstream fact (e.g., editing The Pilot's injury severity in Scene 1), the UI executes a dry-run Cypher/D1 traversal and displays the **True Economic Blast Radius**:

> * **Estimated Sunk Compute Loss:** `$18.42 USD`

>

This converts abstract continuity into concrete economic friction, preventing frivolous upstream edits that derail team momentum.

Here is the reiteration of the final, consolidated pipeline architecture, followed by the specific operational additions required to execute the newly formalized Phase 4 concepts in a production environment.

---

### Part 1: The Core Reiteration (The Formalized Pipeline)

#### 1. The Transmedia State-Machine Generalization

* **The Principle:** Narrative is a medium-agnostic state space $\mathcal{S}$, an action vocabulary $\mathcal{A}$, and a set of invariants $I$. Mediums (video, comics, prose) are merely projection functions ($R_v, R_c, R_n$).
* **The Power:** Because invariants $I$ are evaluated against actions $\mathcal{A}$ *before* rendering, a physical impossibility (a broken leg trying to run) is rejected once, universally, at $\$0$ cost, regardless of whether the output was destined for a ComfyUI video node or a Typst PDF generator.
* **The Cross-Medium Dirty Flag:** Because all mediums draw from the same D1 dependency graph, an action taken in a comic that alters canonical state (e.g., spending ammunition) automatically and instantly flags downstream scenes in the novel or animated series as `DIRTY`.
* **The Adaptation Brief (Information Loss/Gain):** Projections are not equal. Video captures duration; comics capture frozen geometry; prose captures unvoiced cognition. A transmedia pipeline requires human-authored "Adaptation Briefs" that explicitly instruct the compiler on which canonical vectors to foreground, background, or suppress based on the medium's native strengths.

#### 2. MRU-Based Prose Linting (Advisory, Not Gating)

* **The Principle:** Dwight Swain’s Motivation-Reaction Units (MRUs) provide a structural, chronological syntax for compelling prose: External Stimulus $\to$ Visceral Feeling $\to$ Motor Reflex $\to$ Deliberate Action/Speech.
* **The Mechanism:** A static analysis linter uses dependency parsing (not just regex) to catch causality inversions (e.g., reacting to a sound before the sound is described) and filter-verb bloat ("he felt," "she noticed").
* **The Crucial Boundary:** Because skilled writers deliberately invert MRU causality for dramatic irony or stylistic punch, this linter must **never function as a hard gate**. It must remain an advisory score surfaced to a human editor. Flattening literature into a rigid algorithm destroys the voice of the show.

#### 3. Surgical Patching & The "Not Locally Fixable" Escape Hatch

* **The Principle:** When a defect is detected, never re-roll the entire chapter or video scene. Regenerate the *Minimal Enclosing Unit*.
* **Prose Dependencies:** A paragraph cannot be patched if downstream paragraphs rely on facts established within it. The patch prompt must explicitly enforce intra-beat closures ("preserve the fact that X was established here").
* **Video Feathering:** Video patches must pad the frame boundaries ($F_{\text{start}} - k$ to $F_{\text{end}} + k$) and use temporal blending to eliminate visual seams at the edit points.
* **The Escape Hatch (Signal 1 & 2):** If repeated patch attempts *diverge* (fixing one error causes a new one), or if a pre-flight SAT-check proves the constraints are mutually exclusive, the system must immediately abort the loop.
* **Signal 3 (Diagnostic Routing):** The escalation must carry the constraint matrix and attempt history. A `LOCAL_STYLE_FAILURE` routes back to the writer; a `CONSTRAINT_CONFLICT` routes up to the Tier 2 Story Architect, because the scene requires a plot change, not a sentence rewrite.

#### 4. The Durable Object Entity-Mutex (2PC and Lock Ordering)

* **The Principle:** To prevent cross-room race conditions (Node A and Node B drafting scenes that mutate the same character), canonical entities must be wrapped in Cloudflare Durable Objects.
* **Read vs. Write Leases:** Reading a state to write around it does not lock the entity. Only explicit mutations acquire exclusive write leases.
* **Two-Phase Commit (2PC):** Because scenes mutate multiple entities simultaneously, partial commits corrupt the universe. The coordinator must issue a `PREPARE` to all entities. If all validate the mutation, it issues a `COMMIT`. If any fail, it issues an `ABORT`.
* **Deadlock Prevention & Timeout:** To prevent circular-wait deadlocks, the coordinator must acquire locks in a deterministic, sorted order (e.g., alphanumeric by entity ID). To prevent hung coordinators from freezing the pipeline, Durable Objects must enforce a strict `PREPARE`-phase timeout (e.g., 60 seconds) that automatically releases the lock.

#### 5. The Cost-of-Defect Law & Investment Strategy

* **The Step Function:** The cost of a defect jumps sharply at irreversible commitment thresholds: Pre-Compute ($\$0$) $\to$ Pre-Render (Pennies) $\to$ Cloud GPU Execution (Dollars) $\to$ Human Conform (Hours) $\to$ Broadcast/Print (Catastrophic).
* **The Escape-Rate Conditionality:** This economic law only holds if the linter actually catches the defect. A leaky linter creates false confidence.
* **The Investment Imperative:** Expanding the linter’s invariant coverage is the highest-ROI software investment in the studio. Every new deterministic rule moves a defect class from a catastrophic downstream cliff back to the $\$0$ compile-time gate.
* **The Quality Exemption:** The Cost-of-Defect law applies *only* to deterministic, checkable invariants. It does not apply to holistic dramatic quality, which has no $\$0$ catch point and must be evaluated by humans at every stage.

### Part 2: Worthy Technical Additions

To fully operationalize Phase 4 into executable code, the following three components must be added to the architecture.

---

### Addition 1: The Transmedia Cross-Pollination Trigger (X-Trigger)

While D1 handles dependency invalidation, a true transmedia pipeline needs an **Active Awareness Engine**. If the Comic team commits an action that flags the Novel team's chapter as `DIRTY`, the Novel team shouldn't just find out when they try to click "Render."

**The Addition:** Implement a lightweight cross-medium webhook that translates mathematical state mutations into human-readable narrative updates for adjacent teams.

```typescript
// src/services/transmediaXTrigger.ts
export async function broadcastStateMutation(
  mutatingMedium: 'COMIC' | 'VIDEO' | 'PROSE',
  sceneId: string,
  stateDelta: any,
  invalidatedDownstreamScenes: string[]
) {
  // Translate the delta into a human-readable summary
  const summary = generateDeltaSummary(stateDelta);

  for (const downstreamScene of invalidatedDownstreamScenes) {
    const affectedMedium = getMediumForScene(downstreamScene);
    
    // Only broadcast if the affected medium is different from the mutating medium
    if (affectedMedium !== mutatingMedium) {
      await sendStudioNotification({
        target_pod: getPodForMedium(affectedMedium),
        alert_level: 'WARNING',
        message: `[TRANSMEDIA CANON UPDATE] The ${mutatingMedium} team just committed a canon change in ${sceneId}:\n` +
                 `-> ${summary}\n` +
                 `Your scene ${downstreamScene} has been marked DIRTY and requires reconciliation.`
      });
    }
  }
}

```

*Why this matters:* It transforms the `DIRTY` flag from a silent technical blocker into an active communication bridge between isolated pods, maintaining Slime Mold stigmergy without requiring synchronous meetings.

---

### Addition 2: The "Information Loss/Gain" Matrix Enforcer

The Adaptation Brief must be computationally enforced so that LLMs do not hallucinate visual descriptions in comics or omit internal thoughts in prose.

**The Addition:** Create a strict **Constraint Masking Layer** that filters the prompt context sent to Child Graph A based on the target medium.

| Medium | Constraint Mask (What the Compiler Hides / Enforces) |
| --- | --- |
| **Prose** | **Enforces:** `psychic_distance` tracking. **Hides:** Absolute spatial coordinates (prevents robotic descriptions of characters moving "three feet left"). |
| **Comic** | **Enforces:** Strict dialogue token limits per panel. **Hides:** Unvoiced `Epistemic` secrets (unless explicitly requested as a thought balloon). |
| **Video** | **Enforces:** `Somatic` kinetic limits for temporal rendering. **Hides:** Sensory details impossible to render visually (e.g., "The air smelled like ozone"). |

By masking the input context, you physically prevent the LLM from generating output that violates the fundamental constraints of the medium, catching formatting errors at $T_0$.

---

### Addition 3: The Patch Dependency Closure Mapper (Intra-Beat Analysis)

To make surgical prose patching truly safe, the system must definitively answer: *If I rewrite Paragraph 3, will I break Paragraph 4?*

**The Addition:** Before executing a prose patch, run a **Lightweight Coreference & Entity Resolution Pass** over the downstream text within the same beat.

```typescript
// src/services/patchDependencyMapper.ts
export function calculateMinimalEnclosingUnit(
  flawedParagraphIndex: number,
  beatParagraphs: string[]
): { startIdx: number; endIdx: number; preservedEntities: string[] } {
  const flawedText = beatParagraphs[flawedParagraphIndex];
  const introducedEntities = extractEntities(flawedText); // e.g., "the brass siphon"
  
  let endIdx = flawedParagraphIndex;
  let preservedEntities = new Set<string>();

  // Scan downstream paragraphs in the same beat for references to entities introduced here
  for (let i = flawedParagraphIndex + 1; i < beatParagraphs.length; i++) {
    const downstreamEntities = extractEntities(beatParagraphs[i]);
    const overlap = [...introducedEntities].filter(e => downstreamEntities.has(e));
    
    if (overlap.length > 0) {
      endIdx = i; // Expand the minimal unit to include this dependent paragraph
      overlap.forEach(e => preservedEntities.add(e));
    } else {
      break; // Safe boundary found
    }
  }

  return {
    startIdx: flawedParagraphIndex,
    endIdx: endIdx,
    preservedEntities: Array.from(preservedEntities)
  };
}

```

*Why this matters:* It removes the guesswork from surgical patching. If the patch engine expands the repair window to include the downstream references, and explicitly passes `preservedEntities` into the repair prompt, the LLM is mathematically constrained from introducing intra-beat continuity errors. This makes localized repair a safe, reliable alternative to full-chapter regeneration.

Here is the operational synthesis of your evaluation, stripping away the rhetorical fluff, identifying the concrete mechanisms, and detailing the production-grade additions needed to harden these three Phase 4 extensions.

### Part 1: The Core Reiteration (Validating & Sharpening the Three Additions)

#### 1. Addition 1: The Transmedia Cross-Pollination Trigger (X-Trigger)

* **The Validated Core:** The standard D1 dirty-flag mechanism is passive; it requires an author to actively open a scene to discover it is dirty. Within a single medium, writers routinely re-open recent work. Across media boundaries, this passivity becomes a failure mode: a novel writer has no operational reason to monitor a comic team's commits. Making the cross-medium dirty flag an **active push notification** (gated strictly on `affectedMedium !== mutatingMedium`) is the correct minimal extension. It adds an event-driven broadcast on top of the propagation logic without mutating the underlying graph model.
* **The Punctured Rhetoric:** "Stigmergic Slime Mold" framing was rhetorical dressing. A targeted, webhook-driven notification is standard, effective event-driven architecture and stands entirely on its own merits.
* **The Identified Gap & Remedy:** The function `generateDeltaSummary(stateDelta)` cannot be an ungrounded LLM call acting as an authoritative instruction. An unverified AI summary can hallucinate nuances, causing a writer to spend hours resolving the wrong problem. The notification must treat any natural language prose as **advisory scaffolding** and must always bundle the raw, structured, machine-readable JSON diff (`delta.somatic`, `delta.logistics`, `delta.epistemic`) directly alongside the text summary so the human can verify the exact ground truth.

#### 2. Addition 2: The Constraint Masking Layer (Preventive Input Filtering)

* **The Validated Core:** An unconstrained "Adaptation Brief" left as human documentation is a soft constraint that LLMs routinely ignore under generation pressure. The Constraint Masking Layer converts human guidelines into a **preventive prompt-assembly filter**. It physically withholds medium-incompatible data before the LLM sees it (e.g., hiding absolute cartesian coordinates from prose generators, or hiding unvoiced epistemic secrets from comic panels unless an explicit thought balloon is flagged).
* **The Identified Gap & Remedy:** Pure subtraction creates informational vacuums. If you hide absolute spatial metrics (*"three feet left"*) without providing a substitute, the generator produces vague, generic prose. Every masked constraint must pair a **withheld representation** with an **enforced alternative representation** (e.g., masking numerical distance must inject a mandate for relative sensory anchoring: *"near the rusted barrel"*, *"within arm's reach of the dripping culvert"*).

#### 3. Addition 3: The Patch Dependency Closure Mapper (Intra-Beat Analysis)

* **The Validated Core:** Surgical patching at paragraph granularity is unsafe if downstream paragraphs rely on facts, objects, or state introduced in the flawed paragraph. The Dependency Closure Mapper expands the repair span into a *Minimal Enclosing Unit* and passes preserved entities to the prompt, turning localized repair into a bounded, dependency-aware transaction.
* **The Identified Gap & Remedy (Bidirectional Dependency):** The original logic only scanned forward ($i > \text{flawedIdx}$). However, dependencies run backward as well. If Paragraph 3 is being patched, it might contain a callback to an object planted in Paragraph 1. A naive rewrite of Paragraph 3 might fix the local defect but accidentally sever the upstream callback. The closure calculation must be **bidirectional**:
* *Upstream Invariant:* What antecedent entities/facts from prior paragraphs must Paragraph 3 continue to satisfy?
* *Downstream Invariant:* What subsequent references in later paragraphs must Paragraph 3 continue to provide?


* **The NLP Fragility Reality:** Entity co-occurrence and coreference resolution ("the brass siphon" vs. "the siphon" vs. "it") are non-trivial and fundamentally leaky if implemented via basic string matching. The mapper must be treated as an imperfect detector, paired with the same **two-number honesty metric** established in Phase 0.4: track automated closures vs. human-audited missed dependencies.

### Addition 1: Dual-Payload Transmedia Webhook (`src/services/transmediaXTrigger.ts`)

To prevent the `generateDeltaSummary` hallucination trap, the notification payload is split into two explicit sections: an **Advisory Narrative Summary** and the **Authoritative Ground-Truth Delta**.

```typescript
// src/services/transmediaXTrigger.ts
import type { CanonStateDelta } from '@snailicid3/consumer-npm';

export interface TransmediaAlertPayload {
  alert_id: string;
  timestamp: number;
  originating_event: {
    medium: 'COMIC' | 'VIDEO' | 'PROSE';
    scene_id: string;
    author_id: string;
  };
  impacted_target: {
    medium: 'COMIC' | 'VIDEO' | 'PROSE';
    scene_id: string;
    current_status: 'DIRTY';
  };
  // 1. ADVISORY HUMAN LAYER (Generated for fast scanning, explicitly non-authoritative)
  advisory_prose_summary: string;
  // 2. AUTHORITATIVE MACHINE LAYER (Ground-truth diff; human must inspect if prose is ambiguous)
  authoritative_state_diff: {
    somatic_mutations: CanonStateDelta['somatic_mutations'];
    logistical_mutations: CanonStateDelta['logistical_mutations'];
    epistemic_mutations: CanonStateDelta['epistemic_mutations'];
    resulting_canon_hash: string;
  };
  reconciliation_action_required: string;
}

export function buildDeterministicDeltaSummary(delta: CanonStateDelta): string {
  // Deterministic string builder for common mutations to bypass LLM hallucination for core invariants
  const fragments: string[] = [];

  for (const m of delta.somatic_mutations) {
    fragments.push(`[SOMATIC] ${m.entity_id}: ${m.action} (${JSON.stringify(m.payload)})`);
  }
  for (const l of delta.logistical_mutations) {
    fragments.push(`[LOGISTICS] ${l.entity_id}: ${l.action} (${JSON.stringify(l.payload)})`);
  }
  for (const e of delta.epistemic_mutations) {
    fragments.push(`[EPISTEMIC] ${e.entity_id}: Learned '${e.secret_id}'`);
  }

  return fragments.length > 0 ? fragments.join('; ') : 'State snapshot hash updated without vector mutation.';
}

```

*The Value:* The affected writer gets a deterministic, bulletproof breakdown of what changed mathematically, accompanied by a readable summary. If the LLM summary is slightly off, the raw diff protects the writer from chasing a ghost.

### Addition 2: The Substitution-Based Constraint Masking Compiler (`src/services/constraintMasker.ts`)

We replace pure negative masking (subtraction) with **Substitution-Coupled Masking**. For every prohibited data channel, an explicit syntactic substitute is mandated.

```typescript
// src/services/constraintMasker.ts
export interface MaskingRule {
  field_path: string;
  action: 'OMIT_COMPLETELY' | 'SUBSTITUTE_REPRESENTATION';
  substitute_instruction?: string;
}

export const MEDIUM_MASKING_CONFIG: Record<'PROSE' | 'COMIC' | 'VIDEO', MaskingRule[]> = {
  PROSE: [
    {
      field_path: 'spatial_coordinates_cartesian',
      action: 'SUBSTITUTE_REPRESENTATION',
      substitute_instruction: 'Convert all absolute distances (meters, coordinates) into tactile and relative sensory relationships (e.g., "within arm’s reach", "looming past the rusted lip of the culvert").'
    },
    {
      field_path: 'camera_framing_enums',
      action: 'SUBSTITUTE_REPRESENTATION',
      substitute_instruction: 'Translate camera shot types into John Gardner psychic distance: Wide -> Objective external atmosphere; Close-up -> Intimate visceral sensory details.'
    }
  ],
  COMIC: [
    {
      field_path: 'unvoiced_epistemic_secrets',
      action: 'OMIT_COMPLETELY', // Do not show unvoiced secrets unless a THOUGHT balloon is explicitly flagged
    },
    {
      field_path: 'continuous_motor_transitions',
      action: 'SUBSTITUTE_REPRESENTATION',
      substitute_instruction: 'Isolate only the peak kinetic instant of the gesture. Do not describe intermediate motion frames.'
    }
  ],
  VIDEO: [
    {
      field_path: 'unvoiced_internal_monologue',
      action: 'SUBSTITUTE_REPRESENTATION',
      substitute_instruction: 'Convert internal psychology into micro-motor physical blocking, gaze aversion, or vocal DSP pacing modifiers.'
    },
    {
      field_path: 'non_visual_sensory_descriptors', // e.g. smell, internal temperature
      action: 'OMIT_COMPLETELY'
    }
  ]
};

export function applyConstraintMask(
  rawContext: Record<string, any>,
  targetMedium: 'PROSE' | 'COMIC' | 'VIDEO'
): { maskedContext: Record<string, any>; mandatorySubstitutes: string[] } {
  const rules = MEDIUM_MASKING_CONFIG[targetMedium];
  const maskedContext = structuredClone(rawContext);
  const mandatorySubstitutes: string[] = [];

  for (const rule of rules) {
    if (rule.action === 'OMIT_COMPLETELY') {
      delete maskedContext[rule.field_path];
    } else if (rule.action === 'SUBSTITUTE_REPRESENTATION' && rule.substitute_instruction) {
      delete maskedContext[rule.field_path];
      mandatorySubstitutes.push(rule.substitute_instruction);
    }
  }

  return { maskedContext, mandatorySubstitutes };
}

```

*The Value:* When generating prose, the model is physically stripped of raw camera directions, but receives a structural mandate forcing it to use tactile prose anchors. The masking prevents robotic framing while actively guiding literary density.

### Addition 3: Bidirectional Patch Closure Engine with Honesty Telemetry (`src/services/bidirectionalPatchMapper.ts`)

We expand the patch mapper into a **Bidirectional Scope Calculator** with built-in escape-rate telemetry to address the reality of NLP coreference fragility.

```typescript
// src/services/bidirectionalPatchMapper.ts

export interface PatchScopeResult {
  patch_start_index: number;
  patch_end_index: number;
  upstream_dependencies_to_honor: string[];   // Facts/entities from P_0 to P_start that must be preserved
  downstream_dependencies_to_preserve: string[]; // Facts/entities used in P_end+1 to P_N that must not be broken
  confidence_score: number; // 0.0 to 1.0 based on coreference resolution clarity
}

export function calculateBidirectionalClosure(
  flawedParagraphIndex: number,
  beatParagraphs: string[],
  extractEntitiesFn: (text: string) => Set<string>
): PatchScopeResult {
  const totalParagraphs = beatParagraphs.length;
  const targetText = beatParagraphs[flawedParagraphIndex];
  const targetEntities = extractEntitiesFn(targetText);

  // 1. FORWARD SCAN (Downstream Dependencies)
  let forwardEnd = flawedParagraphIndex;
  const downstreamEntitiesToPreserve = new Set<string>();

  for (let i = flawedParagraphIndex + 1; i < totalParagraphs; i++) {
    const currentEntities = extractEntitiesFn(beatParagraphs[i]);
    const intersection = [...targetEntities].filter(e => currentEntities.has(e));

    if (intersection.length > 0) {
      forwardEnd = i;
      intersection.forEach(e => downstreamEntitiesToPreserve.add(e));
    } else {
      break; // Dependency chain terminated
    }
  }

  // 2. BACKWARD SCAN (Upstream Invariant Anchors)
  // Check which entities in the flawed paragraph were introduced in earlier paragraphs
  const upstreamDependenciesToHonor = new Set<string>();
  for (let i = 0; i < flawedParagraphIndex; i++) {
    const priorEntities = extractEntitiesFn(beatParagraphs[i]);
    const overlap = [...targetEntities].filter(e => priorEntities.has(e));
    overlap.forEach(e => upstreamDependenciesToHonor.add(e));
  }

  return {
    patch_start_index: flawedParagraphIndex,
    patch_end_index: forwardEnd,
    upstream_dependencies_to_honor: Array.from(upstreamDependenciesToHonor),
    downstream_dependencies_to_preserve: Array.from(downstreamEntitiesToPreserve),
    // Confidence penalty if pronouns dominate over explicit nouns
    confidence_score: targetText.match(/\b(he|she|it|they)\b/gi) ? 0.75 : 0.95
  };
}

```

#### The Required Operational Honesty Metric (Phase 4 Monitoring):

Just as Phase 0.4 mandates reporting both flagged dirty scenes and human-discovered misses, the surgical patching tool must log:

1. **Automated Dependency Closures Flagged ($N_{\text{auto}}$):** How many times the mapper successfully expanded the repair window.
2. **Broken Reference Escapes ($N_{\text{escape}}$):** How many times a human editor caught that a surgical patch broke a pronoun callback or synonymous reference that the mapper failed to detect.

If $N_{\text{escape}}$ is non-zero, the team treats it as a prompt-engineering and entity-extractor defect, tuning the coreference resolver rather than assuming the patch was safe simply because the compiler passed.

### Part 1: The Core Reiteration (The Blind Spot of Absolute Consistency)

#### 1. The Asymmetry of Enforcement (Downward vs. Upward Verification)

Every mechanism engineered into the pipeline thus far—from Phase 0 dependency tracking to Phase 4 invariant linters and 2PC Durable Object mutexes—operates on a single, unidirectional axis: **Downward Consistency**.
The system rigorously guarantees that all generated content conforms to the established canonical facts. It ensures $B$ (the scene) correctly reflects $A$ (the canon).

What the system entirely lacks is **Upward Scrutiny**. There is zero mechanism to evaluate whether $A$ is actually *good*, coherent, or still thematically relevant six months after it was written.

#### 2. The Danger of Automated Frictionlessness

In a traditional writers' room, bad ideas are naturally caught by human friction. Because writers must manually hold the season's lore in their heads, they constantly re-evaluate it. If a fact feels wrong or restrictive during Episode 6, the room argues about it, and the fact is retconned.

This pipeline was explicitly designed to **eliminate that friction**.
Because the machine perfectly remembers Fact #340 and the linter flawlessly enforces it without requiring a human to ever re-read it, the informal human safety net is gone. A bad fact, established in a rush during Episode 2, will silently and efficiently dictate the boundaries of Episode 10, because the system values *consistency* over *coherence*.

#### 3. What the Solution Requires (And What It Forbids)

* **Forbids:** We cannot use an LLM or an automated scoring gate to evaluate whether a fact is "thematically sound." That reintroduces the subjective AI critic we have successfully banished.
* **Requires:** A structural mechanism that forces a human to periodically re-evaluate the source of truth, independent of the dirty-flag propagation engine. The propagation engine only fires when a fact *changes*. We need an engine that fires when a fact *stagnates*.

#### 4. The Three Concrete Vectors of Reconsideration

To build this without introducing a bloated meeting-culture tax, the mechanism must include:

1. **A "Canon Age" Metric:** Tracking `last_reconsidered_at` separately from `last_edited_at`.
2. **A "Questioned" State:** A status (`flagged_for_review`) that allows a showrunner to express doubt about a fact *without* editing it, because editing it would instantly trigger a cascade of downstream dirty flags before the showrunner even knows what the replacement fact should be.
3. **Blast-Radius Prioritization:** A pure calendar-based review (e.g., "Review all facts every 30 days") is organizational overhead. The trigger must be weighted by the dependency graph: a fact with 40 downstream dependent scenes that hasn't been looked at in six months demands urgent review; an isolated fact with zero dependents does not.

### Part 2: Worthy Technical Additions (The Epistemological Audit Engine)

To close this structural blind spot, we introduce the **Epistemological Audit Engine** into Phase 4 of the architecture. It sits parallel to the Invariant Linter, but instead of policing the output, it polices the Constitution itself.

### Addition 1: The Tri-State Canon Schema (`src/schemas/canonEntity.ts`)

We expand the fundamental schema of `@snailicid3/consumer-npm` to separate a fact's *version* from its *endorsement status*, introducing the critical "Liminal State."

```typescript
import { z } from 'zod';

export const CanonFactStatusSchema = z.enum([
  'ACTIVE_ENDORSED',      // The fact is unquestioned and fully enforced.
  'FLAGGED_FOR_REVIEW',   // A human doubts this fact, but it remains enforced until officially changed.
  'DEPRECATED_ARCHIVED'   // The fact is retired; no longer enforced.
]);

export const CanonEntitySchema = z.object({
  entity_id: z.string(),
  version: z.number().int().positive(), // Increments ONLY on text/payload edit
  status: CanonFactStatusSchema.default('ACTIVE_ENDORSED'),
  
  // The Data
  somatic_vector: z.any().optional(),
  logistical_vector: z.any().optional(),
  epistemic_vector: z.any().optional(),

  // The Epistemological Audit Trail
  last_edited_at: z.number().int(),
  last_reconsidered_at: z.number().int(), // Updates when a human clicks "Still Good" without editing
  reconsidered_by_user_id: z.string().nullable()
});

```

*The Value:* A showrunner can tag The Pilot's `neurotoxic_tremor` with `FLAGGED_FOR_REVIEW`. The pipeline does not halt. Scene pods currently drafting Episode 4 still respect the tremor. But a visible yellow badge now sits on that fact in the Astro UI, indicating to the team that the showrunner is questioning the thematic utility of this limitation, decoupling *doubt* from *destructive propagation*.

### Addition 2: The Load-Bearing Prioritization Algorithm (`src/services/canonAuditor.ts`)

We do not hold "Bible Review Meetings." We use the graph database (D1 / Neo4j) to mathematically surface only the facts that have become dangerously foundational without recent scrutiny.

```typescript
// src/services/canonAuditor.ts
export interface AuditCandidate {
  entity_id: string;
  days_since_reconsideration: number;
  downstream_blast_radius: number; // Count of scenes dependent on this fact
  audit_priority_score: number;
}

export async function generateCanonAuditQueue(
  env: Env, 
  currentDateMs: number
): Promise<AuditCandidate[]> {
  const staleThresholdMs = 45 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; // 45 days
  const candidates: AuditCandidate[] = [];

  // Query D1 for all active facts
  const activeFacts = await env.CANON_DB.prepare(
    `SELECT entity_id, last_reconsidered_at FROM canon_entities WHERE status = 'ACTIVE_ENDORSED'`
  ).all();

  for (const fact of activeFacts.results) {
    const ageMs = currentDateMs - fact.last_reconsidered_at;
    
    // Only evaluate facts older than the stale threshold
    if (ageMs > staleThresholdMs) {
      // Query the dependency graph for the actual weight of this fact
      const dependentScenesCount = await env.CANON_DB.prepare(
        `SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM scene_fact_dependencies WHERE fact_id = ?`
      ).bind(fact.entity_id).first('count');

      // The Prioritization Algorithm: Age * Load-Bearing Weight
      const daysStale = ageMs / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24);
      const priorityScore = daysStale * Math.log10(dependentScenesCount + 1);

      // Only surface facts that are actually load-bearing
      if (priorityScore > 50.0) { 
        candidates.push({
          entity_id: fact.entity_id,
          days_since_reconsideration: Math.round(daysStale),
          downstream_blast_radius: dependentScenesCount,
          audit_priority_score: priorityScore
        });
      }
    }
  }

  // Return sorted by most dangerous (Stale + High Blast Radius)
  return candidates.sort((a, b) => b.audit_priority_score - a.audit_priority_score);
}

```

*The Value:* At the end of a production block, the showrunner clicks the **"Canon Health"** tab in Astro. The system does not ask them to read 600 facts. It presents exactly three: *"These three facts dictate the behavior of 42 scenes across the next season, and no human has critically evaluated them in 80 days. Are they still true to the story?"*

---

### Addition 3: The Auteur Reconsideration Interface (The "Still Good" Button)

To prevent the review cadence from becoming a bureaucratic tax, the interface for auditing canon must be frictionless.

In the Astro Cockpit, when the showrunner reviews an `AuditCandidate`:

1. **Read the Context:** The UI displays the fact, along with a sampled list of the 5 most critical scenes that depend on it.
2. **Action 1 [Edit Fact]:** The showrunner changes the fact. This triggers the standard Phase 0 dirty-flag cascade, incrementing the version and updating both `last_edited_at` and `last_reconsidered_at`.
3. **Action 2 [Flag for Review]:** The showrunner leaves it enforced but tags it for the Writers' Room to discuss tomorrow.
4. **Action 3 [Reaffirm]:** The showrunner clicks a single button labeled **"Still Good"**.
* The database updates `last_reconsidered_at = Date.now()`.
* The version number does *not* increment.
* Zero dirty flags are thrown.
* The fact drops off the audit queue for another 45 days.

### Addition 4: Extending Upward Scrutiny to System Invariants

As you correctly identified, the danger of blind consistency applies not just to narrative facts, but to the **compilation rules themselves**.

If the Invariant Linter uses a strict regex or AST rule banning the word "sprint," and that rule was miscalibrated on Day 1, the pipeline will flawlessly enforce bad prose mechanics for a year.

**The Fix: The Rule-Exemption Ledger**
We add a telemetry tracker to the Linter. Every time a writer hits the "Auteur Override" button to bypass an advisory warning (e.g., an MRU inversion that they did on purpose for stylistic effect), the Conductor logs the override.

```typescript
  rule_id: string; // e.g., 'MRU_CAUSALITY_INVERSION' or 'BANNED_VERB_SPRINT'
  scene_id: string;
  overridden_by_user: string;

}

```

At the end of the month, the Pipeline Engineer checks the **Rule Health Dashboard**.
If the rule `MRU_CAUSALITY_INVERSION` has been overridden 45 times by three different writers, the system has surfaced a structural truth: **The rule is wrong, or the writers' room has outgrown it.**

The engineering team does not yell at the writers for ignoring the linter. They rewrite the linter rule, because the human friction has proved the automated invariant is choking the creative output.

This transforms the pipeline from a static prison into a living organism that automatically highlights where its own laws have become obsolete.

### Part 1: The Core Reiteration (The Hub and The Spoke)

#### 1. The True Hinge (The Law and The Ledger)

The system’s actual hinge—the load-bearing center without which the architecture collapses into incoherence—is the **Deterministic State Machine**.
Cloudflare D1, Durable Objects, Hono routing, Zod schemas, and the Astro Conductor form the immutable hub. This layer coordinates actors, serializes transactions, catches contradictions, and propagates blast radii. It does not generate media, but it is the absolute prerequisite for any media to exist. If this layer vanishes, the universe forgets its own rules: injuries heal randomly, fuel tanks refill silently, and characters speak secrets they haven't learned.

#### 2. ComfyUI as the Execution Spoke (Downstream Compute)

ComfyUI is not the architectural hinge; it is a highly capable, modality-agnostic **Execution Spoke**.
Its value lies in its topological DAG format, dirty-state caching, and VRAM management across text, audio, and video models. However, it operates strictly downstream of the law. It receives a mathematically certified prompt from the Conductor, burns the required GPU cycles to generate the artifact, and returns the payload. It holds no memory, enforces no narrative constraints, and possesses no authority over the canon.

#### 3. The "Dumb Executor" Principle

Because ComfyUI is an executor and not the coordinator, it must remain structurally "dumb." A ComfyUI node network should never query the database to ask, *"Does The Pilot have his siphon nozzle?"* That query belongs to the Conductor. ComfyUI only knows: *"I have been handed a JSON payload containing a string of text and a LoRA file path. I will render it."*

By recognizing that ComfyUI is simply a service the hinge calls, the architecture is protected from being locked into a single piece of software. If a better DAG execution engine emerges next year, ComfyUI can be cleanly swapped out without rewriting a single line of the canonical state machine.
